papers.reason: 为SCLC/LCNEC中tarlatamab等DLL3×CD3 T细胞衔接器的耐药提供5-HT-HTR7-TAM机制假设，提示联合HTR7/TPH1干预的转化研究方向；暂不直接改变当前患者选择或随访决策。
papers.abstract_en: Tarlatamab, a delta-like protein 3 (DLL3) × CD3-directed T cell engager (TCE), provides clinical efficacy against small cell lung cancers (SCLCs), although its efficacy remains limited, indicating the importance of clarifying the resistance mechanisms. We show that serotonin (5-HT) produced by DLL3high neuroendocrine cancers (NECs) induces immunosuppressive tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), resulting in impaired CD8+ T cell function and TCE resistance. Using SCLC and large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma cohorts, we find that DLL3high SCLCs induce immunosuppressive TAMs in the tumor microenvironment and become resistant to tarlatamab. DLL3high NECs increase 5-HT production via TPH1 upregulation. NEC-derived 5-HT augments the immunosuppressive activity of 5-HT receptor 7 (HTR7)-expressing TAMs. Genetic ablation of HTR7 in TAMs or TPH1 in NECs restores CD8+ T cell function and improves the efficacy of TCEs and programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) blockade. We propose that NEC-derived 5-HT-HTR7 axis drives immunosuppressive TAM activation and TCE resistance, making it a key target to increase TCE efficacy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Ribociclib plus nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor (NSAI) demonstrated a statistically significant invasive disease-free survival (iDFS) benefit over NSAI alone in patients with hormone receptor-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HR+/HER2-) early breast cancer (EBC) at the primary efficacy analysis of the phase 3 NATALEE trial. This prespecified 6-year analysis assessed overall survival (OS) and other efficacy outcomes as well as safety. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Eligible patients were adults with HR+/HER2- EBC and anatomic stage IIA (N1 or N0 with high-risk factors), IIB, or III disease. Enrolled patients were randomized 1:1 to ribociclib 400 mg/day (3 weeks on/1 week off for 3 years) plus NSAI (letrozole 2.5 mg/day or anastrozole 1 mg/day for 5 years) or NSAI alone. Premenopausal women and men also received goserelin. The primary endpoint was iDFS, and secondary/exploratory endpoints included OS, distant disease-free survival (DDFS), and distant recurrence-free survival (DRFS). RESULTS: With a median OS follow-up of 66.5 months, ribociclib plus NSAI demonstrated an OS benefit over NSAI alone (6-year ΔOS, 2.1%; HR, 0.809 [95% CI: 0.661-0.989]; nominal 1-sided P = .019), which was generally consistent across key subgroups. An increasing iDFS benefit with ribociclib plus NSAI was also observed (6-year ΔiDFS, 5.3%; HR, 0.741 [95% CI: 0.646-0.849]; nominal 1-sided P < .0001), which was also generally consistent across key subgroups. DDFS (HR, 0.744 [95% CI: 0.646-0.858]) and DRFS (HR, 0.738 [95% CI: 0.634-0.858]) results supported these findings. No new safety signals were observed. CONCLUSIONS: This prespecified descriptive 6-year OS analysis demonstrated positive OS results with a clinically relevant benefit of ribociclib plus NSAI, consistent with the increasing reduction in recurrence risk. These results reinforce the benefit of ribociclib plus NSAI in the adjuvant setting across the broad NATALEE-eligible population. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: NCT03701334 (ClinicalTrials.gov).

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Perioperative immune-checkpoint inhibition improves outcomes in muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC). The phase III, randomized CA017-078 (ENERGIZE) trial evaluated perioperative nivolumab plus neoadjuvant gemcitabine-cisplatin (GC) versus neoadjuvant GC alone for previously untreated, resectable MIBC. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Adults with previously untreated cT2-T4aN0M0 MIBC eligible for radical cystectomy (RC) and cisplatin were randomized to neoadjuvant nivolumab plus GC followed by RC and adjuvant nivolumab (nivolumab plus GC arm), or neoadjuvant GC followed by RC alone (GC arm). Co-primary endpoints were pathological complete response (pCR; defined as ypT0N0) and event-free survival (EFS). Overall survival (OS) was a secondary endpoint within the prespecified hierarchical testing strategy, and formal testing was contingent on a statistically significant EFS result. RESULTS: At this final analysis with 54.5 months of median follow-up, 325 patients were randomized to the nivolumab plus GC arm, 328 to the GC arm. pCR rates were 39.1% and 29.6%, respectively (adjusted difference 9.5%, 99.91% CI -2.6-21.6). EFS was not improved in the nivolumab plus GC versus GC arm (104 events in each arm; HR 0.94, 95.74% CI 0.71-1.25; P=0.6697). OS was summarized descriptively because EFS did not meet the testing criterion (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.64-1.21). Grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 50.0% versus 49.5%; one treatment-related death occurred with nivolumab plus GC. Pretreatment ctDNA was positive in 229/416 tested patients (55%) overall, 108/211 (51%) in the GC arm, and 121/205 (59%) in the nivolumab plus GC arm. Clearance by cycle 4 day 1 (C4D1) occurred in 153/199 patients (76.9%) overall, 87/107 (81.3%) with nivolumab plus GC, and 66/92 (71.7%) with GC. ctDNA detection at baseline and at C4D1 was associated with shorter EFS and OS. CONCLUSIONS: The addition of perioperative nivolumab to neoadjuvant GC did not improve outcomes and was associated with predictable toxicity. Exploratory analysis showed ctDNA was strongly prognostic.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Programmed death 1-blocking antibody, nivolumab, plus lymphocyte-activation gene 3-blocking antibody, relatlimab, is approved for advanced melanoma. We report results from Part 2 of RELATIVITY-104, the first phase II, proof-of-concept, head-to-head study to evaluate first-line nivolumab plus relatlimab plus platinum doublet chemotherapy (PDCT) versus nivolumab plus PDCT in patients with stage IV/recurrent non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). PATIENTS AND METHODS: In Part 2, patients were randomized 1:1 to nivolumab plus relatlimab plus PDCT or nivolumab plus PDCT. The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) per blinded independent central review (BICR). Secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS) and duration of response (DOR) per BICR, ORR and PFS by subgroups, and safety. Exploratory analyses included overall survival (OS), biomarker, translational, and patient-reported outcomes. RESULTS: In part 2, the primary endpoint was not met (ORR, 51.3% for nivolumab plus relatlimab plus PDCT versus 45.0% for nivolumab plus PDCT); PFS hazard ratio (HR; 90% confidence interval [CI]) was 0.89 (0.72 to 1.09). A trend towards improved clinical benefit was seen with nivolumab plus relatlimab plus PDCT in a subgroup of patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1) ≥1% and nonsquamous histology (ORR: 58.0% versus 39.6%; PFS: HR, 0.68; 90% CI 0.46 to 1.01). A potential improvement in OS was observed with nivolumab plus relatlimab plus PDCT in the PD-L1 ≥1% nonsquamous subgroup (HR, 0.60; 90% CI 0.38 to 0.94). The safety profile of nivolumab plus relatlimab plus PDCT was manageable and consistent with previous reports. CONCLUSION: In RELATIVITY-104, the addition of relatlimab to standard-of-care did not improve outcomes in the unselected all-randomized population. However, positive trends observed in the subgroup of patients with tumor PD-L1 ≥1% and nonsquamous NSCLC supports further investigation in these patients in the phase III RELATIVITY-1093 study. CLINICALTRIALS: gov identifier: NCT04623775.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Patients with previously treated biliary tract cancer (BTC) have a short median overall survival (OS), and few treatment options. Tovecimig, a bispecific antibody to delta-like ligand-4 and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)-A, was evaluated in combination with paclitaxel in COMPANION-002, a randomized phase 2/3 study in pretreated patients with advanced BTC. METHODS: Patients with advanced BTC with one prior systemic therapy were randomized to paclitaxel (80 mg/m2; days 1, 8 and 15) with or without tovecimig (10 mg/kg; days 1 and 15). The primary endpoint was RECIST v1.1-defined objective response rate (ORR) as assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR). Secondary endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS) and OS. Crossover from the paclitaxel control arm to tovecimig plus paclitaxel was permitted following BICR-confirmed progression. RESULTS: 168 patients were randomized 2:1 to tovecimig+paclitaxel (n=111) or paclitaxel alone (n=57). Tovecimig+paclitaxel significantly improved BICR-assessed ORR (18.0% vs 5.3%; P=.0228) and PFS (4.7 vs 2.6 months; hazard ratio [HR], 0.44; P<.0001). Among 31 patients (54%) who crossed over, post-progression PFS (time from crossover to subsequent second progression) exceeded initial PFS (PFS from randomization to initial progression on paclitaxel; 3.5 vs 1.9 months; HR, 0.40; P=.0035). Overall, 142 patients (85%) received tovecimig; no difference in OS was observed (HR, 1.05; P=.779). The most common treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) with tovecimig+paclitaxel were hypertension (69.4%) and fatigue (66.7%). Grade ≥3 TEAEs occurred in 93.5% and 64.2% of patients treated with tovecimig+paclitaxel and paclitaxel alone, respectively. CONCLUSION: Tovecimig combined with paclitaxel significantly improved ORR and PFS versus paclitaxel alone as second-line therapy for patients with BTC.

papers.abstract_en: Camupepimut (ELI-002 7P) drives mutated KRAS (mKRAS)-specific T cell responses that correlated with disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS) in patients with mKRAS pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC) in the phase 1 AMPLIFY-201 trial. In the phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P trial, patients with stage I-III KRAS-mutated PDAC without recurrence within 6 months of standard therapy were randomized 2:1 to camupepimut (n = 96) or standard-of-care/observation (n = 48). Stratification balanced nodal status. The primary DFS endpoint was not met (median 23.8 versus 21.2 months; HR 0.85, P = 0.5329). However, prespecified and exploratory analyses were informative. A numerical DFS advantage at 6 months of 14.0% (75.7% versus 61.7%; HR 0.55, P = 0.0557) corresponded to camupepimut dosing. Post hoc multivariate Cox regression analysis of DFS indicated an improved outcome for camupepimut (adjusted HR 0.47, P = 0.0086), a worse outcome for stage III disease (adjusted HR 2.29, P = 0.0127), an elevated baseline CA19-9 (adjusted HR 3.16, P < 0.0001) and baseline circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) positivity (adjusted HR 5.99, P < 0.0001). Prespecified subgroup analyses addressing prognostic and predictive factors suggested DFS benefit for camupepimut (ctDNA negative: HR 0.51, P = 0.0280; no prior radiation: HR 0.59, P = 0.0221). Exploratory analysis demonstrated that ex vivo mKRAS-specific T cell responses were robust (98.9%, 89/90) and associated with antigen spreading (86.7%, 13/15). In camupepimut-treated patients, mKRAS-specific T cell response >9.17-fold over baseline (82.2%, 74/90) correlated with improved DFS (HR 0.22, P < 0.0001), with the median DFS not reached versus 6.08 months for above and below 9.17-fold, respectively. Camupepimut safety was similar to observation, with grade ≥3 adverse events in 10.4% (10/96) versus 14.6% (7/48), and few serious AEs (6.3%, 6/96 versus 8.3%, 4/48; reflecting progression/surgical complication). These efficacy and immunogenicity signals will inform a refined strategy for a confirmatory phase 3 trial. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05726864 .

papers.abstract_en: Although aberrant glycosylation is closely associated with lung cancer (LC), salivary glycopatterns and their discriminatory value across healthy individuals, benign pulmonary disease, and LC remain insufficiently characterized. We profiled saliva from 307 participants using a lectin microarray, comprising a development cohort of 227 participants and an independent test cohort of 80 participants. Five task-specific LASSO-logistic regression models were constructed to distinguish pulmonary disease, LC, and LC subtypes. A separate Nom-LC model combined consensus lectin features selected by LASSO and support vector machine recursive feature elimination with clinical variables. Salivary glycopatterns differed among healthy volunteers, benign pulmonary disease, and LC groups, and the five task-specific models showed discriminatory performance across pulmonary disease, LC, and exploratory subtype classification tasks. The resulting Nom-LC model incorporated smoking history and four lectin signals (HHL, PNA, RCA120, and PWM), yielding AUCs of 0.908 and 0.907 in the training and internal validation sets. In the independent test cohort, the AUC was 0.903 (95% CI, 0.831-0.976); at the prespecified cutoff, sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were 86.36%, 94.44%, and 90.00%, respectively. These findings support further evaluation of salivary glycopatterns as an auxiliary tool for LC risk stratification, but prospective multicenter validation is required.

papers.title_zh: 整合空间代谢、细胞构筑与灌注的三维多模态分形动力学模型术前预测结直肠癌肝转移微血管侵犯：回顾性建模与45例时间验证队列显示高判别力
papers.title_en: Three-dimensional multimodal fractal dynamics integrating spatial metabolism, cytoarchitecture, and perfusion for preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion in colorectal liver metastases.
papers.authors: Guo Z, Guo C, Lu Z, Zou K, Zhang H
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Nuclear Medicine, First Affiliated Hospital of Jinzhou Medical University, Jinzhou, Liaoning, China.
papers.results: 多因素分析示 FD_ADC 为 MVI 最强独立预测因子（OR=3.85，95% CI: 2.45-6.04，P<0.001）；FRAC-3D 模型在验证队列 AUC 0.938、阴性预测值 96.2%；较双模态模型显著改善风险再分层（continuous NRI=0.425，P<0.001）；基于分形特征聚类识别的“高度混沌”影像表型 MVI 发生率高达 96.7%，中位无复发生存期（RFS）仅 5.2 个月
papers.authors_conclusion: 通过多维生物物理特征的交叉验证，FRAC-3D 模型可实现 MVI 状态的高精度术前预测；该研究将 CRLM 围手术期评估从传统“静态解剖指标”推进至“微环境动态演化”的新维度，为个体化手术切缘规划与靶向新辅助治疗的精准分层提供稳健的、物理驱动的工具
papers.ai_note: 验证队列仅 45 例、单中心回顾性设计，AUC 0.938 与 NPV 96.2% 在小样本中易受过拟合与MVI患病率影响，缺乏多中心外部验证；“高度混沌”表型（MVI 96.7%、RFS 5.2 个月）由同一数据集聚类衍生，属探索性亚组，样本量未报告、无置信区间，存在选择性强调次要/衍生发现的风险；摘要未报告校准度指标、决策曲线结果与验证队列 MVI 事件数；结论中“物理驱动”“高精度”等表述超出单中心小样本验证所能支撑的范围

pico.p: 结直肠癌肝转移（CRLM）患者；推导队列 n=100（经sIPTW基线校正），最终核心建模队列 145 例（具备完整 PET/CT、CE-MRI 与 DWI 影像），独立时间验证队列 n=45
pico.ic: 干预：基于三维多模态影像提取的空间代谢分形维数（FD_PET）、结构分形维数（FD_ADC）与灌注分形加速度（Afd_MRI）构建 FRAC-3D 模型；对照：双模态模型（用于增量价值比较）；终点为术前 MVI 状态判别与预后（RFS）

papers.reason: 为 CRLM 术前 MVI 无创判别提供可参照的多模态影像组学建模路径与基线性能数据，提示围手术期切缘规划与新辅助分层的研究方向；同时其小样本单中心验证的局限可作为同类预测模型研究设计与样本量估算的反面参照
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Accurately predicting microvascular invasion (MVI) preoperatively remains a core challenge for precision surgical decision-making in patients with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM). This study developed and validated a three-dimensional multimodal fractal dynamic model (FRAC-3D) that integrates spatial metabolism, cytoarchitecture, and blood perfusion, aiming to non-invasively identify MVI status preoperatively and evaluate patient prognosis. METHODS: Utilizing a retrospective nested cohort design, stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (sIPTW) was applied to the derivation cohort (n = 100) for baseline debiasing. A core cohort of 145 patients with complete PET/CT, CE-MRI, and DWI imaging was ultimately included. Spatial metabolic fractal dimension (FD_PET), architectural fractal dimension (FD_ADC), and perfusion fractal acceleration (Afd_MRI) were extracted to construct the FRAC-3D model. The model's discrimination, calibration, and clinical benefit were validated in an independent temporal validation cohort (n = 45). RESULTS: Multivariable analysis confirmed that FD_ADC is the strongest independent predictor of MVI (OR = 3.85, 95% CI: 2.45-6.04, P < 0.001). The FRAC-3D model achieved an AUC of 0.938 and a negative predictive value of 96.2% in the validation cohort. Compared with the dual-modal model, FRAC-3D significantly improved risk restratification (continuous NRI = 0.425, P < 0.001). A "highly chaotic" imaging phenotype, identified based on fractal feature clustering, demonstrated an MVI incidence as high as 96.7% and a median recurrence-free survival (RFS) of only 5.2 months. CONCLUSION: Through the cross-validation of multidimensional biophysical features, the FRAC-3D model enables high-precision preoperative prediction of MVI status. This study advances the perioperative assessment of CRLM from traditional 'static anatomical metrics' into a novel dimension of 'microenvironmental dynamic evolution', providing a robust, physics-driven tool for individualized surgical margin planning and the precise stratification of targeted neoadjuvant therapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the leading subtype of non-small cell lung cancer. However, the stromal-immune circuits that coordinate matrix remodeling and immunotherapy resistance in LUAD remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize the stromal-immune interactions associated with LUAD progression and poor response to PD-1 blockade. METHODS: Bulk transcriptomic datasets, single-cell RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomic data were integrated with clinical immunotherapy cohorts. Weighted gene co‑expression network analysis, survival meta‑analysis, and tissue enrichment scoring identified high‑risk cell subpopulations. Cell‑cell communication, virtual gene knockout, and spatial deconvolution were used to predict ligand‑receptor interactions and colocalization. Multiplex immunohistochemistry of clinical specimens validated spatial relationships. In vitro, MMP11-overexpressing cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and SPP1-overexpressing macrophages (Macs) were generated, and a macrophage-CAF co‑culture system was constructed. Migration, contractility, extracellular matrix deposition, and YAP/INHBA pathway activation was measured. In vivo, a murine tumor model was established and evaluated using in vivo imaging, flow cytometry, atomic force microscopy assay, HE, masson staining, and multiplexed IHC staining. RESULTS: MMP11⁺ myofibroblastic CAF (MMP11⁺ myCAF) was identified as a high-risk CAF subset enriched in primary tumor and metastatic lesions, characterized by elevated expression of matrix-remodeling and contractile genes, including MMP11, ACTA2, and TAGLN. Increased abundance of MMP11⁺ myCAF was associated with advanced tumor stage, metastasis, poor overall survival, and reduced benefit from immune checkpoint blockade (ICB). Spatial transcriptomic deconvolution and multiplex immunohistochemistry revealed that MMP11⁺ myCAFs spatially co-localized with SPP1⁺ Mac, a pro-tumor myeloid population enriched in malignant and metastatic LUAD tissues. Ligand-receptor and downstream target analyses identified WNT5A as a key macrophage-derived mediator linking SPP1⁺ Mac to MMP11⁺ myCAF activation. Mechanistically, SPP1⁺ Mac exhibited activation of NFKB2/RELB-associated transcriptional programs, and SPP1 overexpression increased Nfkb2, Relb, and WNT5A protein levels in macrophages. WNT5A stimulation promoted YAP/INHBA-associated signaling in CAFs, enhancing CAF migration, contractility and extracellular matrix deposition. In animal models, activation of WNT5A signaling impaired the therapeutic efficacy of PD-1 blockade, reduced intratumoral CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration, and increased MMP11⁺ CAF-associated collagen deposition and tissue stiffness. CONCLUSIONS: SPP1⁺ Mac-derived WNT5A may contribute to MMP11⁺ myCAF-mediated matrix remodeling and immunotherapy resistance in LUAD, highlighting a potential therapeutic strategy to overcome ICB resistance.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Patients with phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN)-deficient de novo metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) have poor prognosis and reduced benefit from current standard of care. The phase III CAPItello-281 study (NCT04493853) showed a statistically significant benefit in radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS) with capivasertib plus abiraterone versus placebo plus abiraterone (combined with prednisone/prednisolone and androgen deprivation therapy): hazard ratio (HR) 0.81, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.66-0.98; P=0.034. The HR for interim overall survival (OS; 26% maturity) was 0.90, 95% CI 0.71-1.15. Here, we report ad hoc, descriptive analyses at 42% OS data maturity. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Patients with de novo mHSPC and PTEN-deficient tumors (defined as ≥90% of viable malignant cells with no specific cytoplasmic staining by immunohistochemistry) received capivasertib plus abiraterone or matched placebo (randomized 1:1) plus abiraterone. Analyses performed at this ad hoc data cut-off, including the alpha-controlled key secondary endpoint of OS as well as the primary endpoint of investigator-assessed rPFS, were descriptive and not prespecified in the protocol. RESULTS: 1012 patients received capivasertib plus abiraterone (n=507) or placebo plus abiraterone (n=505). At this ad hoc analysis at 42% OS maturity (data cut-off: March 9, 2026), with 17 months' additional follow-up (median follow-up 39 months in both arms), HR for OS favored capivasertib plus abiraterone versus placebo plus abiraterone (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.68-0.99, P=0.044) and OS medians were reached: 57.4 versus 46.5 months. Updated rPFS (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.70-0.99, nominal P=0.033; median 35.5 versus 26.0 months) was consistent with the primary analysis. The safety profile remained consistent with the primary findings. CONCLUSIONS: With longer follow-up, findings from this updated descriptive analysis support the clinically meaningful OS benefit of adding capivasertib to abiraterone in the treatment of patients with PTEN-deficient mHSPC. Capivasertib plus abiraterone represents a first-in-class targeted treatment approach for this poor prognosis population with high unmet need.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Perioperative PD-(L)1 inhibitors, either combined with cisplatin-based chemotherapy or enfortumab vedotin, have improved outcomes in patients with muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) who are cisplatin eligible. The double-blind, phase III KEYNOTE-866 study evaluated perioperative (neoadjuvant and adjuvant) pembrolizumab versus placebo added to neoadjuvant cisplatin plus gemcitabine (chemotherapy) and radical cystectomy with pelvic lymph node dissection (cystectomy) in MIBC. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Eligible participants were aged ≥18 years, had centrally assessed clinical stage T2-T4aN0M0 or T1-T4aN1M0 MIBC with ≥50% urothelial histology, and were eligible for cisplatin-based chemotherapy and cystectomy. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to neoadjuvant pembrolizumab or placebo plus chemotherapy every 3 weeks for 4 cycles, followed by cystectomy, and adjuvant pembrolizumab or placebo every 3 weeks for 13 cycles (pembrolizumab or placebo group, respectively). Primary end point was event-free survival (EFS) by investigator assessment. Pathological complete response (pCR) rate by blinded independent central pathological review and overall survival (OS) were key secondary end points. Safety was a secondary end point. RESULTS: Overall, 907 participants were randomly assigned (pembrolizumab, n = 453; placebo, n = 454). Median follow-up was 60.9 months (range, 40.7-78.7). At 60 months, the estimated EFS rate was 63.5% with pembrolizumab versus 61.9% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.88; 95% CI 0.71-1.10; one-sided P = 0.1366). The pCR rate was 44.4% versus 35.8% (estimated difference 8.9%; 95% CI 2.5-15.1); median OS was not reached in both groups (hazard ratio 1.00; 95% CI 0.79-1.27). Treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 99.8% of participants in the pembrolizumab group (grade ≥3 in 80.2%) and 98.7% in the placebo group (grade ≥3 in 75.1%). CONCLUSIONS: The addition of perioperative pembrolizumab to neoadjuvant chemotherapy and cystectomy did not confer a statistically significant EFS benefit in participants with MIBC who are cisplatin eligible. The safety profile of pembrolizumab was manageable and consistent with prior reports.

papers.abstract_en: The International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) established 26 consensus quality indicators (QIs) for lung cancer screening (LCS) programs, of which 20 were rated as essential and 6 as desirable by the expert panel. We evaluated the extent to which the American College of Radiology (ACR) Lung Cancer Screening Registry (LCSR), the largest LCS registry in the U.S., can support measurement of the IASLC QIs. We performed a crosswalk analysis, mapping all 26 IASLC QIs to the LCSR Data Dictionary and its 46 clinical performance measures, classifying each as directly measurable, derivable, or not measurable. The crosswalk was reviewed and independently validated by members of the ACR Early Lung Cancer Detection Registry Quality and Education Committee. Eight QIs (30.8%) were directly measurable, 10 (38.5%) were derivable, and 8 (30.8%) were not measurable from LCSR data alone. The LCSR therefore contains sufficient data elements to support measurement of approximately 69% of IASLC QIs. Remaining gaps involve screening uptake, clinical investigation, procedure complications, curative-intent treatment, treatment equity, diagnostic investigation equity and selected wait-time measures and would require additional registry fields or external data linkage.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Positive margins after breast-conserving surgery (BCS) require additional surgery, a negative patient experience that also adds costs to care. Pilot trials indicate the Breast Cancer LocatorTM (BCL), a novel supine magnetic resonance imaging-based guidance system, helps surgeons resect cancers with a low positive margin rate (PMR). Our objective was to evaluate BCL noninferiority and superiority compared with wire localization (WL) in reducing the PMR with BCS. METHODS: Patients with nonpalpable, magnetic resonance imaging-visualized invasive breast cancer or ductal carcinoma in situ undergoing BCS were prospectively randomized to either BCL or WL. RESULTS: In total, 418 randomized patients underwent surgery. The PMR was 14.4% (30/209) in the BCL group and 21.1% (44/209) in the WL group, a relative decrease of 32%. In primary analysis, the treatment difference was -7.1% (95.4% confidence interval [CI] -14.3 to 0.1). Noninferiority was demonstrated (p = 0.011). The one-sided p-value for superiority (p = 0.025) slightly exceeded the prespecified significance level of 0.023. In prespecified analysis stratified by final tumor type, the PMR was significantly lower in the BCL group (p = 0.019). Fewer BCL patients underwent re-excision: 12.9% versus 19.6%, a relative decrease of 34%. The PMR for all tumor types was lower in the BCL group, with a > 60% relative reduction in PMR in patients with ductal carcinoma in situ (20.6% vs. 53.3% [95% CI -52.1 to -9.1]) and invasive lobular carcinoma (9.1% vs. 25.6% [95% CI -32.9 to -0.2]). Adverse event rates were similar. CONCLUSIONS: BCL was noninferior to WL and superior in analysis stratified by final tumor type. Clinically meaningful relative reductions in PMR and re-excision rates were observed.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Evaluate efficacy and safety of carboplatin plus mirvetuximab soravtansine (MIRV) in folate receptor alpha (FRa)-expressing recurrent PSOC. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This phase 2, single arm trial enrolled patients with recurrent FRa-expressing (≥25% of tumor cells with ≥2+ membrane intensity) PSOC and 1 prior platinum-based therapy. Patients received up to 6-8 cycles of carboplatin (AUC 5) plus MIRV (6mg/kg AIBW) Q3W, followed by single-agent MIRV. Primary and key secondary endpoints were investigator-assessed objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1 in the FRa ≥50% group and FRa ≥25% group (ie, overall population), respectively. RESULTS: Among 125 enrolled patients (102 FRα ≥50%; 61 prior PARPi), ORR by end of 6 combination cycles was 62.7% (95% CI, 52.6-72.1) in the FRα ≥50% group and 62.4% (95% CI, 53.3-70.9) in the overall population. Most patients (n=101; 81%) transitioned to single-agent MIRV continuation with durable responses. Patients with FRa ≥25% had median duration of response of 11.2 months (95% CI, 8.5-13.6) and median progression-free survival of 11.0 months (95% CI, 9.8-13.1). Most common adverse events (AEs) were blurred vision (81%) and corneal events (74%); 96.7% of corneal cases resolved or had final grade 1. Treatment-emergent AEs led to MIRV and carboplatin discontinuation in 15% and 9%, respectively. Adjudicated treatment-related pneumonitis occurred in 19 (15.2%) patients: 14 grade 1-2; 3 grade 3-4, and 2 fatal cases. CONCLUSIONS: Carboplatin plus MIRV was manageable with dose modifications for AEs and showed meaningful activity, including in PARPi-exposed patients, supporting further evaluation in PSOC.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Uniform radiation dose escalation has not improved outcomes in locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and locoregional failure remains common despite multimodal therapy. We evaluated whether fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET)-guided dose escalation to metabolically active tumor subvolumes reduces locoregional failure compared with standard chemoradiation. METHODS AND MATERIALS: PET-BOOST was a multi-institutional, open-label, phase 2 randomized trial conducted at 7 Canadian centers (January 2017-May 2022). Eligible patients had inoperable, FDG-avid stage IIIA/IIIB NSCLC and an achievable boost dose of at least 65 Gy. Patients were randomized 1:1 to standard chemoradiation with 60 Gy in 30 fractions or metabolically adaptive radiotherapy with an integrated boost to FDG-avid subvolumes to a maximum of 85 Gy in 30 fractions. Concurrent platinum-based chemotherapy was planned, and consolidation durvalumab was permitted after 2018. The primary endpoint was 2-year locoregional failure; secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), grade ≥3 treatment-related toxicity, and quality of life (QOL). RESULTS: Seventy-eight patients were randomized: 40 to standard radiotherapy and 38 to dose escalation, with a median follow-up of 5.0 years. Median age was 64.4 years; 53% were male, 62% had stage IIIA disease, and 76% received consolidation durvalumab. Median prescription boost dose was 75 Gy. Two-year locoregional failure was 27.5% with standard radiotherapy versus 18.4% with dose escalation (P=.13). Two-year OS (72.5% vs. 73.7%; P=.91) and PFS (52.5% vs. 57.9%; P=.74) did not differ between arms. Grade ≥3 treatment-related toxicities occurred in 25% versus 37% of patients (P=.26), with one grade 5 pulmonary hemorrhage in the dose-escalation arm. QOL did not differ between arms. CONCLUSIONS: Metabolically adaptive PET-guided radiotherapy dose escalation was feasible in the context of consolidation immunotherapy and resulted in a numerically lower rate of locoregional failure, but did not significantly improve locoregional control or survival. The lower-than-anticipated event rate may have limited statistical power, and larger studies would be required to determine whether selective dose escalation provides a clinically meaningful improvement in locoregional control.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Total mesorectal excision (TME) is standard for low rectal cancer (≤5cm from anal verge) but causes permanent stomas, functional impairments and surgical risks. Local excision (LE) suits early tumors (cTis-T1N0) but has higher recurrence in cT2+; watch-and-wait (WW) after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy risks residual disease. Total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) improves outcomes, but prior LE trials had limitations. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate TNT combined with planned LE for organ preservation in selected low rectal adenocarcinoma patients. DESIGN: Prospective single-arm phase 2 trial (June 2022-March 2024, tertiary center) enrolled 57/60 patients (cT1-3N0M0 nonmucinous adenocarcinoma, etc.). TNT: 50 Gy + 2 cycles of CapoX (standard capecitabine + oxaliplatin) + 4 consolidation CapoX. Clinical complete response (cCR)/near-complete clinical response (ncCR) patients had LE; others got TME. Patients with high-risk residual disease after LE also had additional TME. RESULTS: Median age was 61 years (28-79); 66.7% were male. cT3 tumors were present in 78.9%, and 78.9% had tumors ≤3 cm from the anal verge. After TNT, 47.4% achieved cCR and 38.6% achieved ncCR. Among surgically treated patients, the pathological complete response (pCR) rate was 68.6%; in the overall population, with WW counted as non-pCR, it was 61.4%. The total complete response rate, including pCR and cCR managed with WW, was 68.4%. Sphincter preservation was 94.7%. LE was associated with lower median blood loss (7 vs 50 mL; P<0.001) and shorter median hospitalization (7 vs 14 days; P=0.001) than TME. Grade 3 adverse events occurred in 22.8%, most commonly lymphocytopenia; no grade 4 or 5 events occurred. Low anterior resection syndrome (LARS) scores were assessed after TNT and at 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively. At 6 months, LARS outcomes favored LE (80.0% vs 53.8% reporting no LARS; P=0.027). Wexner incontinence scores did not differ significantly between groups at any time point. CONCLUSION: TNT with planned LE is feasible in cT1-3N0M0 low rectal cancer, yielding a pCR rate of 61.4% in the overall population, 94.7% sphincter preservation, and acceptable toxicity. However, the non-randomized design and immature 3-year organ-preservation endpoint limit this study to a feasibility assessment and do not permit conclusions regarding comparative effectiveness versus WW. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05563922.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: : Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) have reshaped breast cancer treatment, yet their efficacy and toxicity in older adults (≥65 years) remain poorly characterized. METHODS: : We searched PubMed, Ovid MEDLINE, and Embase (Elsevier) through November 17, 2025 for phase 2 or 3 randomized trials comparing ADCs versus non-ADC therapies in metastatic or early-stage breast cancer. The primary analysis assessed progression-free survival (PFS) in metastatic disease and invasive disease-free survival (IDFS) in early-stage disease, stratified by age (≥65 vs. <65 years), using pooled hazard ratios (pHRs). Age-by-treatment interaction was assessed using the ratio of HRs. Secondary outcomes included overall survival (OS) and grade ≥3 adverse events (AEs). RESULTS: Of 3,045 records identified, 20 trials (14 metastatic, 6 early-stage; 13,055 participants, 18% aged ≥65 years) met inclusion criteria. In metastatic trials, ADCs improved PFS in both older (pHR, 0.64; 95% CI, 0.51-0.79) and younger participants (pHR, 0.58; 95% CI, 0.51-0.66), with no significant age-by-treatment interaction (pooled ratio of HRs, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.91-1.33). ADCs also improved OS in the metastatic setting, though no trial reported age-stratified OS. In early-stage trials, only two reported age-stratified IDFS, with discordant results precluding pooled analysis. Grade ≥3 AEs were reported across all trials, but only three provided age-stratified data, and none stratified AEs jointly by treatment arm and age. CONCLUSION: ADC efficacy in metastatic breast cancer was similar across age groups, though data in early-stage disease were limited. Insufficient age- and treatment-stratified toxicity reporting precludes meaningful safety assessment of ADCs in older adults with breast cancer.

papers.abstract_en: Amino acid (AA) substitutions are pivotal modulators of cellular signaling and homeostasis. Current studies of AA substitutions rely mainly on genomic and transcriptomic evidence, while proteome-level characterization remains underexplored, even though such substitutions can arise beyond DNA and RNA mutations. Here we address this gap with PIPI-C, an open-search mass spectrometry tool, and establish an integrated AA substitutomics pipeline to profile AA substitutions across five cancer cohorts and dissect the regulatory roles of substitution-bearing proteins. By cross-referencing 13,399 identified AA substitutions with matched whole-exome sequencing data, we observed no overlap with patient somatic mutations. Specifically, 61% of these substitutions required two or more base alterations and could not be derived from single-nucleotide variants, rendering them exclusively detectable at the proteomic level. The remaining 39% of substitutions were compatible with single-base variations. PIPI-C captured these candidate substitutions at the proteome scale, consistent with a translational-stage origin as reported for alternate RNA decoding in mammals. We further identified notable substitutions, including F43S and E91D in hemoglobin subunit beta, P584T in filamin A, and A175N in fructose-bisphosphate aldolase B, and our pipeline provides a framework for generating hypotheses about AA substitutions in cancer escape.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Optimal timing for distal reintervention after frozen elephant trunk repair remains debated. We evaluated patient characteristics, clinical outcomes, and predictors of distal aortic reintervention following Branched Stented Anastomosis Frozen Elephant Trunk Repair (B-SAFER). METHODS: From May 2021 to January 2025, 405 patients underwent B-SAFER in a prospective, single-arm, nonrandomized PS-IDE cohort. Among them, 117 patients required 148 distal reinterventions. Indications for initial repair were acute type A dissection (36/189, 31%), chronic dissection (62/138, 53%), and degenerative aneurysm (19/78, 16%). Most reinterventions (n=132, 92%) were planned. Primary endpoints were operative mortality, stroke, and paralysis. Kaplan-Meier analysis assessed survival and freedom from reintervention. Median follow-up was 1.3 years, and median time to reintervention was 8.7 months. RESULTS: Mortality after first reintervention was 6.5% (n=8). Permanent stroke occurred in one patient (0.8%), with no cases of paralysis. Causes of death included sepsis (n=4), hemorrhagic shock (n=2), pulmonary embolism (n=1), and intracranial hemorrhage (n=1). Freedom from reintervention at 2 years was 64%, lowest in chronic dissections (48%), intermediate in degenerative aneurysms (71%), and highest in acute dissections (74%). Larger descending and abdominal aortic diameters were the strongest predictors of reintervention. Survival at 2.5 years was similar across groups (81% acute, 81% chronic, 77% degenerative). CONCLUSIONS: Distal reinterventions after B-SAFER are common, safe, and are associated with acceptable early outcomes. Disease chronicity and aortic diameter predict reintervention risk. Frozen elephant trunk is an effective platform for staged aortic repair, and earlier reintervention in high-risk patients warrants further study. (245).

papers.abstract_en: IMPORTANCE: People who become pregnant after living kidney donation may be at increased risk of pregnancy-related adverse outcomes, although the evidence is unclear. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether pregnancies after living kidney donation are associated with a higher risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes than matched pregnancies among nondonors. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This matched cohort study used provincial administrative health care databases from Ontario, British Columbia, and Alberta, Canada, and included living female kidney donors aged 18 to 42 years who donated a kidney between July 1992 and August 2021 and subsequently had singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation. These pregnancies were matched 1:4 with singleton pregnancies of at least 20 weeks' gestation among female nondonors. Pregnancies in donors and nondonors were matched on delivery date, age at delivery, years between cohort entry and delivery, number of prior pregnancies, and income. Final follow-up occurred until March 2023. Outcome analysis occurred from August 2024 to September 2026. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was a composite of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia. Secondary outcomes included 12 maternal, fetal and neonatal adverse outcomes, including the individual components of the primary outcome, the composite of low birth weight or preterm birth, and small for gestational age at birth. RESULTS: The sample included 385 pregnancies in 252 living kidney donors (mean [SD] age, 27.8 [5.0] years) matched to 1540 pregnancies in 1535 nondonors (mean [SD] age, 27.0 [4.8] years). The primary composite outcome of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia occurred in 46 donor pregnancies (11.9%) and 128 nondonor pregnancies (8.3%; risk ratio, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.10-2.08). Among the 12 secondary outcomes, the 95% CI for the risk ratio excluded 1.00 for the outcome of small for gestational age, which occurred in 53 donor pregnancies (13.8%) and 121 nondonor pregnancies (7.9%) (risk ratio, 1.86; 95% CI, 1.37-2.52). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, pregnancy after living kidney donation was associated with a higher risk of the composite outcome of hospitalization with a diagnosis of gestational hypertension, preeclampsia, or eclampsia, when compared with matched pregnancies in nondonors. Most postdonation pregnancies were uncomplicated. These findings support counseling donor candidates who may become pregnant about this risk and informing the prenatal care of donors who become pregnant.

papers.results: 4个月时LDCT开具率Empower LCS组高于EUC组（15/30 [50.0%] vs 4/30 [13.3%]；p=0.002）；肺癌筛查讨论率亦更高（12/30 [40.0%] vs 5/30 [16.7%]；p=0.045）；LDCT完成率组间差异未达统计学显著（9/30 [30.0%] vs 4/30 [13.3%]；p=0.117）。探索性校正模型中，Empower LCS与更高的筛查开具几率相关（OR 7.32；95% CI 1.97-34.16），与更高的筛查讨论几率相关（OR 4.1；95% CI 1.20-16.28）

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: We evaluated the preliminary efficacy of Empower LCS, a culturally-adapted multilevel intervention, compared with enhanced usual care (EUC) for improving LCS uptake among Hispanic patients. METHODS: In this pilot randomized controlled trial, Hispanic patients aged 50-80 years who met 2021 US Preventive Services Task Force LCS eligibility criteria were enrolled between February 2024 and August 2025. Participants were randomized 1:1 to EUC or Empower LCS. EUC included usual care plus a one-page educational handout. Empower LCS included a culturally adapted decision aid, provider notifications, patient text reminders, and health-related social needs support. The primary outcome was LDCT ordering within 4 months, assessed by medical record review or self-report. Analyses used chi-square tests and logistic regressions. RESULTS: Sixty patients were randomized (mean age, 60.8 years ± 7.4; 37/60 [61.7%] male; 21/60 [35.0%] Spanish-speaking). At 4 months, LDCT ordering was higher with Empower LCS than with EUC (15/30 [50.0%] vs 4/30 [13.3%]; p=0.002), as were LCS discussions (12/30 [40.0%] vs 5/30 [16.7%]; p=0.045). LDCT completion was higher but not significant (9/30 [30.0%] vs 4/30 [13.3%]; p=0.117), likely due to small sample size. In exploratory adjusted models, Empower LCS was associated with higher odds of LCS ordering (OR, 7.32; 95% CI, 1.97-34.16), and discussion (OR, 4.1; 95% CI, 1.20-16.28). Qualitative interviews identified provider trust and logistical barriers as drivers of screening engagement and completion, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Empower LCS increased LDCT ordering and screening discussions in this pilot trial. These findings support culturally tailored, low-cost, scalable interventions to reduce disparities in LCS participation.

papers.title_en: Perioperative chemotherapy and stereotactic body radiotherapy versus perioperative chemotherapy alone in patients with high-risk, localised pancreatic cancer (MASTERPLAN): an open-label, phase 2, multicentre, randomised trial of the Australasian Gastro-Intestinal Trials Group.
papers.authors: Oar A, Kneebone A, Sjoquist KM, Espinoza D, Lee M, Le H, Gholamrezaei L, Chu J et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Icon Cancer Centre, Gold Coast University Hospital, Gold Coast, QLD, Australia.
papers.results: 中位随访3.2年（IQR 1.9–4.3）；12个月局部区域复发率SBRT组20.2%（95% CI 9.9–33.1） vs 单纯化疗组52.0%（30.3–69.9），亚分布风险比0.44（95% CI 0.22–0.88），p=0.022；≥3级不良事件47例中33例（70%） vs 25例中16例（64%），p=0.27；≥3级严重不良事件30例（64%） vs 14例（56%），p=0.24；单纯化疗组1例（4%）治疗相关死亡（胆道感染）；SBRT相关严重不良事件2例（2级小肠梗阻、3级胰腺炎）
papers.authors_conclusion: 在高危局限性PDAC患者中，化疗基础上加用SBRT与局部区域复发显著降低相关，且毒性未显著增加，值得在更大规模研究中进一步探索。
papers.ai_note: 主要终点为12个月局部区域复发这一替代终点，未报告总生存、无进展生存及手术切除率，无法判断局部控制改善是否转化为生存获益；因入组缓慢提前终止（74/120），检验效能不足，2:1分配致对照组仅25例，效应量CI较宽（上限0.88），p=0.022接近界值；开放标签设计可能影响复发评估与后续治疗；随访已达3.2年却仅报告12个月复发，随访数据利用不充分；安全性按实际接受治疗分析，与ITT主要分析人群不一致。

pico.p: 2020年2月26日至2025年1月6日纳入74例（男43例[58%]、女31例[42%]）初治局限性胰腺导管腺癌、ECOG 0-1、至少具一项高危因素（肿瘤>4 cm、胰腺外侵犯、淋巴结阳性、交界可切除或局部晚期），来自澳大利亚与新西兰14家医院
pico.ic: 随机（2:1，最小化法，按可手术/不可手术队列、化疗方案、随机时点、机构分层）接受研究者选择化疗（mFOLFIRINOX或吉西他滨+白蛋白紫杉醇）联合SBRT 40 Gy/5次（n=49） vs 单纯化疗（n=25）；诱导后评估手术，术后或继续化疗至计划24周

papers.reason: 为高危局限性胰腺癌是否在围手术期化疗基础上加用SBRT以降低局部区域复发提供随机对照证据，同时其提前终止与替代终点的局限可作为SBRT联合系统治疗试验设计（样本量、终点选择、对照组比例）的方法学参照。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) has poor outcomes and high rates of locoregional recurrence. MASTERPLAN evaluated whether stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) reduced locoregional recurrence in patients with high-risk, localised PDAC. METHODS: MASTERPLAN was an open-label, randomised, phase 2 trial conducted across 14 hospitals in Australia and New Zealand. Eligible participants were aged 18 years or older with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0-1, and had previously untreated localised PDAC with at least one high-risk feature, including tumour size more than 4 cm, extrapancreatic extension, node-positive disease, borderline resectable disease, or locally advanced disease. Participants were randomly assigned (2:1) using the method of minimisation to investigator-choice chemotherapy, with or without SBRT, stratified by participant cohort (potentially operable vs inoperable), planned chemotherapy regimen, randomisation before or within the first 28 days of chemotherapy, and institution. Chemotherapy consisted of mFOLFIRINOX (day 1 oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, irinotecan 150 mg/m2, leucovorin 50 mg, and fluorouracil 2400 mg/m2 over 46 h every 14 days for six cycles; all intravenous) or gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel (gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 and nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, and 15 every 28 days for three cycles; both intravenous). SBRT was delivered as 40 Gy in five fractions, with two to four fractions delivered per week, with real-time radiotherapy quality assurance. Surgical resection was considered following induction therapy, followed by a planned further 12 weeks of adjuvant chemotherapy with either mFOLFIRINOX or gemcitabine plus capecitabine (28-day cycles of 1000 mg/m2 intravenous gemcitabine administered on days 1, 8, and 15 with 830 mg/m2 oral capecitabine twice daily administered on days 1-21). Participants deemed not suitable for surgery continued the same chemotherapy for an additional 12 weeks with reassessment for surgical suitability permitted, for a total planned duration of chemotherapy of 24 weeks. The primary endpoint was 12-month locoregional recurrence in the intention-to-treat population, with safety endpoints analysed by treatment received. The trial planned to recruit 120 patients but due to slow accrual closed to recruitment early on Jan 6, 2025. Trial closure and database lock occurred on July 21, 2026. This trial was registered with the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trial Registry (ACTRN12619000409178) and ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04089150), and is complete. FINDINGS: Between Feb 26, 2020, and Jan 6, 2025, 74 participants (43 [58%] male, 31 [42%] female) were randomly assigned to chemotherapy and SBRT (n=49) or chemotherapy alone (n=25). After a median follow-up of 3·2 years (IQR 1·9-4·3), 12-month locoregional recurrence was 20·2% (95% CI 9·9-33·1) in the SBRT group and 52·0% (30·3-69·9) in the chemotherapy alone group (subdistribution hazard ratio 0·44 [95% CI 0·22-0·88]; p=0·022). Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 33 (70%) of 47 participants in the SBRT group and 16 (64%) of 25 participants in the chemotherapy alone group (p=0·27), with one (4%) treatment-related death secondary to biliary tract infection in the chemotherapy alone group. The most common grade 3-4 adverse events were diarrhoea (seven [15%] in the SBRT group vs five [20%] in the chemotherapy alone group), and thromboembolic events (three [6%]) vs one [4%]). Overall grade 3 or higher serious adverse events occurred in 30 (64%) of 47 participants in the SBRT group, and 14 (56%) of 25 participants in the chemotherapy alone group (p=0·24). There were two serious adverse events attributable to SBRT; grade 2 small bowel obstruction and grade 3 pancreatitis. INTERPRETATION: In patients with high-risk, localised PDAC, the addition of SBRT to chemotherapy was associated with significantly reduced locoregional recurrence without a significant increase in toxicity and warrants further investigation in larger studies. FUNDING: Medical Research Future Fund, Australasian Gastro-Intestinal Trials Group, National Health and Medical Research Council Clinical Trials Centre (University of Sydney), and Gut Cancer Foundation, New Zealand.

papers.abstract_en: Cellular heterogeneity and plasticity are hallmarks of cancer that contribute to tumor growth and therapy resistance. Here, we investigated metabolic heterogeneity in small cell lung cancer (SCLC), an aggressive cancer type with considerable plasticity between neuroendocrine (NE) and non-NE cellular states. Through integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses, we identified a universal dependency on exogenous cysteine/cystine (Cys) across all NE/non-NE SCLC cell states. Notably, NE and non-NE cells with low ASCL1 transcription factor levels underwent ferroptosis upon Cys depletion, whereas ASCL1high cells underwent apoptosis while remaining resistant to ferroptosis. This ferroptosis resistance was driven by the direct transcriptional activation of GCH1 by ASCL1, resulting in increased levels of the antioxidants BH4/BH2. Accordingly, combined Cys depletion and inhibition of BH4/BH2 synthesis reduced tumor growth in patient-derived xenografts. These findings demonstrate that metabolic state influences cell-death susceptibility in SCLC and provide a rationale for therapeutic strategies that exploit these metabolic differences.

papers.title_zh: 胃癌术后死亡负担远超30天窗口：单中心回顾性队列显示6个月内死亡近九成发生于出院后
papers.title_en: Beyond 30-day mortality: causes and risk factors of half-year postdischarge mortality after gastric cancer surgery.
papers.authors: Park K, Lee HJ, Yang HK, Kang MK, Kim JC, Kim SH, Kim J, Kong SH et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Surgery, Seoul National University Hospital, Seoul, Korea.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Conventional 30-day or in-hospital mortality underestimates the true burden of postoperative death after gastrectomy. This study aimed to characterize post-discharge mortality and its evolving determinants following gastric cancer surgery. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients who underwent gastrectomy for primary gastric cancer at Seoul National University Hospital between 2013 and 2019. Mortality data were updated through national death registry linkage with complete follow-up of at least 5 years. In-hospital deaths were reviewed using medical records, while out-of-hospital deaths were classified using death certificates and family interviews. Cox regression analyses were performed across sequential postoperative intervals up to 5 years. RESULTS: Among 4802 patients included in the analysis, overall mortality within 6 months was 1.2% (n = 57), of which 89.5% occurred after discharge. Thirty-day and 90-day mortality were 0.1% and 0.5%, respectively, demonstrating substantial underestimation by conventional short-term endpoints. Early mortality was primarily associated with emergency surgery and postoperative complications. Mid-term mortality was strongly linked to psychiatric disorders and systemic comorbidities, while low body mass index emerged as a significant predictor from 6 months onward. With longer follow-up, older age, renal or hepatic disease, multiple comorbidities, and incomplete (non-R0) resection became dominant risk factors. Tumor stage showed a strong association with mortality at 3 years. CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative mortality after gastrectomy is a dynamic process extending far beyond hospital discharge and shaped by distinct risk factors over time. Because most early deaths occur after discharge, improved survival requires surveillance strategies that target high-risk patients beyond the conventional 30-day window.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Acquired resistance significantly limits the long-term clinical benefit of osimertinib in EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). However, the early non-genetic adaptations and microenvironmental crosstalk that enable initial tumor survival remain poorly defined. This study aimed to elucidate the epigenetic-immune mechanisms driving osimertinib resistance and to identify novel actionable therapeutic targets. METHODS: We integrated transcriptomic profiling and clinical cohort analyses to identify therapy-induced secreted factors during the evolution of EGFR-TKI resistance. The upstream regulatory mechanisms were characterized using ChIP, Co-IP, and dual-luciferase reporter assays. The dual functional roles of the identified factor, serum amyloid A1 (SAA1), in tumor-intrinsic signaling and macrophage polarization were investigated in vitro. Finally, the therapeutic efficacy of combining SAA1 neutralization with osimertinib was evaluated across patient-derived organoids, xenografts, and immunocompetent spontaneous lung tumor models. RESULTS: We identified SAA1 as a critical therapy-induced secreted factor that progressively increases during the transition from drug tolerance to established resistance, which negatively correlates with clinical outcomes in patients receiving osimertinib. Mechanistically, osimertinib treatment suppressed the ERK-dependent phosphorylation of the transcriptional repressor GATAD2A at Ser114. This event destabilized the NuRD complex, thereby relieving the epigenetic transcriptional repression of SAA1. Secreted SAA1 promoted therapeutic resistance through dual mechanisms: activating the autocrine TLR4/NF-κB survival signaling in tumor cells and inducing the paracrine polarization of pro-tumorigenic SPP1⁺ macrophages. Therapeutically, targeted neutralization of SAA1 synergized robustly with osimertinib to reverse immunosuppressive remodeling and induce profound tumor regression in multiple preclinical models. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings define a novel therapy-induced ERK/GATAD2A/SAA1 epigenetic-immune axis that drives acquired resistance to osimertinib. SAA1 acts as a pivotal bridge between tumor-intrinsic survival adaptations and microenvironmental immune suppression, highlighting SAA1 neutralization as a tractable combinatorial strategy to enhance EGFR-TKI efficacy in LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Bone regeneration unfolds through sequential inflammatory, reparative, and remodeling phases, with macrophages functioning as pivotal regulators across these stages. Accumulating evidence identifies macrophage-derived exosomes (M-Exos) as key mediators of intercellular communication that dynamically shape the bone healing microenvironment. MAIN BODY: This review synthesizes current evidence on the spatiotemporal roles of M-Exos during bone healing and discusses how donor macrophage states may shape vesicle function across inflammatory, reparative, and remodeling phases. The discussion elucidates how dynamic macrophage functional states shape exosomal cargo and biological activity during distinct stages of repair. Concurrently, emerging engineering strategies to harness and enhance M-Exos' regenerative functions are evaluated, including exosome engineering, therapeutic cargo optimization, and biomaterial-assisted delivery approaches. In addition, this paper scrutinizes the translational landscape of M-Exos, emphasizing their potential as a cell-free therapeutic modality for bone tissue engineering while outlining key challenges critical for clinical implementation. CONCLUSIONS: By integrating the spatiotemporal functions of macrophage-derived exosomes (M-Exos) and single-cell-resolved landscapes of macrophage functional states, this review delineates the mechanistic links among macrophage state transitions, M-Exo cargo profiles, and regenerative outcomes across distinct phases of bone healing. It further provides a theoretical basis for developing stage-adaptive and functionally tunable M-Exo-based strategies for bone regeneration.

papers.abstract_en: In patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) treated with chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy, factors associated with efficacy overlap with prognostic biomarkers. Currently, there is no consensus on optimal product characteristics. We analyzed the phenotypic attributes of the anti-CD19 CAR T therapy axicabtagene ciloleucel (axi-cel) from 580 patients with NHL across multiple clinical trials with long-term follow-up (median, 41.9 months). A high proportion of naive-like (CCR7+CD45RA+) T cells was the most significant feature associated with prolonged progression-free survival (PFS; hazard ratio = 0.46, 95% confidence interval: 0.31-0.68, P = 9.8 × 10-5, high versus low naive-like T cell groups) without impacting safety. The relationship between naive-like T cells and efficacy was independent of tumor microenvironment characteristics (assessed in 112 patients). In multivariate models, the naive-like phenotype outperformed clinicopathologic features such as inflammatory markers and tumor burden, remaining significant after adjusting for product expansion. An inverse correlation was observed between prior lines of therapy and the proportion of naive-like T cells in both product and matched apheresis samples, suggesting a benefit of earlier intervention. The key findings were validated in an independent cohort of 203 patients treated with axi-cel-based therapy or brexucabtagene autoleucel. Mass cytometry by time-of-flight analysis of products from a subgroup of 116 patients confirmed an association between a CD8 naive-like T cell phenotype lacking expression of exhaustion markers, such as TIGIT, LAG-3 and PD-1, and PFS. The evidence generated by this study has the potential to advance the development of more effective cellular therapies.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Our purpose was to compare the safety and toxicity profiles of concurrent versus sequential administration of cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 inhibitors (CDK4/6i) and postoperative radiotherapy (RT) in patients with Positive regional nodes, operable, hormone receptor-positive (HR+), HER2-negative breast cancer (HER2-). METHODS: We conducted a real-world, multicenter retrospective cohort study enrolling 364 patients with node-positive, operable HR+/HER2- breast cancer who received postoperative radiotherapy combined with CDK4/6 inhibitors between January 2019 and December 2024. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to balance baseline covariates between the two arms, yielding 87 patients in each matched group. The primary endpoint was permanent CDK4/6i discontinuation, and secondary endpoints included dose reduction, drug substitution, grade ≥3 toxicities, and symptomatic radiation-induced lung injury (sRILI). RESULTS: No significant intergroup differences were observed in CDK4/6i discontinuation rates before or after PSM (unmatched: 10.4% vs. 8.4%, P=0.536; PSM-matched: 10.3% vs. 9.2%, P=0.798). Similar non-significant findings were identified for dose reduction and drug substitution across unmatched and matched cohorts. For severe toxicities, univariate analysis of the unmatched cohort revealed a significantly higher rate of grade ≥3 drug eruption in the concurrent arm (4.3% vs. 0.4%, unadjusted P=0.013), while this association attenuated to borderline statistical significance after covariate balancing via PSM (4.6% vs. 0.0%, unadjusted P=0.059). No significant between-group differences were detected in sRILI, interstitial pneumonia, grade ≥3 radiation dermatitis, grade ≥3 diarrhea, or hematologic toxicities pre- and post-matching. All grade ≥3 drug eruptions occurred outside radiation fields and presented as diffuse maculopapular rashes involving the trunk and extremities, consistent with CDK4/6i-related hypersensitivity. CONCLUSIONS: Concurrent CDK4/6 inhibitor therapy and postoperative RT demonstrate a manageable safety and tolerance profile. Given that treatment discontinuation due to ≥G 3 toxicities was observed in both groups, close toxicity monitoring and comprehensive management throughout the treatment course should be implemented when combining RT with CDK4/6i.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Colonoscopy is the gold standard for colorectal cancer detection and prevention, but its performance depends on operator skill and lesion features. Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted colonoscopy has been introduced to improve adenoma detection. METHODS: A comprehensive search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, ClinicalTrials.gov, and major Chinese databases to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing AI-assisted and conventional colonoscopy. Meta-analyses were performed using Review Manager 5.4 and Stata 14.0. The quality of evidence was graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) system, while trial sequential analysis (TSA) was applied to assess the robustness and information sufficiency of the results. RESULTS: A total of 46 RCTs encompassing 37,012 participants were included. Compared with conventional colonoscopy, AI-assisted colonoscopy was associated with a higher ADR (RR = 1.22, 95% CI = 1.17-1.27, P < 0.00001), polyp detection rate (PDR: RR = 1.22, 95% CI = 1.16-1.29, P < 0.00001), polyp detection per colonoscopy (PPC: MD = 0.28, 95% CI = 0.21-0.36), and adenoma detection per colonoscopy (APC: MD = 0.22, 95% CI = 0.15-0.29). The detection rate of sessile serrated lesions (SSL) was also higher in the AI-assisted group (RR = 1.20, 95% CI: 1.05-1.36, P = 0.007), whereas no significant difference was observed in advanced adenoma detection rate (AADR). CONCLUSIONS: AI-assisted colonoscopy was associated with improvements in several detection-related quality indicators, including ADR, PDR, PPC, APC, and SSL detection rate. However, given the very low GRADE certainty for ADR and PDR and the lack of long-term outcome data, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: Not applicable.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: High-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) is widely used as an early respiratory support strategy for adults with acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (AHRF). Although HFNC may reduce the risk of endotracheal intubation, it remains uncertain whether the available evidence is sufficiently mature and whether this potential benefit translates into improved survival. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis with trial sequential analysis (TSA) and GRADE assessment to assess HFNC versus standard oxygen therapy (SOT) in adult AHRF. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception to March 31, 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of HFNC versus SOT in adults with AHRF were included. The primary and secondary outcomes were endotracheal intubation and all-cause mortality, respectively. For each dichotomous outcome, the risk ratio (RR) with a 95% confidence interval (CI) was pooled using a random-effects model. Prespecified subgroup analyses were performed. TSA was performed for intubation, and evidence certainty was assessed using GRADE. RESULTS: Ten independent RCTs reported across 11 publications were included. Compared with SOT, HFNC was associated with a lower risk of endotracheal intubation (RR, 0.85; 95% CI, 0.77-0.93; P < 0.01; I² = 40%), but did not reduce all-cause mortality (RR, 1.01; 95% CI, 0.88-1.16; P = 0.85; I² = 0%). Subgroup analyses suggested a lower intubation risk with HFNC among non-immunocompromised patients, patients with COVID-19, and those with baseline PaO₂/FiO₂ ≤ 200 mmHg, although no statistically significant subgroup interactions were observed. In the primary TSA, the accrued sample size represented only 36.8% of the diversity-adjusted required information size. The cumulative Z-curve crossed the conventional significance boundary, but not the trial sequential monitoring boundary. TSA sensitivity analyses yielded consistent findings, indicating that current evidence remains inconclusive. GRADE certainty was low for endotracheal intubation and moderate for all-cause mortality. CONCLUSIONS: HFNC may reduce the risk of endotracheal intubation compared with SOT in adults with AHRF, but a survival benefit has not been demonstrated.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Providing caregivers with the skills and awareness of forgiveness is crucial to help them express their emotions, navigate the grieving process more smoothly, enhance their interaction with the patient, and make the time until the patient's death more meaningful. OBJECTIVE: To examine the effect of forgiveness psychoeducation on death anxiety, caregiver burden, and forgiveness tendencies in caregivers of patients at the end of life. METHODS: A randomized controlled experimental method was used, including a pretest, posttest, 1-month follow-up, and 3-month follow-up. The research sample included 56 caregivers of patients (experimental group = 28, control group = 28) at the end of life. During the study, forgiveness psychoeducation was administered to the experimental group, whereas no intervention was carried out in the control group. Data were collected using the Personal Information Form, Thorson-Powell Death Anxiety Scale, Caregiver Burden Scale, and Heartland Forgiveness Scale. RESULTS: The average scores of death anxiety and caregiving burden in the posttest and follow-up measurements of caregivers in the experimental group were statistically significantly lower than those of caregivers in the control group (P < .05). CONCLUSION: Forgiveness psychoeducation reduces death anxiety and caregiving burdens in caregivers of patients at the end of life. It is recommended to provide psychoeducation on forgiveness. IMPLICATION FOR PRACTICE: The psychoeducation conducted by Consultation Liaison Psychiatry Nurses aimed at increasing the internal process of forgiveness can positively influence the communication, emotions, and spiritual development of caregivers of patients at the end of life. Thus, improving the quality of care can be achieved through forgiveness.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Comparative evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of almonertinib in epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains fragmented across randomized and real-world studies. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to comprehensively evaluate the comparative clinical performance of almonertinib. METHODS: Eight electronic databases were systematically searched from inception to March 2025. Comparative studies evaluating almonertinib versus active control regimens in patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC were included. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed to synthesize objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and treatment-related adverse events. Methodological quality was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool and analogous domains for observational studies, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE framework. RESULTS: Fifteen comparative studies involving 1,902 patients met the eligibility criteria. Compared with control regimens, almonertinib was associated with higher pooled ORR (RR = 1.33, 95% CI 1.08-1.65) and DCR (RR = 1.14, 95% CI 1.03-1.26). However, after trim-and-fill adjustment for potential publication bias, the 95% CIs for both ORR and DCR included the null value, suggesting that the observed response benefits may be influenced by small-study effects. No statistically significant differences were observed for pooled PFS or OS. Almonertinib demonstrated a generally favorable safety profile, with a lower incidence of diarrhea, while rates of grade ≥3 adverse events and other major toxicities were broadly comparable between groups. Integrated analyses further suggested consistent concordance between ORR and DCR across most studies, supporting improved short-term disease control despite moderate-to-substantial between-study heterogeneity. CONCLUSION: Current comparative evidence suggests that almonertinib may improve tumor response and disease control while maintaining a favorable tolerability profile in patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC. Although favorable objective response outcomes were observed, these benefits may be influenced by small-study effects, and definitive survival advantages remain uncertain. These findings support almonertinib as a clinically meaningful therapeutic option, while underscoring the need for cautious interpretation and for larger, high-quality comparative trials with longer follow-up to further define its long-term clinical value. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Gastrin regulates gastric acid secretion and increases when gastric acidity is reduced. Erlotinib, a small-molecule inhibitor used to treat patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), has a pH-dependent absorption. We therefore investigated whether elevated gastrin levels, for example, due to proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use or achlorhydria, are associated with reduced erlotinib absorption. METHODS: Data of patients treated with erlotinib for NSCLC that were included in two previously conducted pharmacokinetic studies were used for this pharmacological proof-of-principle analysis. In these studies, patients were randomized to PPI use or not. Gastrin levels were quantified in samples drawn just before intake of erlotinib and used to study correlations with erlotinib concentrations. The pharmacokinetic endpoints area under the curve (AUC), trough concentration, and maximum concentration (Cmax) were correlated to gastrin concentrations and compared in patients with and without hypergastrinemia (gastrin ≥ 150 pg/mL). RESULTS: A total of 52 patients on erlotinib were included. Gastrin showed a significant inverse correlation with erlotinib AUC0-12h (r = -0.277; p = 0.047) and Cmax (r = -0.423; p = 0.002). In 11 patients with hypergastrinemia (gastrin ≥ 150 pg/mL), median erlotinib Cmax was > 30% lower (1890 ng/mL vs 1200 ng/mL; p = 0.024). The median AUC0-12h and AUC0-24h of erlotinib showed a non-significant trend towards lower AUCs of, respectively, 29% (p = 0.087) and 23% (p = 0.074), in patients with hypergastrinemia. CONCLUSIONS: Gastrin concentrations could potentially serve as a marker for erlotinib absorption, helping identify patients at risk for low erlotinib exposure.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: The biological basis distinguishing thymomas from thymic carcinomas (TCs) remains incompletely defined, despite longstanding efforts to interpret thymic epithelial tumors (TETs) in relation to thymic epithelial cell (TEC) differentiation. We integrated single-cell transcriptomic, immunohistochemical, and bulk transcriptomic analyses to define TEC programs associated with TET subtypes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We reanalyzed a publicly available human thymus single-cell RNA-seq dataset to define signature genes of TEC subclusters. Immunohistochemistry was performed on non-neoplastic thymus across developmental stages and on 83 TETs. Transcriptomic analyses were conducted using the TCGA-THYM cohort comprising 117 TETs. RESULTS: We identified an adult-enriched TEC subset with an aged progenitor-like program, marked by monoamine oxidase A (MAOA). Strikingly, MAOA immunohistochemistry highlighted spindle-shaped epithelial cells in the involuted adult thymus and in type A/AB thymomas. Most type B3 thymomas also exhibited broad MAOA reactivity, whereas TCs were negative or showed only scattered tumor-cell staining. Furthermore, MAOA immunostaining complemented KIT in the distinction between thymomas and TCs. In the TCGA-THYM cohort, MAOA expression reproduced these subtype-associated patterns and correlated with aged progenitor signatures. TEC signature scoring further revealed enrichment of aged progenitor-like programs in type A/AB thymomas, while type B3 thymomas concomitantly exhibited aged progenitor-like and cortical TEC-like signatures. In marked contrast, TCs showed low levels of aged progenitor scores but prominent mature medullary TEC signatures. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings refine the biological framework of TETs by linking thymomas to an aged progenitor-like TEC state. MAOA also offers practical diagnostic utility, particularly for distinguishing thymomas from TCs.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The Surgery As Needed for Oesophageal cancer (SANO)-trial demonstrated that active surveillance is non-inferior to standard surgery in terms of two-year overall survival in patients with a complete clinical response after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT). Active surveillance resulted in improved quality of life. Here, we report five-year outcomes. METHODS: From 2017 to 2021, a multicentre stepped-wedge cluster-randomised non-inferiority trial was conducted. Patients with locally advanced oesophageal cancer who achieved complete clinical response (defined as no tumour detected on endoscopic biopsies, -ultrasound, or PET-CT) underwent active surveillance or standard surgery. Cox regression was used to compare five-year overall and disease-free survival, and the cumulative incidence of distant metastases was estimated using competing risk analysis. RESULTS: A total of 309 patients were included, 198 underwent active surveillance and 111 underwent standard surgery. Median follow-up was 76 months (IQR 67-86). Five-year overall survival was not statistically significantly different between active surveillance and standard surgery (50%, 95%CI 43-57 vs. 54%, 95%CI 46-64; HR 1.17, 95%CI 0.77-1.77) with similar results across histologic subtypes. Disease-free survival was not statistically significantly different (HR 1.39, 95% CI 0.94-2.06). The cumulative incidence of distant metastases at five years was significantly higher in the active surveillance group compared to the standard surgery group (46%, 95%CI 39-53 vs. 29%, 95%CI 21-37; P<.01). Overall, 85 of 198 patients (43%) avoided oesophagectomy, including those with sustained complete clinical response at last follow-up or distant metastases detected within six months after nCRT. CONCLUSIONS: Overall survival at five years is not statistically significantly different between active surveillance and standard surgery in patients with oesophageal cancer and a complete clinical response after nCRT, despite a higher incidence of distant metastases in the active surveillance group. These findings support active surveillance as a feasible treatment strategy in selected patients.

papers.abstract_en: Microsatellite-stable (MSS) colorectal cancer (CRC) is a molecularly complex and clinically challenging disease subtype, lacking effective targeted therapies. Leveraging multiomic data from ∼2,000 tumor samples (including 316MSS CRCs not previously profiled) representing ∼4,500 molecular profiles and 195,246 single cells/nuclei, we uncover complex biology and therapeutic vulnerabilities. Application of a multiomic-phenomic integrative framework, including iPhenMap (a machine-learning tool), reveals complex molecular programs, including replication stress, right-sided biology, glutaminolysis-driven metabolic reprogramming, and MYC-E2F transcriptional networks governing epigenetic remodeling and perineural invasion. Focusing on RAS-mutant MSS CRC, functional validation in state-of-the-art patient-derived tumoroid and matched xenograft models confirms focal adhesion kinase (FAK), phosphoinositide-dependent kinase (PDK)1/2, and proteasome inhibition as potential therapeutic strategies when combined with mitogen-activated protein kinase (MEK) blockade. This work underscores the power of integrated multiomic profiling and functional modeling to refine potential treatment approaches in MSS CRC patient populations.

papers.abstract_en: Invikafusp alfa (invika), a first-in-class, bispecific, dual T cell agonistic antibody selectively targeting Vβ6/Vβ10 T cell subsets, is being evaluated in START-001, a multicenter phase 1/2 monotherapy trial in participants with mostly immune checkpoint blockade (ICB)-resistant, antigen-rich solid tumors. Primary outcomes were safety/tolerability and recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) in phase 1 and anti-tumor activity in phase 2. As of 12 March 2025, phase 1 completed dose escalation (n = 34) through dose levels of 0.01, 0.02, 0.04, 0.08, 0.12 and 0.16 mg kg-1 without reaching maximum tolerated dose, and initial phase 2 enrolled 18 participants. Two participants experienced reversible dose-limiting toxicities, one at each of the 0.08 mg kg-1 and 0.16 mg kg-1 dose levels. The most common treatment-related adverse event was cytokine release syndrome, mainly grades 1 and 2. No treatment-related deaths or non-laboratory grade 4 adverse events were reported. At the optimal biological doses (OBDs; 0.08 mg kg-1 and 0.12 mg kg-1) in combined phase 1 and phase 2 cohorts, the overall objective response rate was 14.8% (4/27), including confirmed partial responses in immunologically cold tumors, such as microsatellite stable colorectal cancer and programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1)-negative non-small cell lung cancer. No objective responses were seen at doses lower than 0.08 mg kg-1. Invika selectively and potently expanded peripheral and intratumoral Vβ6/Vβ10 T cells, of a predominantly memory-like phenotype, dose-dependently, peaking at the OBDs. Pharmacodynamic increases in interferon-γ and soluble CD25 followed a similar pattern. Integrated analyses from safety, pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic and preliminary anti-tumor data supported the selection of 0.08 mg kg-1 as the RP2D. In conclusion, phase 1 of START-001 met its primary outcomes by demonstrating the acceptable safety profile of invika consistent with its mechanism of action and selecting an RP2D. Initial phase 2 results further corroborated the safety of invika and expanded its preliminary evidence of clinically meaningful anti-tumor activity in ICB-resistant solid tumors, supporting further evaluation in the ongoing phase 2. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05592626 .
