papers.abstract_en: Paclitaxel (PTX) resistance is a major obstacle in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The metabolic enzyme phosphoglycerate mutase 1 (PGAM1) is implicated in chemoresistance, but its role in PTX resistance and cuproptosis remains unknown. We analyzed PGAM1 expression in PTX-resistant NSCLC cells and patient cohorts, performed truncation mapping and co-immunoprecipitation, and evaluated the PGAM1/PP2A/AKT/β-catenin/ATP7B axis. Drug sensitivity and cuproptosis were assessed in vitro, in patient-derived organoids (PDOs), and in xenograft models using the PGAM1 inhibitor HKB99. We identified that PGAM1 is overexpressed in PTX-resistant NSCLC and correlates with poor prognosis. PGAM1 overexpression reduces PTX sensitivity and confers cuproptosis resistance. Mechanistically, PGAM1 binds PP2A via its 1-150 region (critical residues V81, R83, N135, D144), inhibiting PP2A and enhancing AKT/GSK3β phosphorylation. This stabilizes β-catenin and promotes its nuclear translocation, where β-catenin/TCF4 drives ATP7B transcription. Elevated ATP7B lowers intracellular copper, impairs DLAT oligomerization, and confers resistance to elesclomol-induced cuproptosis. Pharmacologic or genetic inhibition of PGAM1 restored PP2A activity, re-sensitized PTX-resistant NSCLC cells to paclitaxel, and re-engaged cuproptosis. These effects were rescued by reconstitution with wild-type PGAM1, but not with the PP2A-binding-deficient mutant, indicating that PTX resistance is driven by the scaffolding function of PGAM1. The therapeutic potential of this strategy was validated in PDOs and xenograft models, where HKB99 synergized with PTX to suppress the growth of resistant tumors. In conclusion, PGAM1 drives PTX resistance by enabling cuproptosis evasion through the PP2A/AKT/β-catenin/ATP7B axis; combining PGAM1 inhibition with PTX represents a promising strategy for refractory NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: Cisplatin (DDP) resistance remains a major obstacle in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). This study investigates whether M2 macrophage‑derived exosomal miR‑3662 contributes to DDP resistance and uncovers the underlying mechanism. miR‑3662 was upregulated in LUAD tissues, further elevated in DDP‑resistant specimens and cell lines, and correlated with poor prognosis. Functionally, miR‑3662 overexpression enhanced DDP tolerance, clonogenicity, proliferation, and autophagy‑related activity while suppressing apoptosis; miR‑3662 inhibition reversed these effects. M2 macrophage exosomes transferred miR‑3662 into LUAD cells and promoted resistance, whereas GW4869 treatment or depletion of exosomal miR‑3662 attenuated this protection. Mechanistically, miR‑3662 directly bound the IRF8 3'UTR and reduced IRF8 protein expression. IRF8 occupied the RASSF5 promoter and activated its transcription. Consequently, miR‑3662‑mediated downregulation of the IRF8/RASSF5 axis induced cytoprotective autophagy. Restoration of IRF8 or RASSF5 counteracted M2‑exosome‑induced autophagy and resensitized cells to DDP. In xenograft models, targeting exosomal miR‑3662 restored IRF8/RASSF5 signaling, reduced autophagy markers, suppressed tumour growth, and improved DDP efficacy. These findings identify a novel microenvironment‑derived vesicular pathway where M2 macrophage exosomal miR‑3662 drives DDP resistance via IRF8/RASSF5 inhibition and autophagy activation, providing new insights into potential therapeutic strategies for overcoming platinum resistance in LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate a multimodal model integrating pancreatic parenchymal and peripancreatic fat radiomics with independent clinical predictors for early severity stratification in hyperlipidemic acute pancreatitis (HLAP). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included 356 patients with HLAP from three centers. HLAP was defined as acute pancreatitis (AP) with serum triglycerides ≥11.3 mmol/L or 5.65 to 11.3 mmol/L, accompanied by lactescent serum after exclusion of other etiologies. Patients from Center 1 were assigned to the training (n = 193) and internal validation (n = 83) cohorts, whereas patients from Centers 2 and 3 formed the external test cohort (n = 80). One noncontrast abdominal computed tomography examination acquired within 72 hours of symptom onset was analyzed per patient. Clinical, radiomics, and fusion models were developed using four machine-learning algorithms. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, decision curve analysis, and DeLong tests. RESULTS: The cohort included 107 patients with severe AP and 249 with nonsevere AP. The median age was 37.0 years (interquartile range, 31.75-45.0), and 268 patients (75.3%) were male. The final pancreatic parenchyma-peripancreatic fat-clinical combined model achieved AUCs of 0.947 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.897-0.986) and 0.846 (95% CI, 0.735-0.940) in the internal validation and external test cohorts, respectively, with external sensitivity and specificity of 0.611 and 0.871. DeLong testing showed significant improvements over the pancreatic parenchyma radiomics, 15 mm peripancreatic fat radiomics, and clinical models in internal validation (all p < 0.05), but not in external testing (all p > 0.05). papers.abstract_en: In proliferative glioblastoma, a subset of tumor cells survives early temozolomide (TMZ) exposure and drives eventual-resistance, yet the underlying mechanism remains unclear. We found that MYC target activation was associated with attenuated TMZ survival benefit in CGGA cohorts. In patient-derived MYC-high glioma cells, TMZ increased apoptosis but left a larger residual viable population due to enhanced proliferation; we defined these surviving cells as pioneer resistant (P-R) cells, which exhibited reduced TMZ sensitivity and a competitive survival advantage. Mechanistically, P-R cells adopted a senescence-like state via two coordinated arms of chromatin remodeling. On one hand, H3K27ac-dependent super-enhancers were gained at senescence-associated secretory genes; the CBP/p300 inhibitor A485 reverted the senescence-like state and restored TMZ cytotoxicity; On another hand, chromatin closed, reducing MYC occupancy at cell-cycle genes despite unchanged MYC protein, and suppressed nascent transcription and m6A modification, accompanied by cell-cycle arrest in some P-R cells. Furthermore, time-course analysis revealed that chromatin closure at cell-cycle genes is likely a temporally ordered epigenetic remodeling process, initiated by DNA damage-associated G2/M arrest mediated by WEE1 activation, followed by γH2AX-mediated recruitment of SUV39H1, which deposits H3K9me3 at MYC-bound loci to close chromatin. Functionally, early, but not delayed, inhibition of WEE1 with the novel brain-penetrant inhibitor TSL2304 blocked senescence-like epigenetic reprogramming, synergized with TMZ in vitro, and significantly prolonged survival in an orthotopic glioblastoma model. Together, these findings reveal a temporally ordered epigenetic remodeling in MYC-high glioblastoma that promotes survival after early TMZ exposure, and identify early WEE1 inhibition as a strategy to synergize with TMZ.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Non-invasive ventilation (NIV) adherence is critical to its effectiveness, yet no standardized pediatric definition of "optimal" adherence exists, and population-level data are scarce. RESEARCH QUESTION: What are adherence patterns to NIV in children, and which factors are associated with adherence in a provincial longitudinal cohort? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Canadian retrospective longitudinal cohort study linking records from the Ontario Ventilator Equipment Pool to health administrative databases. We identified children <18 years prescribed NIV with telemonitoring (2020 to 2022) and ≥1 month of data. The adherence definitions explored were the adult definition of ≥4 hours/day (primary) and measures of any daily use, daily NIV hours, and data missingness ("days not used" = 0 hours recorded; "days no data" = no signal). Mixed-effects regression models were used to explore adherence factors. RESULTS: We included 237 children (mean age 12.9 years; 61% male) with 3,685 person-months of NIV data (median 13 [IQR 8-24]). Across person-months, mean adherence by the ≥4-hours/day definition was 69.6%. Child-level monthly mean (SD) adherence was 59% (32%) by this definition, and 68% (26%) for any use. Mean (SD) daily use when used was 7.5 (3.2) hours. Monthly "days not used" and "no data" averaged 5.1 (6.4) and 4.4 (5.0) days, respectively. Greater adherence was associated with younger age (2-percentage-point decrease per year increase; 95% CI, 1-3), having ≥3 complex chronic conditions vs none (14 percentage-points higher; 95% CI, 3-26), and longer time prescribed NIV (2-percentage-point increase per year; 95% CI, 1-3). INTERPRETATION: NIV adherence was moderate across definitions, with higher adherence among younger children, greater medical complexity, and those using therapy longer, highlighting the need for pediatric-specific adherence targets and home NIV support strategies.

papers.abstract_en: Purpose Death receptor (DR) agonism is a promising strategy for cancer treatment, but clinical success has been limited by insufficient efficacy and/or on-target off-tumor toxicity, particularly hepatotoxicity. We hypothesized that restricting DR4 activation to the tumor microenvironment may enhance both therapeutic efficacy and safety. Fibroblast activation protein alpha (FAPα) is overexpressed on cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) within the tumor stroma of several solid cancers, making it an attractive target for conditional activation of DR4 on tumor cells. Experimental Design DuoBody-FAPαxDR4 is an Fc-silenced IgG1 bispecific antibody that binds to DR4 on tumor cells and FAPα on CAFs. Functional activity of DuoBody-FAPαxDR4 was assessed in tumor cell lines and colorectal carcinoma (CRC) patient-derived organoids (PDOs) using viability and bioluminescent reporter assays. Toxicity was tested using human primary liver spheroids in vitro. In vivo, antitumor activity was evaluated in patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models and models for spontaneous multiorgan metastasis by implantation of CRC-derived organoids into the cecum. Results DuoBody-FAPαxDR4 localized to the fibroblast-tumor cell interface, where it induced conditional caspase-8 activation and cytotoxicity in DR4-expressing tumor cells while sparing the fibroblasts. DuoBody-FAPαxDR4 did not induce cytotoxicity in human primary liver spheroids. In vivo, DuoBody-FAPαxDR4 demonstrated potent antitumor activity in PDX models and in mouse models of multiorgan metastases of CRC. Conclusions DuoBody-FAPαxDR4 is a novel bispecific antibody that conditionally activates DR4 on cancer cells exclusively in the presence of FAPα-expressing cells, resulting in targeted apoptosis and antitumor activity. These findings supported the initiation of a first-in-human trial in patients with solid tumors.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: This study aimed to estimate the familial risk of biliary tract cancer (BTC) encompassing bile duct cancer (BDC) and gallbladder cancer (GBC) in offspring and to evaluate the interaction between family history and gallstones. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Korean National Health Insurance claims and Health Screening databases (2002-2018) were linked to create a cohort of 6,217,057 offspring and 3,655,642 parent couples from 1.4 million families. Incidence rate ratios (IRRs) and hazard ratios (HRs) compared BTC risk in offspring with versus without an affected parent. Interaction between family history and gallstones was assessed with the relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI). Subgroup analyses were stratified by age, sex, and residence in Clonorchis sinensis-endemic areas. RESULTS: Offspring with an affected parent had a 2.17-fold higher BTC risk than those without (0.35 vs. 0.08 cases per 10,000 person-years). Maternal history conferred greater risk than paternal history (HR 3.20 vs. 1.33). The IRR was higher in younger offspring. GBC or BDC risk in offspring was significantly associated with maternal, but not paternal, history of the other biliary cancer type, whereas no same-site associations were detected. Familial risk was lower in endemic than in non-endemic regions. Offspring with both gallstones and a family history showed markedly elevated risk (HR 17.36; 95% CI 9.80-30.81), although the interaction was not statistically significant (RERI 7.63; 95% CI -2.32-17.58). CONCLUSION: Offspring with gallstones and a family history of BTC have more than a ten-fold increase in BTC risk. Early and intensive surveillance should be considered for this high-risk population.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The optimal salvage therapy for relapsed germ cell tumors (GCTs) remains undefined and the optimal timing for high-dose chemotherapy (HD-CT) is unclear. We analyzed data from the European Society for Blood and Marrow Transplantation registry to evaluate contemporary outcomes in patients treated with HD-CT across salvage lines. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We extracted data of adult males with GCTs (excluding mediastinal primary) who received one or more courses of HD-CT with carboplatin and etoposide between 2000 and 2022. Patients treated within 3 months from diagnosis were excluded, as this was considered upfront therapy. Time from diagnosis to first HD-CT (TT) was categorized in 3-6, 6-12, and >12 months. A Cox model with restricted cubic splines was used to evaluate the nonlinear effect of TT on survival. RESULTS: Data from a total of 2204 patients were analyzed. Histology was available for 1074, of whom 69% had nonseminoma. Among 969 patients with primary site information, 69% had testicular GCT. International Prognostic Factors Study Group (IPFSG) categories were available for 500 patients: 17% very high, 38% high, 31% intermediate, 10% low, and 3.6% very low risk. TT was 3-6 months for 280 (13%), 6-12 months for 831 (38%), and >12 months for 1093 (50%). Of the patients, 1118 (51%) received three cycles of HD-CT. Median overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were 36.4 [95% confidence interval (CI) 30.3-58.7] and 9.9 months (95% CI 8.5-12.4), respectively. Spline analysis showed increasing hazard of progression and death with longer TT. No interaction was observed between TT and IPFSG risk for PFS (P = 0.62), whereas a significant interaction was found for OS (P = 0.04) in non-high-risk patients. CONCLUSIONS: In the largest contemporary series of salvage HD-carboplatin-etoposide in GCTs, HD-CT was effective regardless of TT as a surrogate of salvage line, with a significant interaction in non-high-risk patients, suggesting a nonlinear association between HD-CT timing and OS.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of night shift-induced fatigue on radiology residents' diagnostic performance and to assess whether AI assistance offsets potential performance loss. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective intra-individual reader study, ten radiology residents (mean experience: 35 months; three women) interpreted three sets of 33 chest radiographs before and after a first-call on-site night shift. Sessions included two pre-shift readings (morning/afternoon, without AI) and two post-shift readings (morning, with/without AI). Eye tracking captured fixation duration and saccade count, and fatigue was defined as a ≥ 5% reduction in the slope of the saccadic main sequence between pre- and post-shift sessions. Diagnostic accuracy (Cohen's κ vs. expert majority vote), efficiency (mean reporting time per radiograph), eye-tracking metrics, and user surveys were analyzed with generalized linear mixed models and post-hoc Tukey-adjusted pairwise comparisons. RESULTS: Six of ten radiology residents were classified as fatigued, among whom diagnostic accuracy declined significantly post-shift (from κ = 0.71 ± 0.05 to κ = 0.61 ± 0.10; p < 0.001), with reduced fixation duration (p = 0.010) and saccade count (p = 0.015). Non-fatigued readers showed a smaller decline in accuracy (from κ = 0.72 ± 0.03 to κ = 0.65 ± 0.03; p = 0.037). Reporting times remained stable pre- and post-shift (p ≥ 0.463). AI assistance did not significantly improve diagnostic accuracy (Δκ = 0.03-0.04; p ≥ 0.525). Reporting times were numerically shorter with AI assistance in fatigued readers (Δ6.3 s; p = 0.122) and significantly shorter in non-fatigued readers (Δ9.9 s; p = 0.031). Surveys indicated mental exhaustion and reduced focus in fatigued readers. CONCLUSION: Night-shift-induced fatigue impaired diagnostic accuracy without slowing reporting speed, raising patient safety concerns. The utilized AI model did not restore pre-shift performance. KEY POINTS: Question Night-shift-induced fatigue may reduce diagnostic accuracy of radiology residents in chest radiography, yet its objective quantification and the compensatory potential of AI assistance remain unclear. Findings Fatigue, based on eye-tracking measurements of oculomotor efficiency, reduced diagnostic accuracy after night shifts without slowing reporting speed; AI assistance did not significantly improve accuracy. Clinical relevance Night-shift-induced fatigue can lower diagnostic accuracy in chest radiography despite unchanged reporting speed, posing patient-safety risks. The AI model used in this study cannot fully compensate for fatigue-related performance decline.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Peritoneal dissemination accounts for more than 40% of recurrences after radical gastrectomy for gastric cancer. Although peritoneal lavage cytology (CY) is routinely used to detect intraperitoneal free cancer cells, peritoneal recurrence still occurs in a subset of CY-negative patients. Novel molecular biomarkers are urgently needed to identify high-risk individuals within this cohort. METHODS: Direct flow injection quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (DFI-Q-TOF-MS) in negative ion mode was applied to profile peritoneal lavage supernatants from gastric cancer patients stratified by recurrence outcome (CY-R + vs. CY-R-). Candidate recurrence-associated features were selected by volcano plot, LASSO logistic regression, and Random Forest. PLS-DA with VIP scores was applied for stage-associated feature identification. RESULTS: A recurrence-associated lipid signature was identified comprising phosphatidylethanolamine species (PE (34:0), PE (34:1), PE (38:1), PE O-38:5), phosphatidic acid PA (39:3), phosphatidylinositol PI (22:1), and oxidized sphingoid base SPB (18:3;O2), implicating membrane remodeling, lipid signaling pathway alterations, and oxidative stress in the peritoneal microenvironment of recurrence-prone patients. CONCLUSION: This study presents an exploratory lipidomic characterization of peritoneal lavage supernatant in CY-negative gastric cancer, identifying hypothesis-generating candidate lipid features associated with recurrence status. Given the small recurrence group and absence of external validation, all findings should be interpreted as exploratory and require confirmation in prospective multicenter studies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Pre-existing psychiatric disorders have been associated with the severity of acute respiratory infections, including COVID-19, particularly in hospitalized populations. However, the underlying mechanisms, especially in community-based populations, remain unknown, limiting preparedness for future pandemics. We investigated the role of genetic liability for psychiatric disorders and related traits in COVID-19 and other respiratory infection severity among individuals reporting SARS-CoV-2 testing and available respiratory symptom data. METHODS: We included population-based cohort data from Denmark, Estonia, Iceland, Norway, and the United Kingdom (N = 78,507; 62% female; 41% SARS-CoV-2-positive; May 2020-March 2023). Respiratory infection severity was defined by self-reported days bedridden and an eleven-symptom composite score during the acute illness phase. Polygenic scores (PGSs) for eight psychiatric disorders and the personality trait neuroticism indexed genetic liability. Meta-analysed estimates from stepwise-adjusted regression analyses controlling for education, lifestyle, and psychiatric and somatic diagnosis history were used to assess associations between PGSs and acute respiratory infection severity, stratified by COVID-19 status. RESULTS: Higher genetic liability to insomnia, major depression (MD), and neuroticism was consistently associated with longer time bedridden (relative risk ratios per 1 SD change in PGS: 1.07-1.14, 95% confidence intervals [CIs]: 1.03-1.21) and more symptoms (incident rate ratios [IRRs]: 1.02-1.04, 95% CIs: 1.01-1.05) due to COVID-19. PGSs for insomnia, MD, neuroticism, anxiety disorder, bipolar disorder, and schizophrenia were also linked to higher non-COVID-19 symptom count (IRRs: 1.01-1.05, 95% CIs: 1.00-1.07). These associations remained robust after adjustment for lifestyle, education and medical comorbidities. Individuals in the highest MD PGS decile reported 20% more symptoms in non-COVID-19 illness and 10% more in COVID-19 compared with the bottom decile. No consistent associations were detected with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, alcohol dependence and post-traumatic stress disorder. No genetic link was observed with ischaemic heart disease or type 2 diabetes. CONCLUSIONS: Shared genetics may contribute to the link between psychiatric conditions and respiratory infection severity in community settings. Our results underscore the role of psychiatric genetic liability, beyond diagnosed psychiatric disorders, in contributing to both COVID-19 and other respiratory infection severity. These findings provide insights that may improve future risk stratification and public health strategies targeting respiratory viruses.

papers.abstract_en: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory dermatosis driven by abnormal keratinocyte proliferation and extensive immune cell infiltration. Emerging evidence links its pathogenesis to lipid metabolic dysregulation, yet the specific molecules bridging lipid remodeling to immune activation remain largely unknown. In this study, we integrated transcriptomic datasets through weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), differential expression analysis, and ensemble machine learning (random forest [RF] and support vector machine recursive feature elimination [SVM-RFE]), identifying ganglioside GM2 activator (GM2A) as a top lipid metabolism-related hub gene. Multi-cohort validation confirmed its robust upregulation in psoriatic lesions and its responsiveness to anti-psoriatic therapies. Furthermore, GM2A expression positively correlated with PASI scores and demonstrated strong diagnostic power in a nomogram-based model, reinforcing its candidacy as a diagnostic biomarker. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that GM2A is specifically elevated in spinous keratinocytes, where it drives ganglio-series glycosphingolipid reprogramming. Intercellular communication analysis demonstrated that spinous keratinocytes promote inflammatory infiltration primarily through the macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF)-CD74 signaling axis, targeting T cells and myeloid cells. In an imiquimod (IMQ)-induced psoriasis-like mouse model, GM2A was significantly upregulated and predominantly localized to the thickened spinous layer, accompanied by elevated levels of inflammatory cytokines. In M5-induced HaCaT cells, GM2A knockdown reduced the mRNA levels of IL-17 A, TNF, IL-6, and IL-1β, attenuated p65 phosphorylation, and decreased MIF release into the supernatant. Additionally, molecular docking identified cyclosporine A as a potential direct binder of GM2A with high affinity. Collectively, our study delineates a novel GM2A-driven metabolic-immune axis in psoriasis, positioning GM2A as a potential diagnostic biomarker and therapeutic target.

papers.abstract_en: Ionizing radiation (IR) induces oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation with ferroptosis contributing to radiation-induced cancer cell death. Peroxiredoxin 6 (PRDX6), a multifunctional enzyme involved in phospholipid repair and redox regulation, has been implicated in ferroptosis regulation, but its role in the radiosensitivity of cancer cells remains unclear. Here, we show that PRDX6 depletion enhances radiosensitivity in A549 lung cancer cells. PRDX6-silenced A549 cells exhibited elevated lipid peroxidation and labile iron levels, indicating a ferroptosis-prone state that was amplified by radiation. To identify the underlying drivers of ferroptosis sensitivity in the PRDX6 background, we performed global proteomic profiling of PRDX6-silenced A549 cells, with and without radiation. Basal PRDX6-deficient cells displayed increased levels of ACSL4 and DHCR7. ACSL4 activates peroxidation-prone polyunsaturated fatty acids for incorporation into membrane phospholipids, and DHCR7 depletes the antiferroptotic moiety, 7-dehydrocholesterol. MPST, an antioxidant protein, was downregulated. These changes were accentuated upon IR exposure with further suppression of GINS4, a negative regulator of ferroptosis. Functional rescue by oleic acid suggested the role of ACSL4 in the observed phenotypes. Radiosensitization via ferroptosis induction was additionally demonstrated in another human lung cancer cell line under the PRDX6-silenced state. Collectively, PRDX6 loss remodels the cellular proteome to establish a presensitized redox and lipid compositional state, which favors ferroptosis-driven radiosensitivity.

papers.abstract_en: Metabolic reprogramming fuels cancer progression, but whether common metabolic patterns exist across diverse malignancies remains incompletely understood. To address this, we integrated large-scale proteomic, transcriptomic [The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)], and spatial transcriptomic (Spatial Meta-Transcriptome Database) data sets comprising 3226 samples across 24 human cancer types. Utilizing a highly controlled, predominantly patient-matched design to minimize background noise, we characterized the pan-cancer metabolic landscape via reaction-level functional task scoring, pathway enrichment, multiomics integration, network modeling, survival analysis, and microenvironmental coupling. Consistently upregulated glycan biosynthesis pathways─particularly fucosylation and sialylation─and broadly enhanced nucleotide metabolism highlighted conserved programs potentially associated with tumor growth, adaptation, and immune evasion. These signatures proved robust against variations in tumor purity across the TCGA cohorts. Furthermore, gene coexpression network modeling prioritized specific hub genes associated with this pan-cancer restructuring. Exploratory high-resolution mapping aligned tumor immunogenicity with specific glycan pathways. Notably, tumor-intrinsic glycan upregulation negatively correlates with their immune score alignment, suggesting that tumor hyperactivation may obscure immune signals in bulk tissue. Together, our results define a robust computational landscape of shared metabolic alterations, providing a data-driven framework to guide future experimental validation of candidate therapeutic targets across diverse oncological contexts.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Sexual dysfunction, particularly erectile dysfunction (ED), is well documented after pelvic radiotherapy, but evidence in men with squamous cell carcinoma of the anus (SCCA) remains sparse. PURPOSE: To assess erectile and ejaculatory function, and sexual interest up to five years after curative-intent radiotherapy for SCCA, based on physician-graded toxicity and validated patient-reported outcomes (PROs). METHODS: This sub-study of the prospective DACG-I cohort (NCT05570279) included men treated with curative-intent radiotherapy for SCCA (2015-2020). PROs (EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-CR29) and physician-graded toxicity (CTCAE v4.0) were collected at baseline, 1, 3, and 5-years. Symptom prevalences were described descriptively. Longitudinal changes were assessed using linear mixed-effects models on linearly transformed EORTC scores. RESULTS: Of 80 enrolled men, baseline data were available for 76. At baseline, majority were symptom-free. Erectile and ejaculatory dysfunction emerged mainly within 1-3 years after treatment and persisted through 5 years. For the total cohort, ejaculatory dysfunction increased from 4.5% at baseline to 12.3% at 3 years. Physician-assessed ED (NCI-CTCAE grade ≥ 2) increased from 11.9% to 39.3% at 3 years. PROs indicated greater deterioration in erectile function at parallel time points. EORTC scores confirmed moderate-to-major clinically important deterioration at 1 and 3 years. Sexual interest remained stable over time. CONCLUSION: Sexual dysfunction, particularly ED, represents an increasingly prevalent and persistent late adverse effect in men treated with curative-intent radiotherapy for SCCA. The early onset of symptoms and the limited extent of recovery underscore the need for structured assessment based on PROs to support timely identification and supportive care.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of carbon ion radiotherapy (CIRT) in patients with non-metastatic, inoperable pancreatic cancer in a prospective phase 2 setting. METHODS: In this single-center investigator-initiated phase 2 trial, 25 patients with locally advanced or locally recurrent pancreatic cancer were included. CIRT was performed using an intensity-controlled rasterscanning system for beam application [total dose: 48 Gy (RBE), 12 fractions]. Concurrent chemotherapy with Gemcitabine 300 mg/m2 was administered weekly. The primary endpoint was the 1-year OS rate, defined as time from study inclusion. 1y- and 2y-OS and -PFS were calculated using the Kaplan-Meier method, 95 % confidence intervals are shown. Toxicity was evaluated using CTCAEv5.0. RESULTS: Twenty-three patients were included in the final analysis. After the completed 12-month follow-up of the last patient, the 1- and 2-year OS rates were 78 % [CI 63 %; 97 %] and 59 % [CI 41 %; 84 %]. The median OS was 26.5 months. The 1- and 2-year PFS rates were 26 % [CI 13 %; 52 %] and 10 % [CI 3 %; 37 %] with a median PFS of 8.1 months. Study treatment was well tolerated with three treatment-related CTCAE grade 3 toxicities, including one case of abdominal pain, one upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage and one ureteric stricture. No treatment-related CTCAE grade 4-5 toxicities were observed. CONCLUSION: Chemoradiation with carbon ions demonstrated encouraging overall survival and acceptable toxicity in non-metastatic pancreatic cancer patients. A subsequent randomized Phase 3 trial should investigate OS superiority of CIRT compared to conventional chemoradiotherapy or chemotherapy.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Krebs Von den Lungen-6 (KL-6) is an established biomarker for interstitial lung diseases (ILDs), but the utility of exosomal KL-6 versus plasma KL-6 in connective tissue disease-associated ILD (CTD-ILD) remains unclear. METHODS: We integrated single-cell transcriptomic re-analysis (GSE135893) with a multi-center cohort of 223 subjects, including 167 ILD, 22 CTD without ILD[CTD (Non-ILD)], 34 healthy controls(HCs). Plasma and exosomal KL-6 were measured, and diagnostic performance was evaluated via Receiver operating characteristic(ROC) analysis. Ten progressive ILD patients were monitored longitudinally. RESULTS: Single-cell sequencing revealed a significantly stronger correlation between Mucin 1 (MUC1)and exosomal markers (CD63/CD81) in alveolar type II cells from ILD patients compared to HCs, suggesting a potential vesicular association of KL-6. Clinical validation demonstrated that both plasma and exosomal KL-6 levels were significantly elevated in the ILD group. Crucially, for distinguishing CTD-ILD patients with negative plasma KL-6 results [CTD-ILD (plasma KL-6-)] from HCs, exosomal KL-6 [Area under the curve(AUC) = 0.900] outperformed plasma KL-6 (AUC = 0.879). More importantly, in differentiating CTD-ILD (plasma KL-6-) from CTD (Non-ILD), exosomal KL-6 again showed superior diagnostic accuracy (AUC = 0.782, sensitivity = 90.0%, specificity = 77.3%) compared to plasma KL-6 (AUC = 0.705, sensitivity = 65.0%, specificity = 81.8%). Plasma and exosomal KL-6 concentrations were highly correlated (rs = 0.968, p < 0.001). In longitudinal monitoring, both biomarkers increased in patients with radiographic disease progression. CONCLUSIONS: Exosomal KL-6 is superior to plasma KL-6 for diagnosing CTD-ILD, especially in plasma KL-6-negative patients, and shows potential for monitoring disease progression.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Microbeam Radiotherapy (MRT) is an emerging radiotherapy technique which delivers spatially fractionated beams on a micrometre scale. In preclinical studies MRT has demonstrated superior normal tissue sparing compared to conventional radiotherapy while maintaining tumour control. However, MRT has traditionally been achievable only at large synchrotron facilities which has impeded clinical translation. The development of a compact line-focus X-ray tube (LFXT) provides a pathway for clinical MRT, but identification of clinically and dosimetrically suitable patient scenarios is required for first-in-human trials. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Potentially eligible patients were selected from our patient cohort based on clinical criteria including palliative treatment indication, superficial tumour location, reproducible and safe positioning, minimal interference from other therapies, and expected benefit from MRT. Three-dimensional forward treatment planning was performed in Eclipse using gantry rotations, collimator positioning, and conformal masks to treat the clinical target volume (CTV). Dose was calculated in Eclipse using a custom Monte Carlo-based hybrid algorithm adapted for the compact LFXT system with a 300 kVp beam and an eccentric focal spot. A single-fraction equivalent uniform doses (EUD) of 3 Gy was prescribed to the target volume. Dose distributions were analysed using dose-volume histograms (DVHs), peak and valley depth dose profiles, and peak-to-valley dose ratios (PVDRs). RESULTS: Selected cases included primary lymphoma, squamous cell carcinoma, and superficial soft tissue metastases. Dosimetric analysis under exploratory assumptions demonstrated dosimetrically feasible treatment plans with optimal target coverage and organ-at-risk (OAR) sparing for gluteal, nuchal, and inguinal tumours. Maximum OAR doses remained below 8.5 Gy, except in bone or overlapping high-density regions. The mean peak and valley dose across all plans was 57.2 Gy and 3.9 Gy, respectively, with a mean PVDR of 15.4. Dose inhomogeneities were observed due to tissue heterogeneity, kilovoltage beam interactions, and a limited range of suitable gantry angles. Tumours in anatomically complex regions, including those in proximity to OARs or tissue inhomogeneities, showed less favourable trade-offs between target coverage and OAR sparing. CONCLUSION: This study identifies clinically and dosimetrically suitable scenarios for first-in-human MRT trials, highlighting superficial tumours as optimal initial indications. While peak, valley, and PVDR values align with preclinical evidence, their clinical significance remains uncertain. Careful, safety-driven dose escalation studies will be required to establish a foundation for responsible and effective clinical application of MRT in early-phase clinical trials.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Minimally invasive surgery (MIS) videos support education and quality review, but raw recordings contain non-informative frames that impede review and increase storage. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 300,832 frames from 120 MIS videos performed by 30 surgeons. An EndoViT-initialized Vision Transformer (ViT) was evaluated using leave-six-surgeons-out cross-validation and compared with conventional vision models. GPT-4o-mini, LLaVA, and Doubao were separately evaluated under zero- and few-shot prompting on a balanced 400-frame subset that was not sample-size matched to the ViT evaluation. We also explored the association between surgeon experience and non-informative-frame ratio. RESULTS: In the within-dataset comparison of trained vision models, the EndoViT-initialized ViT achieved an aggregate accuracy and F1-score of 0.942. In an exploratory few-shot analysis within a separate 400-frame balanced benchmark, GPT-4o-mini achieved an accuracy of 0.890 and F1-score of 0.880; exemplar-test disjointness could not be confirmed. Because the ViT and LMM evaluations used different test sets and sample sizes, these estimates do not support a direct comparison of model superiority. The surgeon-level analysis showed no statistically significant association between experience and the non-informative-frame ratio (r = - 0.421, 95% CI - 0.83 to 0.28; p = 0.226). CONCLUSION: The EndoViT-initialized ViT performed well in this single-institution dataset, whereas prompt-only LMM performance varied in a separate small benchmark. Matched evaluation with documented exemplar-test separation and external validation is required before determining relative performance or clinical readiness. Automated frame triage may support MIS video management with human oversight.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Surgical video review is increasingly used to support self-reflection and technical skill development. However, little is known about which aspects of video review are the most effective for general surgery residents. We hypothesize that senior residents would find self-review most helpful while junior residents would benefit more from guided review with an attending coach. METHODS: In this single institution prospective cohort study, residents reviewed hepatocystic triangle dissection videos cropped from laparoscopic cholecystectomy operations captured on OR Black Box where the resident was the primary surgeon during this portion of the case. Over one-hour sessions, residents completed four structured video review modalities: standardized public video, peer video, self-review, and attending coach-guided review. Attending coaches were fellowship-trained MIS faculty with surgical education training. Outcomes included perceived usefulness (5-point Likert-type scale) and modified Objective Structured Assessment of Technical Skills (mOSAT) scores. RESULTS: Thirteen residents (5 seniors, 38.5% completed PGY 3-year or more) participated, having completed a mean of 72.2 (SD 36.7) laparoscopic cholecystectomies. Attending coach-guided review was rated most helpful (mean = 4.9/5), followed by self-review (4.2/5), peer video (3.3/5), and standardized public video (2.9/5). Differences across modalities were significant (ANOVA F(3,48)=6.53, p < 0.001). Junior residents tended to overestimate their performance compared to blinded coach assessment significantly more than senior residents (- 4.4 vs 1.8, p = 0.038). CONCLUSIONS: Attending coach-guided video review is perceived as most useful by residents at all levels. The time investment of attending coaches appears worthwhile, as both junior and senior residents benefit most from guided expert reflection. Incorporating structured video review sessions with attending coaches could enhance surgical residency training in technical skills, decision-making, and self-assessment.

papers.abstract_en: The reliability of emergent histopathology foundation models (Histo-FMs) for real-world diagnostic tasks remains unproven. Given the complexity of diagnostic tasks and the challenges inherent in real-world data, we utilized Histo-FMs to investigate their utility for morphological subtyping of Barrett's esophagus (BE) and detecting esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) across the BE progression spectrum. We benchmarked Histo-FMs on the BarrettNet cohort, spanning diagnostic categories ranging from normal to EAC (N2EAC). The dataset comprised 3528 hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole-slide images (WSIs) from 790 patients. A multi-magnification, multi-backbone aggregation of the five most expert-consistent single-scale models yielded incremental performance gains (AUROC of 0.907, F1-score of 0.696, accuracy of 0.795, and κ of 0.651 for morphological subtyping; AUROC of 0.909, F1-score of 0.836, accuracy of 0.959, and κ of 0.673 for EAC detection), with non-uniform gains across single-model comparisons and limited benefit for dysplasia. The findings support the capability of Histo-FMs for BE morphological subtyping and EAC detection in a multicenter clinical cohort, while highlighting persistent challenges in dysplasia assessment and the need for external validation. This study provides a foundation for future clinical validation.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: Engagement of the co-stimulatory receptor OX40on activated T cells enhances T-cell activation, survival, and proliferation. First-generation agonistic OX40 antibodies have shown limited clinical efficacy so far. The investigational HexaBody®-OX40 (GEN1055/BNT315) was designed to promote FcγR-independent higher-order OX40 clustering on the cell surface, thereby leveraging receptor biology to achieve optimal stimulation. We assessed the in vitro and in vivo functional activity of HexaBody-OX40, and evaluated the potential of concomitantly blocking PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitory signals to amplify T-cell activity. EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN: Reporter assays and primary human T-cell assays using healthy donor and cancer patient cells were used to study the effects of HexaBody-OX40, alone and in combination with PD-(L)1 blocking antibodies, on T-cell activation and proliferation in vitro. Antitumor activity and pharmacodynamic effects were evaluated in human OX40 knock-in mice and human OX40/PD-1 double knock-in mice bearing MC38 tumors. RESULTS: HexaBody-OX40 exhibited FcγR-independent OX40 agonistic activity in vitro, enhancing T-cell activation, proliferation, and cytokine secretion, and promoted tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte expansion in primary tumor samples ex vivo. In vivo, HexaBody-OX40 demonstrated antitumor activity accompanied by peripheral and intratumoral T-cell immunomodulation. PD-(L)1 blockade further potentiated HexaBody-OX40-induced T-cell proliferation, activation, and cytokine secretion in assays using PBMCs from either healthy donors or cancer patients previously treated with PD-(L)1 blocking antibody. Combined with pembrolizumab, HexaBody-OX40 enhanced antitumor activity and T-cell immunomodulation beyond either monotherapy in vivo. CONCLUSIONS: HexaBody-OX40 agonistically enhanced T-cell mediated antitumor immunity through FcγR-independent OX40 agonism. The combination of HexaBody-OX40 with PD-(L)1 blocking antibodies enhanced the effect of both single agent treatments.

papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint blockade has transformed cancer therapy, but immune-related adverse events (irAEs) remain a major, sometimes fatal, limitation, and the lack of robust preclinical models has hindered mechanistic insight. We present the lifestyle-induced susceptibility to irAEs (LISA) model, in which diet-driven metabolic and microbial alterations recreate human-like susceptibility to anti-PD-1 toxicity. LISA recapitulates multi-organ irAEs with immune infiltration and cytokine production, severity depending on sex, age, treatment modality, and immunotherapy response. Mechanistically, dysbiosis marked by Akkermansia muciniphila enrichment accompanies aberrant immune activation, driving regulatory T cell (Treg) fragility and CD8+ cytotoxic effector populations, both observed in patients with irColitis. Dietary reversal, metabolite supplementation, and blocking interferon (IFN)-γ production or signaling in Tregs restored Treg stability and resolved inflammation. Human-to-mouse fecal microbiome transfer interacts with recipient diet to shape susceptibility. Together, these findings identify dietary, microbial, and immune drivers of irAEs, which can be leveraged to improve immunotherapy responses while minimizing toxicity.

papers.abstract_en: Cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and natural killer cells are critical effectors of anti-tumor immunity. Cytotoxic lymphocytes eliminate tumor cells by releasing perforin (Prf1), a pore-forming protein that enables granzymes (Gzms) to enter target cells and trigger both caspase-dependent and -independent cell death. Here, we uncover a previously unrecognized, Gzm-independent function of Prf1. We find that Prf1 directly induces tumoral ferroptosis, an iron- and lipid-dependent form of cell death. Mechanistically, Prf1-mediated pore formation drives endocytosis of the transferrin receptor, which increases cellular iron uptake. Prf1 promotes the formation of endosomal-mitochondrial contacts, which leads to mitochondrial iron accumulation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and tumor cell ferroptosis. Dietary iron supplementation suppresses tumor progression in murine tumor models in a Prf1-dependent manner. Higher Prf1 expression correlates with improved survival and enhanced response to immune checkpoint blockade in patients with cancer. These findings define a Gzm-independent function of Prf1 as a direct executioner of cancer cell death through ferroptosis.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: HERV-K (HML-2) is the most studied transcriptionally active endogenous retrovirus in human cancers, yet immune tolerance and incomplete mechanistic understanding have impeded its clinical use as an immunotherapy target. We hypothesized that rational engineering of the HERV-K envelope putative immunosuppressive domain (ISD) could improve immunogenicity. METHODS: We performed a mutational screen across the ISD region, evaluated NF-κB activation and then analyzed antigen expression in human monocyte-derived dendritic cells (moDCs) using flow cytometry, RNA-seq, and TEM. Human PBMCs were expanded with HERV-K-transduced moDCs to assess T cell priming and expansion ex vivo. Immunogenicity was tested in mice, HERV-K transgenic mice, and cynomolgus macaques using adenoviral and LNP-mRNA vectors. Antitumor efficacy was evaluated in a murine metastatic renal carcinoma HERV-K expressing tumor model. RESULTS: Engineering the HERV-K envelope ISD to Q525A (ISDmut) enhanced NF-κB activation, antigen expression, and antigen presentation and cell death associated gene expression pathways in human dendritic cells while preserving virus-like particle assembly. HERV-K-ISDmut-transduced human dendritic cells expanded CD4+ and CD8+ T cells capable of recognizing HLA-matched, HERV-K expressing tumors, demonstrating that T cells from the human repertoire can be expanded ex vivo. In vivo, mRNA and adenoviral vectors encoding HERV-K-ISDmut elicited strong immune responses in mice, broke tolerance in HERV-K transgenic mice, and induced humoral responses in cynomolgus macaques. In mice, an adenovirus vectored HERV-K-ISDmut immunization further conferred increased survival in a murine renal carcinoma HERV-K expressing tumor model and benefitted from anti-PD-1 therapy. CONCLUSIONS: These results show that the rational redesign of the HERV-K ISD generates a potent immunogen capable of expanding human T cells and mediating mechanistically relevant anti-tumor immunity. We propose that HERV-K-ISDmut antigens represent a promising platform for cancer immunotherapy which should be explored in future clinical trials.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess the additional prognostic value of white matter hyperintensity (WMH) beyond Coronary Artery Disease Reporting and Data System (CAD-RADS) for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with suspected or known coronary artery disease (CAD). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study included 1085 patients who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography and brain magnetic resonance imaging between November 2018 and December 2022. Time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves were used to evaluate the predictive values, and the C-statistic was employed to determine their discriminatory power. RESULTS: 170 (15.7%) patients experienced MACE during a median follow-up of 63.1 months. WMH remained a significant and independent risk factor for predicting MACE after adjustments with clinical variables alone or with CAD-RADS. In the training set, the clinical-CAD-RADS-WMH model showed area under the curves (AUCs) of 0.719, 0.740, and 0.776 for predicting MACE at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. The model showed a consistent performance trend with AUCs of 0.819, 0.836, and 0.823 in the test set over 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. Both the addition of WMH to the clinical model and to the clinical plus CAD-RADS model significantly increased the C-statistic index (p = 0.007, p = 0.038 in the training set and p = 0.002, p = 0.004 in the test set). These trends continued to be present when WMH was analyzed as a continuous variable. CONCLUSION: An elevated WMH was related to a higher risk of MACE in patients with suspected or established CAD. Moreover, WMH demonstrated additional prognostic value for MACE beyond CAD-RADS.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: To investigate the preoperative predictive value of histogram features of diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI), and intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) parameters for isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) and telomerase reverse transcriptase promoter (TERTp) mutation status in adult diffuse gliomas, and to identify independent prognostic factors for overall survival (OS). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 404 patients who underwent DWI, DKI, and IVIM imaging. Region-specific logistic regression models were developed using stratified 70:30 training and hold-out test splits. Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic curves were used to assess predictive performance. Decision-curve, synthetic minority over-sampling technique (SMOTE) sensitivity, and bootstrap stability analyses were also performed. Prognostic factors were evaluated using Cox regression in 343 patients with follow-up. RESULTS: For IDH prediction, areas under the curve (AUCs) ranged from 0.874 to 0.920 in solid tumor and 0.902 to 0.936 in peritumoral edema, without significant between-region differences. For TERTp prediction in IDH wild-type gliomas, peritumoral edema models achieved higher AUCs than their solid tumor counterparts: DWI, 0.893 versus 0.677 (P = 0.019); DKI, 0.916 versus 0.754 (P = 0.036); IVIM, 0.934 versus 0.819 (P = 0.022); and combined, 0.948 versus 0.819 (P = 0.020). Decision-curve analysis favored the peritumoral edema combined model, and the regional discrimination pattern persisted after SMOTE balancing. In the overall cohort, peritumoral edema Kskewness, D*10th, and fentropy were independently associated with OS, alongside age, IDH status, O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase promoter methylation, and Ki-67 LI. Within the IDH wild-type subgroup, age, TERTp status, and Ki-67 LI were independent prognostic factors. CONCLUSION: Diffusion histogram models provided high discrimination for IDH status in both regions. Peritumoral edema models offered superior TERTp prediction in IDH wild-type gliomas, while selected peritumoral features provided prognostic information in the overall cohort.

papers.abstract_en: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Deep learning-based high-resolution computed tomography (CT) of the lung parenchyma has not been directly compared with ultra-high-resolution CT (UHR-CT). We compared image quality between deep learning-based super-resolution CT and UHR-CT using identical cadaveric human lungs. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 10 cadaveric human lungs scanned using conventional CT and UHR-CT at two dose levels (9 mGy, 2 mGy). Five reconstruction methods were evaluated, including deep learning-based synthetic super-resolution CT (CCT-1024-PIQE) and UHR-CT-derived high-resolution images reconstructed using a deep learning-based denoising algorithm (UHR-1024-AiCE). Two radiologists independently assessed the bronchioles, seven abnormal findings, and overall image quality using a 5-point scale. The objective image noise was also quantified. Statistical comparisons were performed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. RESULTS: At 9 mGy, no significant differences were observed in the bronchioles, whereas UHR-1024-AiCE demonstrated higher scores than CCT-1024-PIQE for ground-glass opacities and intralobular reticulation (all P ≤ 0.007). At 2 mGy, CCT-1024-PIQE showed no significant differences from UHR-1024-AiCE for most findings. Compared with the 512-matrix reconstructions, CCT-1024-PIQE achieved consistently higher visual scores at both dose levels (most comparisons, P < 0.05). Image noise increased at 2 mGy across all methods, while PIQE-based reconstructions showed lower noise (P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Deep learning-based super-resolution CT showed no significant differences from UHR-CT in many pulmonary findings, particularly under low-dose conditions, while improving visualization compared to conventional 512-matrix reconstructions.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Mitral annular calcification (MAC) presents a formidable challenge in mitral valve surgery owing to risks of atrioventricular groove disruption, circumflex artery injury, and paravalvular leaks. The optimal operative strategy varies according to the severity of annular calcification, extent of ventricular extension, and the patient-specific risk profile. METHODS: A narrative expert review was performed synthesizing contemporary surgical series, imaging-guided approaches, and transcatheter strategies for mitral valve intervention in the setting of MAC. Technical considerations, complication avoidance strategies, and decision-making frameworks were integrated into a new severity-based operative algorithm. RESULTS: We developed a decision matrix to stratify patients into four categories to guide preoperative planning and operative decisions. MAC management lies on a spectrum between working around the MAC with no resection ("respect" the MAC) to complete MAC resection with atrioventricular groove reconstruction ("resect" the MAC). Severe or circumferential MAC demands tailored strategies, including transcatheter or hybrid approaches. In patients with mild MAC, mitral valve repair remains feasible and preferred. Moderate MAC requires individualized decision-making; repair is achievable when leaflet mobility is preserved, and decalcification permits secure annuloplasty. Replacement is favored when leaflet restriction or annular rigidity precludes durable reconstruction. The extent of decalcification should be tailored to the patient's risk profile and surgical expertise to ensure durable results. CONCLUSIONS: Mitral valve intervention in the setting of MAC requires an individualized approach. We propose a practical management algorithm, stratified by patient risk and anatomic feasibility.

papers.abstract_en: The Mexican Duck (Anas diazi) is a quasi-endemic North American dabbling duck whose evolutionary history is marked by recent Pleistocene divergence and ongoing introgressive hybridization with the Mallard (Anas platyrhynchos). Because the two species are morphologically and genomically very similar, identifying where their genomes differ structurally is central to understanding how species integrity is maintained under gene flow. Here we present the first highly contiguous de novo genome assembly of A. diazi (PacBio HiFi) and use it to map chromosomal inversions across the phylogeny of the mallard complex. k-mer profiling revealed high heterozygosity (1.08%), and read-depth haplotype purging recovered an accurate 1.19 Gb haploid consensus (BUSCO 95.7%). Using independent, orientation-aware approaches-including read-based structural-variant detection and phylogenetic polarization-we find that structural differences between A. diazi and the Mallard are numerous but small (kb-scale), and strongly enriched on the Z chromosome. Loci within these species-specific inversions (e.g., PIK3C3, RIT2, and DIPK2B) exhibit high structural protein conservation, while functional annotation highlights post-transcriptional mechanisms. Furthermore, the capture of master non-coding RNAs within these rearrangements, including the spliceosomal U1 and the nucleolar SNORA5, provides a mechanism for species-specific alternative splicing and translational control. Ultimately, we find no evidence for macro-inversion 'supergenes'; instead, the Mexican Duck maintains its divergence through fine-scale, Z-concentrated and post-transcriptional rewiring, consistent with the genomic architecture of recently diverged, hybridizing lineages.

papers.abstract_en: Radiotherapy (RT) combined with PD-1/PD-L1 blockade can induce systemic antitumor responses, but robust control of distant lesions remains uncommon. We identified a quadruple regimen combining immunogenic hypofractionated RT (hRT; 8 Gy × 3) to the primary tumor, low-dose RT (LDRT; 3 Gy × 3) to the secondary tumor, anti-PD-1 (αPD-1), and fenofibrate (FFB), a clinically approved PPARα agonist, that enhanced antitumor efficacy in two bilateral tumor models. Only this regimen substantially improved secondary-tumor control, eradicating LDRT-treated secondary tumors in all mice in the immunologically cold C51 model and inducing prolonged control in the aggressive, αPD-1-poorly responsive B16-CD133 model. This effect required CD8+ T cells. Tumor-specific CD8+ TILs showed enhanced effector function, reduced exhaustion, increased mitochondrial fitness, and a shift toward mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation (FAO), with scRNA-seq supporting PPARα/FAO-associated remodeling, including upregulation of Cpt1a, encoding the FAO enzyme CPT1A, in effector-associated, proliferative, and clonally expanded subsets. Both antitumor efficacy and T-cell metabolic remodeling were reversed by the CPT1 inhibitor etomoxir. By contrast, LDRT impaired tumor-cell mitochondrial fitness, while FFB shifted tumor cells from FAO toward glycolytic reliance and induced only slight apoptosis. Consistently, in vivo data argued against direct LDRT-mediated tumor-cell debulking. The quadruple regimen increased vascular MECA-79 expression, while LDRT enhanced endothelial ICAM-1/VCAM-1 and tumor-cell CXCL9/CXCL10 expression in secondary tumors, consistent with local conditioning favoring T-cell recruitment. These findings highlight FFB as a clinically tractable metabolic modulator and link FFB-enhanced hRT/LDRT/αPD-1-induced systemic antitumor efficacy to metabolic reprogramming of tumor-specific CD8+ TILs and conditioning of the LDRT-treated tumor microenvironment.

papers.abstract_en: Deruxtecan-based antibody-drug conjugates (DXd ADCs) provide substantial clinical benefit across multiple malignancies but are associated with clinically significant interstitial lung disease (ILD), for which the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. To enable mechanistic and translational studies, we established a transgenic rat model expressing human trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 (hTROP2) under the control of the surfactant protein C promoter, driving selective expression in alveolar type II (AT2) cells. Repeated administration of a TROP2-directed DXd ADC with an average drug-to-antibody ratio of 7.9 (TROP2-DXd) reproducibly induced lung injury characterized by alveolar epithelial damage, inflammatory cell infiltration, and fibroblast/myofibroblast proliferation. These pathological changes were accompanied by inflammatory and tissue-remodeling transcriptomic responses, including increased expression of fibrosis-associated genes and decreased expression of AT2-associated genes. These molecular alterations showed partial concordance with molecular programs observed in a cynomolgus monkey ILD model. In hTROP2 transgenic rats, prednisolone markedly attenuated TROP2-DXd-related lung injury and inflammatory and tissue-remodeling transcriptomic responses without altering systemic exposure. Although hTROP2 expression is transgene-driven and does not fully recapitulate physiological expression patterns and distribution in normal human lungs, this model provides a controlled experimental system for evaluating epithelial injury-associated mechanisms. Notably, parallel studies in BALB/c and C57BL/6 mice showed no pulmonary findings despite prolonged high-exposure dosing, suggesting species-dependent susceptibility. Collectively, this transgenic rat model represents a unique rodent ILD model that recapitulates key pathological and molecular features and provides a scalable, experimentally tractable platform for mechanistic and translational evaluation across DXd ADCs.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Less-invasive, lower-risk alternatives to surgical lung biopsy (SLB) have emerged for interstitial lung disease (ILD) diagnosis, such as transbronchial lung cryobiopsy (TBLC) and Envisia Genomic Classifier (EGC), but suffer from limited sampling and simplified binomial classification, respectively. Endobronchial optical coherence tomography (EB-OCT) is a low-risk, large-volume bronchoscopic imaging modality with microscopic resolution, which accurately detects features and patterns for ILD diagnosis as previously validated against SLB. RESEARCH QUESTION: How does EB-OCT contribute to ILD diagnosis and diagnostic confidence at multidisciplinary discussion (MDD) when paired with clinically indicated TBLC and EGC? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: Patients with low-confidence ILD diagnosis clinically referred for both TBLC with EGC were enrolled to undergo concurrent EB-OCT imaging. Each modality was interpreted independently by blinded pathologists. Separate MDD sessions were conducted at two independent sites, including one without prior EB-OCT experience. RESULTS: Fifteen patients were included (9 male; mean age: 70.6 years) with final diagnoses of UIP/IPF (n=5), secondary UIP (n=2), and various non-UIP ILDs (n=8) in agreement at both MDDs. EB-OCT provided diagnostic data that was in agreement with final MDD diagnosis for 100% of subjects (15/15), including in the 40% of subjects (6/15) where TBLC was non-diagnostic. In the subjects where TBLC yielded diagnostic data (60%, 9/15), EB-OCT diagnosis was in agreement. EB-OCT combined with TBLC/EGC increased diagnostic confidence and/or narrowed the differential diagnosis from baseline clinical/radiologic data review in all subjects, with replication across both independent MDDs. INTERPRETATION: In this pilot study, we demonstrate EB-OCT is a safe, large-volume imaging method that detects microscopic features and patterns for ILD diagnosis, which increases diagnostic confidence in the context of MDD and complements TBLC and EGC. Future multicenter studies are needed to further validate these findings.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Adherence to lung cancer screening (LCS) follow-up is essential to achieve mortality benefits from screening. However, population-based studies demonstrate follow-up is <50% in clinical settings. Determinants (barriers and facilitators) of LCS follow-up in community settings are under-studied. RESEARCH QUESTION: What are determinants of LCS follow-up in community settings? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: This qualitative multi-case study informed a pre-post intervention trial, testing pragmatic interventions to address LCS follow-up in community settings. We conducted rapid ethnographic assessments (REA) through virtual and in person site visits of LCS delivery in three community-based healthcare systems in Washington state. Additionally at the two future intervention sites, we conducted provider and patient interviews. Interview transcripts were analyzed using Rapid Group Analysis Process. All data were triangulated according to Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research and National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities Research Framework domains. RESULTS: Twenty-eight organizational leaders, providers, and staff participated in REA. Thirty-one patients and 15 providers from the future intervention sites participated in interviews. Determinants of LCS follow-up in the intervention domain included role of primary care, LCS complexity and care process standardization. In the inner setting domain (organization and clinic), screening prioritization, EHR use, radiology support, and context of wellness visits affected LCS. The main theme in the outer setting domain was the influence of social determinants of health on LCS. In the individuals domain, shared beliefs in LCS and LCS education and information sharing were key. In the process implementation domain, clinical champions and use of data and metrics were crucial. INTERPRETATION: Integrated findings suggest determinants related to LCS complexity, care fragmentation, socioeconomic status and language, and limitations of PCPs could be overcome through more centralized approaches. However, increased use of EHR tools, increased education and standardizing LCS performance metrics may enable follow-up in decentralized settings. CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: NCT06324110.

papers.abstract_en: PURPOSE: To evaluate long-term outcomes and determine whether longitudinal plasma profiling provides biological insight into disease progression after proton hypofractionated ablative radiation therapy (HART) for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC). PATIENTS AND METHODS: In this single-arm, multi-institutional phase II trial, 92 patients with localized unresectable HCC or ICC with Child-Pugh class A/B liver function received HART (up to 67.5 GyE in 15 fractions). Overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Plasma samples were collected at baseline, days 1, 8, 15, and 1-month after treatment for exploratory correlative analyses. RESULTS: Among evaluable patients (44 HCC, 39 ICC), median OS was 29.2 months (HCC) and 20.8 months (ICC), with 5-year OS rates of 25.9% and 12.3%, respectively. Median PFS was 13.8 months (HCC) and 8.4 months (ICC). In-field local failure occurred in 2 HCC (4.5%) and 7 ICC (17.9%) patients, whereas out-of-field intrahepatic/distant progression remained the predominant pattern of failure. No grade >3 treatment-related toxicities were observed. Exploratory plasma profiling identified distinct biological signatures associated with progression: HCC was characterized by markers of hypoxia, inflammation, vascular remodeling, stromal activation, and hepatic regeneration, whereas associations in ICC predominantly involved signatures of hypoxia and vascular remodeling. CONCLUSIONS: HART provides durable long-term in-field local control with minimal toxicity, but disease progression remains predominantly out-of-field intrahepatic/distant. Exploratory correlative analyses suggest that biological signatures reflecting vascular remodeling, hypoxia, inflammation, stromal activation, and hepatic reserve are associated with progression despite successful local therapy, informing future translational studies and combination strategies.

papers.abstract_en: Whether a decline in taurine drives aging is debated, and despite high millimolar intracellular concentrations, its function as a potential guardian of cytosolic homeostasis is unclear. Here, we show that aging increases circulating taurine concentrations in humans and mice. Further elevating taurine in aged mice enhances health span, engaging anti-inflammatory pathways previously linked to youthfulness, and reduces mortality from sepsis and inflammasome-mediated inflammation, suggesting an enantiostatic response. Mechanistically, diverse NLRP3-specific "danger signals" induce taurine efflux from macrophages as a proximal step to activate the inflammasome and the resultant pyroptosis. Taurine restoration in macrophages prevents NLRP3-induced trans-Golgi network disassembly, thereby suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation. Conversely, lowering taurine biosynthesis combined with reduced bioavailability in macrophages exacerbated inflammasome activation. In humans, sustained caloric restriction elevates adipose tissue taurine and is accompanied by lower inflammation. Together, we identify taurine as an immunometabolic rheostat that links danger sensing to NLRP3 inflammasome activation, suggesting taurine-based strategies to alleviate inflammaging and inflammasomopathies.

papers.abstract_en: Metabolites are increasingly recognized as circulating molecules that regulate physiology, yet the mechanisms that couple local intracellular production to organism-wide action remain poorly defined. Using the anorexigenic metabolite N-lactoyl-phenylalanine (Lac-Phe) as a model system, we identify the orphan transporter MCT6/SLC16A5 as a physiologic intestinal Lac-Phe exporter. This mechanism controls the extent to which intracellularly synthesized Lac-Phe acquires systemic activity. MCT6 transports Lac-Phe in vitro, mediates Lac-Phe efflux in cells, and is required for maintaining normal circulating Lac-Phe levels in vivo, particularly following metformin treatment or high-intensity exercise. High-fat-diet-fed mice with global or intestinal epithelial-specific deletion of MCT6 exhibit resistance to metformin-associated weight loss. Bypassing the transport defect with exogenous Lac-Phe normalizes the body weight phenotype of MCT6-knockout (KO) mice. These data connect MCT6 to Lac-Phe and gut glycolytic flux and underscore the importance of transporter-mediated release in the conversion of an intracellular metabolic state into a circulating metabolite effector.

papers.abstract_en: Physical activity promotes health primarily by decelerating the aging process. Bone is one of the tissues capable of sensing mechanical force and can adapt to different physical demands. However, its role in whole-body aging is unknown. We found that reduced mechano-sensing in osteocytes, caused by deletion of the mechanosensory channel, Piezo1, accelerated whole-body aging in mice. Dynamic tibial axial loading (DTAL) in mice at 20-24 months of age extended both healthspan and lifespan (9.4%/79.5 days). Furthermore, DTAL reversed bone marrow immunosenescence and induced anti-aging and protective factors while downregulating pro-aging and pro-inflammatory factors. We also identified pigment epithelium-derived factor (PEDF) as a novel mechano-responsive anti-aging factor that is highly associated with healthy aging in humans. Thus, our findings highlighted an essential role for bone mechano-sensing in whole-body aging. This could potentially be manipulated to prevent aging, extend health, and aid those unable to exercise or with decreased mobility.

papers.abstract_en: Radiotherapy is often limited by tumor-intrinsic DNA repair and an immunosuppressive microenvironment, both of which are reinforced by lactate accumulation. Here, we develop a CXCR4-engineered enucleated hepatocyte cytoplast platform decorated with Au-Pt Janus nanorobots (AP/LCCXCR4) to deplete intratumoral lactate and amplify radiation-induced oxidative stress. The hepatocyte cytoplasts home to tumors and consume lactate through gluconeogenesis, reducing repair-associated protein lactylation and impairing MRE11-RAD50-NBS1 (MRN) co-fractionation and chromatin recruitment, thereby impairing double-strand break repair. In parallel, the Au-Pt nanorobots enhance reactive oxygen species generation under acidic tumor conditions, increasing radiation damage. In radioresistant colorectal cancer models and a metastatic cervical cancer model, AP/LCCXCR4 combined with radiotherapy sustains DNA damage, promotes immunogenic cell death, reduces immunosuppressive myeloid and regulatory T (Treg) cell populations, enhances dendritic cell maturation and CD8+ T cell activation, and improves tumor control and survival.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: Emergency departments face increasing overcrowding, resulting in diagnostic delays, higher mortality, and rising healthcare costs. Early risk stratification is essential to optimise clinical decision-making. Although medical imaging plays a central role in initial assessment, workload pressures and operational constraints have driven the development of artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support triage and prioritisation in emergency radiology. OBJECTIVE: To map and synthesise evidence on the applications, performance, and limitations of AI in emergency radiology for early risk stratification in acute care. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines and Joanna Briggs Institute recommendations. The protocol was developed a priori and registered in the Open Science Framework. A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science identified studies published between 2015 and 2025 that evaluated AI applications in medical imaging in acute care settings. Evidence was synthesised using conceptual mapping and thematic analysis. RESULTS: Seventy-one studies were included. Computed tomography was the most frequently evaluated modality, followed by radiography and ultrasound. Major domains included neurovascular disease, acute cardiopulmonary conditions, trauma, COVID-19, and acute aortic syndromes. Studies reported high diagnostic performance and potential workflow benefits; however, evidence was predominantly retrospective and internally validated, with limited prospective evaluation, external validation, or evidence of improved patient-level outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: AI applications in emergency radiology show promising diagnostic and workflow-support capabilities. However, current evidence largely reflects early-stage development, with limited prospective validation, scarce real-world impact assessment, and insufficient evaluation of clinically meaningful outcomes. KEY POINTS: Question How clinically mature are AI applications designed to support early risk stratification and prioritisation in time-sensitive emergency radiology workflows? Findings Most studies report high diagnostic performance in time-sensitive conditions, yet evidence remains predominantly retrospective with limited external validation or prospective real-world implementation. Clinical relevance AI may support earlier identification and prioritisation of critical imaging findings, but routine adoption requires prospective external validation and evidence of meaningful effects on clinical decisions and patient outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: The presence of extra-pancreatic nerve plexus invasion (EPNI) in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is known to correlate with aggressive disease, however, it is unknown whether specific pathways or morphologies carry different prognostic implications. This study evaluates whether distinct CT-defined patterns of EPNI predict mortality in PDAC. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective, single-center study included 89 patients with pathologically confirmed PDAC who underwent preoperative pancreatic protocol multidetector CT (MDCT) followed by surgical resection. Patients were identified from an institutional database and required available preoperative CT and histopathology. Two blinded, experienced radiologists reviewed MDCT images to assess EPNI, which was categorized by anatomic pathway and morphologic pattern. Overall survival was compared between EPNI-positive and EPNI-negative groups and among EPNI subtypes using log-rank testing, with stratification by tumor stage. Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, and surgical margin were performed. RESULTS: A total of 89 patients (M/F: 54/35), median age: 66 years (IQR, 60-70 years), were evaluated. CT evidence of EPNI was present in 65 patients (73%) and was associated with decreased overall survival (p < 0.001). This association remained significant in Stage I tumors (p < 0.001). PPC2 pathway involvement (p < 0.001) and mass-with-stranding morphology (p < 0.001) were each associated with reduced overall survival. PPC2 (p = 0.003) and mass-with-stranding (p < 0.001) remained significant in stage I tumors. CONCLUSION: Preoperative CT detection of EPNI, especially PPC2 pathway involvement and mass-with-stranding morphology, identifies high-risk PDAC patients. KEY POINTS: Question Extra pancreatic nerve plexus invasion in pancreatic adenocarcinoma is associated with aggressive disease, but the prognostic significance of specific pathways or morphologies remains unknown. Findings Plexus pancreaticus capitalis 2 involvement and mass-with-stranding morphology in EPNI of pancreatic adenocarcinoma are associated with decreased overall survival. Clinical relevance Identifying high-risk EPNI features on CT may facilitate early prognostic stratification and inform surgical and neoadjuvant treatment planning in pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Some evidence reported that rivaroxaban use is associated with a higher risk of clinically relevant bleeding (CRB) than apixaban during the first months of treatment of venous thromboembolism (VTE). We aimed to determine whether the risk of CRB is higher with rivaroxaban than apixaban during extended treatment, either at full or reduced dose. METHODS: The RENOVE open-label randomised controlled trial compared full-dose versus reduced-dose of apixaban or rivaroxaban in patients who had completed at least 6 months of full-dose treatment for VTE and required extended anticoagulation. Drug choice was not randomised. In this post-analysis, the primary outcome was centrally-adjudicated CRB events. Treatment effects were estimated using crude hazard ratio (HR), adjusted HR, and an inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW). RESULTS: Among 2768 enrolled patients, 1513 received rivaroxaban (755 full-dose, 758 reduced-dose) and 1255 apixaban (630 full-dose, 625 reduced-dose). Median age was 62.6 versus 66.5 years and proportion of female was 32.1% versus 38.7%, respectively. Median follow-up was 37 months. The 5-year cumulative incidence of CRB was 11.7% with rivaroxaban and 13.7% with apixaban (adjusted-HR 0.90 [95%CI 0.70-1.17], HRIPTW 0.92 [0.70-1.21]). The incidence of major bleeding, recurrent VTE, composite outcome, arterial thromboembolic events, and all-cause death were similar. Serious adverse event not related to VTE and CRB was 7.7% and 10.8%, respectively (adjusted-HR 0.74 [95% CI 0.57-0.97], HRIPTW 0.76 [0.55-1.04]). CONCLUSIONS: During extended anticoagulation, no difference in clinically relevant bleeding or recurrent VTE was observed between rivaroxaban and apixaban, although that non-randomised treatment allocation possibly influenced outcomes.
