papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Adenocarcinoma (AC) is the leading histopathological type of lung cancer (LC), curative surgery being the cornerstone for the best survival results. However, even in the patients who had curative surgery, the survival outcomes differ. Spread through air spaces (STAS), recognized as a histopathological feature in the 2015 World Health Organization (WHO) Classification, causes poor survival outcomes in lung AC. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic impact of STAS on recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) in surgically resected T1-2N0 lung AC, with particular attention to its interaction with tumor size. METHODS: This single center retrospective study evaluates the effect of STAS on RFS and OS in 296 surgically resected T1-2N0 lung AC patients. For further analysis, patients were divided into four subgroups combining their STAS status and tumor size. RESULTS: STAS presence rate was 37.5%, which was associated with aggressive tumor characteristics, such as non-lepidic predominant subtypes, higher pathological T stage (pT), visceral pleura invasion (VPI), and lymphovascular invasion (LVI). OS and RFS were significantly worse in the STAS-Present (STAS-P) group (p = 0.030). Subgroup analysis revealed that STAS-P tumors > 2 cm had the worst outcomes, as expected. Notably, on univariate analysis STAS presence appeared most prognostically decisive in tumors ≤ 2 cm, in which there was no significant difference in survival between STAS-P tumors ≤ 2 cm and STAS-Absent (STAS-A) tumors > 2 cm. CONCLUSIONS: STAS was a significant prognostic factor on univariate analysis but did not retain independent significance after multivariable adjustment. In an exploratory subgroup analysis, STAS-P tumors ≤ 2 cm carried survival outcomes comparable to STAS-A tumors > 2 cm, suggesting STAS may attenuate the prognostic advantage of smaller tumor size. This hypothesis-generating finding warrants prospective validation before informing surgical management.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: This study evaluated the incidence and clinical impact of radiation pneumonitis (RP) in patients with unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) treated with durvalumab following concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT), with a particular focus on durvalumab interruption, re-administration, and overall survival (OS). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included patients treated at our institution between April 2018 and June 2024. Durvalumab was administered for up to one year or until discontinuation due to adverse events or disease progression. RP was graded according to CTCAE version 5.0. Associations between grade ≥ 2 RP and clinical or treatment-related factors were assessed using univariate and multivariate analyses. Survival outcomes were analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method and Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: Among 101 patients, 48 (47.5%) developed grade ≥ 2 RP (grade 2: 41.6%; grade 3: 4.0%; grade 4: 2.0%). Lung V20 > 30% was independently associated with grade ≥ 2 RP. Durvalumab interruption occurred in a subset of patients with grade 2 RP; among these patients, 25 (59.5%) were able to undergo durvalumab re-administration, with RP recurrence observed in only one patient after re-administration. The 2-year and 3-year OS rates were 75.1% and 60.9%, respectively. Completion of durvalumab was the strongest independent predictor of OS (hazard ratio 0.14; P = 0.00007), whereas grade ≥ 2 RP itself was not significantly associated with OS. CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort, completion of durvalumab consolidation after CCRT was strongly associated with improved OS in patients with stage III NSCLC. Although grade ≥ 2 RP was a frequent complication, temporary interruption and re-administration were feasible in selected patients. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the retrospective design and potential residual confounding.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The Naples Prognostic Score (NPS) has demonstrated prognostic value across malignancies; however, its applicability to oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC) remains uncertain. We aimed to develop a disease-specific immunonutritional model for prognostic stratification in surgically treated OCSCC, informed by the NPS framework. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 351 patients undergoing curative surgery for OCSCC (2009-2018). Survival-optimized cutoffs for albumin, total cholesterol, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, and lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio were determined using X-tile and integrated into a composite score (OCSCC-specific Naples Prognostic Score, OCNPS) to classify patients into three risk groups (Groups 0-2). Associations with overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) were evaluated using Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: The proposed model stratified patients into distinct risk groups and was associated with adverse pathological features. Five-year OS rates were 81.2%, 63.4%, and 10.4% across Groups 0-2, whereas the original NPS did not discriminate between low- and intermediate-risk patients. In multivariable analyses, higher OCNPS categories independently predicted worse OS and DFS (Group 1: HR 1.63 and 1.42; Group 2: HR 6.46 and 6.66). A nomogram incorporating OCNPS improved prognostic discrimination compared with TNM staging (C-index 0.769 vs. 0.652) with good calibration. CONCLUSIONS: The OCNPS enables preoperative identification of patients with OCSCC at higher risk of adverse postoperative outcomes and provides clinically applicable prognostic information beyond conventional staging, supporting its potential role in OCSCC management.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Emerging evidence links neuronal-like phenotypic transition to glioblastoma (GB) recurrence and therapy resistance, yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. We hypothesized that dysregulated alternative splicing leads to a neuronal-like state and chemoresistance at tumor recurrence. METHODS: We reanalysed longitudinal bulk RNA-seq data from paired primary and recurrent GBs to quantify dynamic alternative splicing during tumor evolution. By integrating single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, we characterized shifts in cellular composition and spatial interactions linked to these splicing changes. We then prioritized splicing regulators and validated their effects on tumor cells using in vitro cell lines and co-culture assays. RESULTS: A subset of recurrent GBs exhibits neuronal programs and chemoresistance during tumor evolution, accompanied by pronounced differential splicing patterns. Single-cell analyses link these splicing changes to the co-enrichment of neurons and a neuronal-like tumor subpopulation at recurrence. Spatial transcriptomics further indicates close synaptic interactions between this tumor state and adjacent neurons in tumor-infiltrative regions. Through integrative computational ranking and experimental validation, we find that the neuron-specific splicing factor RBFOX3 promotes the neuronal-like GB tumor state by dysregulating splicing. In tumor-neuron co-culture systems, RBFOX3 overexpression is linked to the upregulation of presynaptic markers. CONCLUSIONS: Dysregulated alternative splicing mediated by RBFOX3 is associated with a neuronal-like tumor state and might contribute to chemoresistance at GB relapse, highlighting the potential role of splicing regulation in GB evolution.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a disruptive technology in medicine, with rapidly developing implications for education, diagnosis, image enhancement and assessment, prognosis, and treatment. The literature on AI-assisted ultrasound is still developing. Therefore, we aimed to investigate how AI is employed in ultrasound for trauma and how AI-assisted ultrasound could be deployed in clinical practice. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The review was conducted according to JBI's scoping review methodology. An appropriate search strategy was initially formulated for PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science (WoS), and Google Scholar (backward and forward citation tracking). The concepts of "artificial intelligence", "ultrasound", and "trauma" were searched across these databases using their respective Medical Subject Headings (MeSH). The core concepts were AI applications integrated with ultrasound in trauma. In this context, studies focusing on the following categories relating to the use of AI-assisted ultrasound in the field of trauma have been included in the review: (1) diagnostic accuracy, (2) differential diagnosis and confirmation of diagnosis, (3) quality and standardization, (4) operator support, and (5) training and modelling. Data extraction and analysis were performed using Microsoft Excel and were verified. RESULTS: Twenty-one studies were included. Targeted AI tasks primarily comprised diagnostic abnormality detection and segmentation/localization. Predominantly focused assessment with sonography for trauma (FAST), thoracic trauma evaluation, and extremity trauma. Although high apparent diagnostic accuracy was reported across development-stage retrospective cohorts, independent external validation was executed in only one study, with the remainder bounded by single-center data or synthetic phantoms. Crucially, none of the studies assessed subsequent patient outcomes such as mortality, time to intervention, or resource utilization. CONCLUSION: This scoping review confirms that while deep learning frameworks show promising retrospective diagnostic performance and image-quality automation, their translation into acute trauma care faces critical technical and clinical bottlenecks. Key current limitations include restricted model interpretability, missing regulatory pathways, a lack of clinician trust, inherent decision-making biases, poor algorithmic transparency, and the lack of patient-outcome tracking. To address these barriers, future studies should be designed with stronger methodological rigor, including prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled, and externally validated approaches. TRIAL REGISTRATION: No clinical trial number is available.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: To quantify fetal choroid plexus (CP) morphological changes across ventriculomegaly (VM) grades using routine 1.5-T MRI and assess their association with lateral ventricle dilatation. METHODS: In this retrospective study, 135 singleton fetuses (24-37 weeks' gestation) were categorized by atrial width (AW): normal, mild VM, moderate VM, severe VM). On coronal T2-weighted images, CP length, width, perimeter, and area were measured. The two-dimensional (2D) CP ratio (CPR-2D) and CP-to-ventricle width ratio were calculated. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) adjusted for gestational age and fetal biometrics, and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) were used for analysis. RESULTS: Absolute CP measurements exhibited non-linear, stage-specific alterations: CP length and perimeter increased in mild VM, decreased in moderate VM, and increased again in severe VM. CP width progressively decreased until moderate VM before rebounding in severe cases. Conversely, ratio-based indices demonstrated a consistent, monotonic linear decrease as VM severity increased, which remained significant after adjusting for covariates (p < 0.05). While morphological asymmetry existed, the downward trend of ratios remained consistent for both ventricles. CONCLUSIONS: The fetal CP undergoes a non-linear change process during the expansion of the lateral ventricle. However, based on ratio-based indicators, especially CPR-2D, stable and reproducible imaging biomarkers can be provided.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: Accurate identification of acute ischemic infarcts on diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (DWI) is a critical prerequisite for reliable lesion quantification and effective clinical decision support in the management of cerebrovascular events. METHODS: This study presents EPRA U-Net (Efficient Pyramid Residual Attention U-Net), a task-specific integrated architecture for efficient and accurate infarct segmentation of DWI images. In the proposed architecture, an EfficientNet-based encoder was used as a hierarchical feature extractor with a minimized parameterization. In addition, a Residual-Recurrent (R2) block (recurrent unrolling step t = 2, following the original formulation) and Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) were integrated to enhance the performance of spatial dependency modeling. Additionally, a dual attention mechanism was incorporated to highlight lesion-related activations while concurrently enabling the suppression of extraneous background responses. To prioritize lesion detection consistent with clinical imperative, a Tversky loss function (α = 0.4, β = 0.6) was adopted, thereby emphasizing the sensitivity of detection over its specificity during the optimization process. RESULTS: Experimental evaluations were conducted utilizing an in-house dataset comprising 167 patients with 4,895 DWI slices; subsequently, the performance of the proposed EPRA U-Net was assessed in comparison with state-of-the-art models, specifically UNet++, DeepLabV3+, and TransUNet. The experimental results suggest that EPRA U-Net attained superior performance, evidenced by a pixel-aggregated Dice of 0.8984, a per-sample Dice of 0.9469, an IoU of 0.8155, a Recall of 0.8887, a Lesion F1 of 0.9378, and an HD95 of 11.62 px (median: 2.00 px). Furthermore, a clear reduction in the rate of missed lesions, specifically by 16%, 25%, and 29%, was observed when compared with UNet++, DeepLabV3+, and TransUNet, respectively. Additionally, a comprehensive ablation study was systematically conducted. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that the proposed architecture affords a more robust and accurate infarct segmentation, consequently facilitating a more reliable estimation of treatment eligibility.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to evaluate changes in clinical, functional, and inflammatory parameters in patients with severe eosinophilic asthma receiving benralizumab treatment, to determine clinical remission rates, and to explore factors associated with clinical remission. METHODS: This retrospective single-center real-world study included 33 patients with severe eosinophilic asthma treated with benralizumab at a tertiary referral center. Demographic characteristics, clinical findings, pulmonary function test results, peripheral blood eosinophil counts, and treatment responses were obtained from medical records. Baseline findings were compared with those obtained after at least 12 months of treatment. Clinical remission was defined as the absence of exacerbations, no maintenance oral corticosteroid use, well-controlled asthma, and stable or improved lung function. Factors associated with clinical remission were evaluated using multivariable Firth's penalized logistic regression. RESULTS: The mean age of the 33 included patients was 54.6 ± 13.8 years, and 60.6% were female. After 12 months of treatment, clinical remission was achieved in 75.8% (25/33) of patients. The proportion of patients with well-controlled asthma increased to 90.9%, while maintenance oral corticosteroid use decreased from 48.5% to 24.2% (p = 0.008). The median annual exacerbation rate decreased from 2 to 0 (p < 0.001). Mean FEV₁ increased from 1514 mL to 2188 mL (+ 674 mL; p < 0.001), and FEV₁ (% predicted) improved from 54.9% to 76.8% (p < 0.001). Peripheral blood eosinophil counts decreased from a median of 720 cells/µL to 0 cells/µL (p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, lower baseline exacerbation frequency (OR 0.52, 95% CI 0.27-0.91; p = 0.021) and higher baseline FEV₁ (per 100 mL increase; OR 1.27, 95% CI 1.01-1.59; p = 0.037) were associated with clinical remission. CONCLUSIONS: Benralizumab was associated with high clinical remission rates, substantial reductions in exacerbations, and significant improvements in lung function in patients with severe eosinophilic asthma. Given the limited sample size, the findings from the exploratory multivariable analysis should be interpreted with caution and require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Vaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (vNOTES) is an important technique in minimally invasive gynecology. However, conventional vNOTES relies on CO₂ pneumoperitoneum, which may lead to complications such as postoperative pain and hypercapnia. Gasless vNOTES has been proposed as an alternative, but existing techniques often require additional abdominal wall lifting devices that increase procedural complexity and trauma. This study aimed to assess the feasibility and safety of gasless vaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (vNOTES) without abdominal wall retractors in benign adnexal surgery. METHODS: This retrospective case series included patients who underwent benign adnexal surgery with gasless vNOTES between September 2024 and August 2025 at the International Peace Maternity and Child Health Hospital in Shanghai. Data were collected on baseline characteristics and surgical outcomes were collected, including history of abdominal surgery, pathological types of adnexal masses, surgical procedures, operative time, volume of intraoperative blood loss, complications, postoperative pain scores using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), time to first flatus, and length of postoperative hospital stay. RESULTS: A total of 373 patients who underwent vNOTES for benign adnexal disease were included in the study. Overall, 370 (99.2%) patients successfully underwent gasless vNOTES, while one case required conversion to gas‑based vNOTES and two cases required conversion to transumbilical laparoendoscopic single-site surgery (TU-LESS) due to pelvic adhesions (conversion rate, 0.8%). In five cases (1.4%), in which the ovarian cyst was located anterior to the uterus and difficult to expose, brief pneumoperitoneum (< 5 min) was applied to retract the mass posterior to the uterus, after which gasless vNOTES was resumed following desufflation. Surgical procedures included ovarian cystectomy (314 cases, 84.9%), surgery for ectopic pregnancies (11 ruptured and 28 unruptured cases, 10.5%), and adnexectomy (10 cases, 2.7%). The mean operative time was 54.41 ± 25.94 min, and mean intraoperative blood loss was 25.63 ± 14.31 mL. No intraoperative complications, such as visceral injury or major hemorrhage, occurred. The median postoperative VAS pain scores were 1.0 (0, 2.0) at 6 h and 0 (0, 1.0) at 12 h. The mean time to first flatus was 7.12 ± 4.51 h, and the mean postoperative hospital stay was 22.09 ± 10.36 h. The postoperative infection rate was 1.9%, and all cases were managed successfully using antibiotics. CONCLUSIONS: Gasless vNOTES is a safe and feasible technique for benign adnexal surgery. In this series, 99.2% of procedures were completed without conversion. The findings suggest that this approach is technically straightforward and associated with short operative time, low postoperative pain, and rapid recovery. papers.abstract_en: Successful immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) treatment of cancer requires adequate infiltration of cytotoxic CD8+T lymphocytes (CTLs) in tumors. Previous studies have identified the compound naringin, which increases CTL infiltration and rescues ICI efficacy in CTL-lacking tumors, and cancer CTL priming has been shown to rely on antigen cross-presentation (XPT). Therefore, the present study aimed to examine the effect of naringin on XPT by various human and murine antigen-presenting cells (APCs). The results indicated that naringin increases XPT by XPT-competent APCs, including murine bone marrow (BM) dendritic cells, peritoneal macrophages (MΦs), and human monocyte-derived dendritic cells (HMDCs). However, XPT was not observed with BM- or human monocyte-derived MΦs with or without naringin. Naringin reduced the activity of lysosomes, suppressing the degradation of internalized antigens, thereby increasing antigen cytosolic escape and MHC class I molecule-presenting antigens. In addition, human lymph node (LN) sinus MΦs were transcriptomically more similar to XPT-competent HMDCs than other LN MΦ groups. Taken together, these data suggest that naringin promotes XPT by XPT-competent APCs, which may explain why naringin was found to promote cancer immunity in our previous studies. This finding highlights the potential for developing cancer immunotherapies that induce XPT, offering a promising strategy to enhance antitumor immune responses.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Sleep disturbances are prevalent among cancer patients and can often persist or worsen during hospital stays. However, nurses' practices to promote oncology patients' sleep during hospitalization and factors affecting their sleep promotion practices are not well understood. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine nurses' behaviors to promote oncology patients' sleep during hospitalization and associated factors. METHODS: An exploratory descriptive correlational research design was used. Bedside registered nurses in inpatient oncology settings were invited to complete an online survey consisting of a demographic questionnaire, self-reported questionnaires, and open-ended questions. Bivariate tests and multivariable linear regression were conducted to identify relationships between study variables. Qualitative and quantitative content analysis was used to analyze the qualitative data. RESULTS: A total of 201 nurse participants were included. Nurses' sleep knowledge significantly predicts their sleep promotion behaviors, attitudes, and perceived control to improve inpatients' sleep (P < .05). Nurses' sleep hygiene practices also affect their perceived control over enhancing patients' sleep (P < .05). Qualitative findings reflected positive nurses' attitudes to improving patients' sleep. However, various barriers emerged, and recommendations were provided to facilitate enhancing patients' sleep in hospitals. CONCLUSION: Nurses have positive attitudes toward improving oncology patients' sleep. However, increasing their sleep knowledge and sleep hygiene is important for effective practice. IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: To enhance nurses' sleep knowledge, nurse educators can incorporate sleep related topics, including sleep hygiene practices, into nursing education. Furthermore, it is important for nurse leaders to focus on adopting strategies that empower nurses to effectively implement sleep promotion interventions.

papers.abstract_en: Smoking is associated with structural and functional alterations in the lungs, some of which may be reflected in quantitative imaging features. Radiomics enables the extraction of high-dimensional image-derived descriptors and may provide information beyond routinely available clinical variables. We investigated whether bilateral lung radiomics, both independently and integrated with clinical variables, could classify patient-level smoking status. An exploratory secondary analysis was also performed to assess whether radiomic and clinical feature representations could discriminate smoking exposure intensity among smokers. A total of 506 patients were included, comprising 253 smokers and 253 nonsmokers. Right and left lung radiomic features were extracted separately from visually normal-appearing lung parenchyma on thoracic CT images. Multiple feature representations were evaluated, including right lung radiomics, left lung radiomics, concatenated right-left radiomics, summary/asymmetry radiomics, clinical variables alone, and radiomics combined with clinical variables. Clinical variables included age, sex, height, weight, and body mass index. Pack-years were excluded from the binary smoking status classification models to avoid target-related information leakage. For each binary classification task, a balanced internal hold-out set containing 25 smokers and 25 nonsmokers was reserved, while the remaining patients were evaluated using stratified tenfold cross-validation. Four feature selection or dimensionality reduction strategies and five classifier families were assessed, resulting in 435 model configurations across the main cohort and sex-specific subgroup analyses. Threshold selection was performed using the Youden index derived from cross-validated out-of-fold predictions. For the exploratory smoking exposure analysis, 253 smokers with available pack-year information were categorized into < 10, 10-20, and > 20 pack-year groups and evaluated using pooled stratified tenfold cross-validation. The best-performing radiomics-based configurations showed higher discrimination than the clinical-only configuration. The clinical-only random forest model achieved a cross-validation ROC-AUC of 0.673 and a hold-out ROC-AUC of 0.610. Among radiomics-only configurations, concatenated bilateral radiomics achieved a cross-validation ROC-AUC of 0.734 and a hold-out ROC-AUC of 0.712. The strongest hold-out discrimination was obtained using concatenated bilateral radiomics combined with clinical variables, ReliefF feature selection, and stacking classification, achieving a hold-out ROC-AUC of 0.803, balanced accuracy of 0.700, sensitivity of 0.720, and specificity of 0.680. Feature selection stability analysis showed that the final concatenated bilateral radiomics + clinical configuration retained five clinical variables and 15 radiomic features, several of which were repeatedly selected across cross-validation folds. Sex-specific subgroup analyses showed moderate but variable performance. In the exploratory three-class smoking exposure analysis, integrating left lung radiomics with clinical variables yielded the most balanced class-wise performance, achieving the highest balanced accuracy (0.658) and the highest sensitivity for the intermediate 10-20 pack-year group (0.417), although the clinical-only model achieved the highest macro-AUC. Bilateral lung radiomics showed potential for patient-level smoking status classification, particularly when combined with clinical variables. These findings suggest that quantitative imaging features could provide complementary information beyond routinely available patient-level variables. The exploratory smoking exposure analysis further suggested that radiomics + clinical configurations may contain limited information related to smoking exposure intensity, although intermediate exposure remained challenging to discriminate. However, the moderate performance, subgroup variability, and lack of external validation indicate that this approach should be considered investigational until confirmed in larger independent cohorts.

papers.abstract_en: Uniportal robotic-assisted thoracic surgery (uRATS) seeks to combine the dexterity of robotic platforms with reduced access trauma, yet its comparative value over multiportal RATS (mRATS) remains uncertain. We systematically evaluated perioperative recovery and surgical quality after anatomical pulmonary resection. PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through 2026. Comparative studies of uniportal/single-port versus multiportal robotic anatomical lung resection were included. Random-effects meta-analyses pooled risk ratios (RRs) and mean differences (MDs). Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I V2 and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Nine non-randomised studies involving 813 patients were included, with seven studies rated at critical risk of bias. Postoperative complications occurred in 16.0% of uniportal and 30.2% of multiportal patients, with no statistically significant pooled difference (RR 0.49, 95% CI 0.22-1.06; p = 0.069; I²=66%). No significant differences were identified in major complications, conversion, mortality, operative time, blood loss, chest-tube duration, length of stay, or lymph-node yield, or R0 resection. Uniportal surgery was associated with shorter console time (MD - 23.5 min, 95% CI - 35.6 to - 11.4) and lower postoperative day-1 pain (MD - 0.6 points, 95% CI - 0.9 to - 0.3). The 0.5- point pain difference was below commonly used thresholds for clinical importance and lost statistical significance when digitised values were excluded (p = 0.092). Available observational evidence does not demonstrate a clear difference in perioperative safety or surgical quality between uniportal/single-port and multiportal robotic-assisted thoracic surgery. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested differences in length of stay and operative time by comparator port count, potentially reflecting confounding by operative era and experience. A possible reduction in console time and early postoperative pain was observed, but these findings were based on very-low-certainty evidence and were sensitive to individual studies.

papers.abstract_en: Occult lymph node metastasis (OLM) remains a major clinical challenge in patients with lung cancer despite comprehensive preoperative staging efforts. Although several predictors of OLM, including tumor diameter, metabolic activity, molecular characteristics, and radiomics, have been extensively investigated, the predictive role of tumor volume remains poorly defined. This study aimed to evaluate whether tumor volume, quantified semi-automatically using artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted Synapse 3D software, could predict OLM in patients with clinically early-stage lung cancer. Patients who underwent surgical resection for clinically staged cT1b-cN0M0 lung cancer between 2018 and 2024 were included. Tumor volume was quantified using Synapse 3D software. Associations between tumor volume and OLM were assessed using univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses. Because tumor diameter and tumor volume may introduce multicollinearity in multivariable models, separate receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were generated, and the corresponding areas under the curve (AUCs) were compared using the DeLong test. A total of 248 patients were included, of whom 59 (23.8%) were female. The mean age was 65.4 years. OLM were identified in 10.8%, 4.8%, and 2.0% of patients at the N1, N2a, and N2b nodal stations, respectively. Multivariable logistic regression identified younger age (p = 0.004), greater tumor volume (p = 0.01), and histopathological subtypes other than adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma as independent predictors of OLM. Tumor diameter, extent of resection, surgical approach, and PET-CT metabolic activity were not significantly associated with OLM. ROC analysis demonstrated that tumor volume had significantly greater discriminatory ability for predicting OLM than tumor diameter (AUC: 69% vs. 58%; DeLong test, p = 0.004). AI-assisted tumor volumetry is an independent predictor of occult lymph node metastasis in patients with clinically early-stage lung cancer.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Postoperative empyema with persistent air leak remains a challenging complication after pulmonary resection. Fenestration may be required in refractory cases but is highly invasive, particularly in high-risk patients. We report two patients successfully treated with prolonged open drainage using a large-sized cut tube without fenestration and propose clinical criteria for selecting suitable candidates. CASE PRESENTATION: A 72-year-old man with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis developed Aspergillus empyema with persistent air leak after bullectomy for pneumothorax, and a 71-year-old man developed empyema with persistent air leak after left lower lobectomy and lingulectomy with bronchoplasty for lung cancer. Both were initially treated with closed chest drainage and antimicrobial therapy. On days 23 and 32, respectively, after infection was controlled, drainage volume decreased to < 50 mL/day, the empyema cavity became localized, and residual lung expansion remained stable despite persistent air leakage, the drainage tubes were cut and shortened to convert them to open drainage. CT confirmed that both cavities were anatomically separated from the pulmonary artery and other major hilar vessels. Both patients were subsequently managed as outpatients, and the empyema cavities gradually became obliterated by granulation tissue, allowing tube removal without fenestration. No recurrence occurred during 2 and 4 years of follow-up, respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged open drainage with a large-sized cut tube may provide a less invasive alternative to fenestration in selected patients with postoperative empyema and persistent air leak. Suitable candidates may be characterized by controlled infection, low drainage volume, a localized empyema cavity, stable residual lung expansion, and anatomical separation from major hilar vessels.

papers.abstract_en: BAP1 and HMGB1 alterations are implicated in the pathogenesis of mesothelioma, an aggressive cancer of the membranes covering the thoracic and abdominal cavities. Genetic inactivating mutations of BAP1 cause cancer in ~100% of carriers. The mechanism/s that regulate BAP1 expression were unknown. We discovered that HMGB1 directly modulates BAP1 expression. Studying our Hmgb1 knock-out mouse mesothelioma models, primary fibroblasts obtained from carriers of pathogenic heterozygous germline BAP1 mutations, and mesothelioma cell lines, we discovered that HMGB1 loss caused a significant reduction in BAP1 expression and protein levels, whereas HMGB1 overexpression increased BAP1 mRNA and protein levels. We demonstrated that HMGB1 binds to the BAP1 promoter and activates its transcription, leading to BAP1 overexpression, which in turn promoted the proliferation, migration, and invasion of mesothelioma cells. These findings were confirmed in lung, colon, and cholangiocarcinoma cell lines. These findings indicate that while BAP1 inactivating mutations promote cancer development, cancer cells that do not express BAP1 are less aggressive, pointing to the HMGB1-BAP1 axis as a novel attractive target for therapy. Furthermore, our discovery that HMGB1-driven BAP1 overexpression supports cancer growth provides a mechanistic rationale for the improved survival observed in mesothelioma patients with somatic BAP1 inactivating mutations.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer is a leading cause of cancer mortality, yet early diagnosis remains difficult, highlighting the need for sensitive, noninvasive methods. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) and their surface proteins (e.g., PD-L1) are promising biomarkers; nevertheless, current EV detection requires time-consuming purification, sophisticated instrumentation, and long measurement protocols, resulting in high expenses and operational difficulties. This study developed an integrated colorimetric sensor, IMAN, based on a strategy of "Immunomagnetic Microbeads (IM) capture + Aptamer(Apt) recognition + Nanozyme (N) catalysis". IMAN employs magnetic beads modified with antibodies against CD9 and CD81 to directly capture EVs from serum, eliminating the need for time-consuming prior isolation; combined with a one-step colorimetric readout, the entire workflow can be completed with only ∼40 min of hands-on time, requiring no complex instrumentation. The PD-L1 protein on the EV surface is specifically recognized by a nanoparticle-bound nucleic acid aptamer. Signal generation is achieved through the catalytic oxidation of 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) by a platinum-gold bimetallic nanozyme (Pt@Au). The facile IMAN colorimetric method demonstrated a relatively broad dynamic range (107-1010 particles/mL), high specificity (unaffected by 100 pg/mL soluble PD-L1 in serum), and reproducibility (relative standard deviation, RSD = 9.1%). Analysis of clinical serum samples revealed significantly elevated EV-PD-L1 levels in patients with lung cancer compared with healthy donors and patients with benign nodule (p < 0.01). Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis yielded areas under the curve (AUC) of 0.849 for distinguishing patients with lung cancer from healthy donors and 0.860 for distinguishing patients with lung cancer from patients with benign nodules, which are superior to those of the conventional serum biomarkers CEA and Cyfra21-1. By addressing the cost, complexity, and slow response of current methods, IMAN offers a simple, cost-effective platform for direct EV surface protein detection without complex instrumentation, providing a novel tool for the noninvasive lung cancer diagnosis.

papers.abstract_en: Screening for kidney cancer and other serious abdominal conditions in conjunction with lung cancer screening (LCS) is potentially feasible and cost-effective. Targeted Abdominal CT in Conjunction with Lung Cancer Screening (TACTICAL1) aims to pilot this integrated screening model in a real-world setting to inform a future large-scale randomised controlled trial (RCT). TACTICAL1 is a pilot study, with embedded process evaluation, of adding abdominal noncontrast computed tomography (CT; ANCCT) to low-dose CT (LDCT) thorax amongst ever smokers aged 55-70 yr at high risk of lung cancer who were attending the first round of LCS in Yorkshire, UK. There are two points of randomisation. First, participants are randomised 1:1 at the individual level to receive either an LCS invitation letter (invitation control) or an invitation letter for LCS with potential for an additional ANCCT (invitation intervention). Participants in the latter group are then cluster randomised 1:1 to be offered either LDCT thorax alone (scan control) or both LDCT thorax and ANCCT (scan intervention). TACTICAL1 has four primary endpoints and will assess the following: (1) whether the invitation intervention affects LCS uptake, (2) feasibility of cluster randomisation, (3) impact of adding ANCCT to LCS on scanning throughput, and (4) acceptability to participants and screening staff. Strengths include the real-world setting and robust randomisation. TACTICAL1 is a pilot study; therefore, it does not aim to evaluate the prevalence or stage of screen-detected findings nor survival. TACTICAL1 will inform the development of a future large-scale RCT assessing outcomes such as stage shift, earlier detection, and potential survival benefits. A previous study showed that it is possible to offer an additional computed tomography scan of the abdomen at the same time as lung cancer screening. This extra scan may help detect kidney cancer and other serious abdominal conditions early. TACTICAL1 is a pilot research study in which people are randomly assigned to different groups. Its aim is to test how this combined screening approach could work in practice. The results will help design a much larger future study to find out whether combining these scans can save lives.

papers.abstract_en: Detection of low-abundance biomarkers like circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) remains challenging for molecular diagnosis and therapeutic management of cancer. Here, we developed a homogeneous electrochemical platform using metal ion-mediated DNA self-assembly enhanced by molecular fillers, enabling simultaneous, amplification-free, label-free, and enzyme-free detection of dual biomarkers. Incorporation of methylene blue into DNA nanostructures can suppress non-specific ion leakage, enhance sensitivity by 100-fold and signal-to-noise ratio by 2.5-fold. Target binding triggered DNA nanomachines disassembly, releasing Ag+ or Hg2+ for simultaneously electrochemical analysis, thereby facilitating precise quantification of the target biomarkers. The system achieved high-performance detection of L858R and T790M with limits of 5.2 and 6.0 amol/L, respectively, when applied to epidermal growth factor receptor mutations in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Using qPCR as the reference, mutation detection achieved AUCs of 0.96 for both L858R and T790M. In disease discrimination, L858R showed moderate sensitivity, whereas T790M provided limited discrimination in the predominantly treatment-naive cohort. In addition, the platform also demonstrated applicability in detecting BRAF V600E mutations in thyroid cancer. Exploratory analyses further revealed differences in ctDNA-associated signals between non-metastatic and metastatic cases. This filler-enhanced DNA nanomachine strategy offered a high-performance tool for ultrasensitive ctDNA analysis and showed potential for clinical applications.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Adults with prediabetes or diabetes and cardiovascular disease (CVD) face a substantial burden of premature mortality. Chronic inflammation, malnutrition and vascular aging are key pathways linking dysglycaemia and CVD to adverse outcomes. The Advanced Lung Cancer Inflammation Index (ALI) reflects systemic inflammation and nutritional status, while estimated pulse wave velocity (ePWV) serves as a surrogate of vascular aging. However, their independent and joint associations with mortality in dysglycemic adults with CVD remain unclear. METHODS: NHANES 1999-2018 data comprising 101,316 participants were analyzed. After exclusions, adults ≥ 20 years with prediabetes/diabetes and CVD were included (n = 1,992). ALI and ePWV were analysed as continuous variables and cross-classified using maximally selected cut-points. Survey-weighted Cox models, restricted cubic splines and subgroup/sensitivity analyses were applied. Time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves and C-indices were used to compare prognostic discrimination. RESULTS: Higher ALI was inversely associated with all-cause, cardiovascular, and premature mortality, whereas higher ePWV was positively associated with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality. Per 10-unit increment in ALI, fully adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) were 0.899 (95% CI 0.872-0.928) for all-cause mortality, 0.938 (0.885-0.995) for cardiovascular mortality, and 0.889 (0.837-0.945) for premature mortality. For ePWV, the corresponding HRs per 1 m/s increment were 1.139 (1.072-1.211) for all-cause mortality and 1.216 (1.102-1.341) for cardiovascular mortality. In joint analyses, combined ALI-ePWV categories showed a risk gradient: participants with high ALI/low ePWV had the lowest risks of all-cause mortality (HR 0.382, 95% CI 0.280-0.520), cardiovascular mortality (HR 0.379, 95% CI 0.228-0.630), and premature mortality (HR 0.402, 95% CI 0.245-0.659) compared with those with low ALI/high ePWV. CONCLUSIONS: ALI and ePWV provide complementary information on systemic inflammation-nutrition status and vascular ageing, and their combined categories define distinct risk strata for mortality in adults with dysglycaemia and CVD. Their combined categories may help characterize mortality-risk heterogeneity and inform future risk-assessment studies in this high-risk population.

papers.abstract_en: Erlotinib hydrochloride (ERL), an oral tyrosine kinase inhibitor used in non-small cell lung cancer, is a classic example of drug polymorphism. However, the influence of crystallisation methods, PLGA, and thermal ageing on its polymorphic behaviour remains unexplored. This study investigated ERL polymorphism in binary mixtures prepared by blending, co-grinding, and solvent evaporation. PXRD revealed that blending and co-grinding retained ERL polymorphic form A, whereas solvent evaporation yielded form B in all binary mixtures. Thermal ageing has a significant effect on ERL crystallinity. DSC melting endotherms for form A are at 213.75 and 233.26°C, whereas form B shows a single melting endotherm at 231.96°C. MDSC efficiently captured the melt-mediated recrystallisation of form A. Further, ATR-FTIR with chemometric analysis differentiated the polymorphs into form A (anti) and form B (syn) conformations based on spectral regions at 3270 cm⁻1 (non-classical H-bonding) and 2540 cm⁻1 (N⁺-H···Cl⁻ interactions). SEM revealed plate-like and needle-like morphologies for forms A and B, respectively. Conversely, saturation solubility results reported higher solubility for the solvent-evaporated drug, due to its crystal morphology. Drug content by RP-HPLC (98-102% w/w) confirmed that the observed changes were solely physical transitions. Overall, this study provides insights into the development of ERL-loaded PLGA microspheres.

papers.abstract_en: Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC), a major subtype of non-small cell lung cancer, presents substantial therapeutic challenges due to limited targeted therapy options and prevalent drug resistance. In this study, we characterised 1-octen-3-ol, an active compound derived from bamboo leaves, as a bioactive natural compound with anti-LUSC activity. In vitro, 1-octen-3-ol significantly suppressed LUSC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and colony formation, while promoting apoptosis. Network pharmacology predicted the PI3K/AKT pathway as a central mediator of its activity. Mechanistic studies confirmed that 1-octen-3-ol inhibited PI3K and AKT phosphorylation, accompanied by increased expression of p53 and cleaved-caspase3. The PI3K agonist 740Y-P and AKT agonist SC79 partially reversed the effects of 1-octen-3-ol on LUSC cell migration, invasion, colony formation, and protein expression, underscoring the critical role of the PI3K/AKT pathway. In vivo, 1-octen-3-ol markedly suppressed LUSC xenograft growth, and its tumor-suppressive effect was abrogated by co-administration of either the PI3K or AKT agonist. This study is the first to demonstrate that 1-octen-3-ol exerts potent inhibition of LUSC progression via modulation of the PI3K/AKT pathway, thereby activating p53 and initiating caspase-3-dependent apoptosis. These findings provide mechanistic insights into the anti-LUSC activity of 1-octen-3-ol, a natural volatile small-molecule, and support further lead-discovery efforts based on natural-product sources.

papers.abstract_en: Lung cancer remains one of the most widespread and deadly malignancies worldwide, underscoring the urgent need for rapid and noninvasive diagnostic strategies. Compared with conventional clinical detection techniques, breath analysis based on gas-sensing VOC detection offers exceptional advantages, including high sensitivity, operational simplicity, and real-time capability. In this work, we conduct a comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) investigation into the adsorption characteristics and electronic responses of Au-, Pd-, and Pt-doped WTe2 monolayers toward representative lung-cancer-associated VOCs. Our results reveal that transition-metal doping markedly improves the structural stability and adsorption activity of WTe2, while inducing pronounced modulations in its electronic structure that collectively enhance its gas-sensing performance. Among the examined systems, Au-doped WTe2 exhibits the strongest adsorption strength and the most significant band gap perturbations upon exposure to C5H8, C3H6O, and C3H8O. Moreover, the differentiated sensing behaviors of the three doped monolayers toward various analytes effectively reduce cross-interference issues. These findings provide valuable theoretical insight and identify promising material candidates for the development of highly selective and high-precision breath sensors for early lung cancer detection.

papers.abstract_en: Hypoxia and immunosuppression limit photodynamic therapy (PDT) in treatment-resistant solid tumors. We developed structure-guided, lysosome-targeted Ir(III) photosensitizers and identified a symmetric, π-conjugation-extended dinuclear complex with 810 nm two-photon activation, high singlet-oxygen quantum yield, low dark cytotoxicity, and sustained type-I reactive oxygen species generation under hypoxia. Photoactivation triggered lysosomal membrane permeabilization, cathepsin B release, Ca(II) dysregulation, mitochondrial depolarization, and PINK1-associated mitophagy. This lysosome-to-mitochondria stress relay depleted GSH, inactivated GPX4, increased Fe(II) and lipid peroxidation, and sensitized cisplatin-resistant lung cancer cells to ferroptosis. In a sequential contralateral CMT167 rechallenge model, local treatment suppressed primary tumor growth and delayed the growth of a subsequently implanted, non-irradiated contralateral tumor, accompanied by broad remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment. These findings establish a hypoxia-tolerant dinuclear photosensitizer that couples two-photon PDT to ferroptosis and systemic antitumor immune activation.

papers.abstract_en: Unfavorable drug metabolism drives clinical failure, limited by the low accuracy of existing AI predictors. To address this, we constructed a database of 11,665 human-specific reactions and developed Mettle, a novel AI model integrating chemical feature interaction with contrastive learning. By explicitly training the model to distinguish true metabolic transformations from structurally similar decoys, Mettle achieves state-of-the-art performance with ∼80% top-5 accuracy. We demonstrate Mettle's utility by tackling poor oral bioavailability in RSK4 inhibitors. This metabolite-aware design strategy yielded R636, which maintains high potency while exhibiting a remarkable 63-fold increase in absolute bioavailability (to 63%). R636 showed a favorable safety profile and significant antitumor efficacy in two ESCC PDX models. Mettle thus emerges as a powerful tool for metabolite-aware oral drug design.

papers.abstract_en: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) kinase inhibitors have revolutionized non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) treatment; however, the inevitable acquired resistance necessitates alternative strategies beyond conventional inhibition. Herein, we report the discovery and optimization of VHL-recruiting PROTAC degraders targeting the EGFR. Representative compounds C4 and D4 demonstrated potent, selective, and durable degradation of EGFRDel19 (C4: DC50 = 1.41 nM, Dmax = 99%; D4: DC50 = 9.14 nM, Dmax = 98%) and EGFRL858R (C4: DC50 = 3.30 nM, Dmax = 95%; D4: DC50 = 15.2 nM, Dmax = 98%). C4 induced cell cycle arrest and apoptosis, displayed subnanomolar antiproliferative activity, and drove significant tumor regression in an HCC827 xenograft model at low intravenous doses with a reduced twice-weekly schedule. Remarkably, D4 was orally bioavailable (F = 11.3%) and blood-brain barrier penetrant and completely inhibited tumor growth in vivo after oral dosing. Overall, this work provides promising starting points for next-generation EGFR-directed therapy.

papers.abstract_en: Toll-like receptor 2 (TLR2) agonists hold great promise for cancer immunotherapy. Our previously identified TLR2 agonist SMU-Z1 contains a nitro group associated with potential metabolic toxicity. Herein, 47 analogs were designed and synthesized to mitigate toxicity, and SMU-H1 emerged as a potent, selective TLR2 agonist (EC50 = 5.14 ± 0.7 nM) with superior safety relative to SMU-Z1. Mechanistically, SMU-H1 binds TLR2 to recruit MyD88, activates the MAPK/NF-κB pathways, and induces proinflammatory cytokines. TLR2 dependence was confirmed for the first time using TLR2-knockout mice. SMU-H1 also drives M1 macrophage polarization and dendritic cell activation via TLR2. In vivo, SMU-H1 enhanced immune cell activation and improved antitumor efficacy when combined with conventional anticancer drugs. Overall, SMU-H1 retains robust TLR2 agonistic activity with reduced toxicity, representing a promising candidate for cancer immunotherapy development.

papers.abstract_en: Accurate discrimination of lung cancer subtypes and evaluation of chemotherapeutic efficacy remain critical challenges in precision oncology owing to the heterogeneity of tumor cellular microenvironments. Herein, we report a mitochondrial microenvironment-responsive fluorescence sensor array, MR-SA, for intelligent analysis of lung cancer cells and chemotherapeutic efficacy. Four mitochondria-targeting fluorescent probes were rationally designed by integrating indolium salts with environment-sensitive fluorophores, enabling selective sensing of mitochondrial hypoxia, polarity, pH, and viscosity in living cells. Benefiting from distinct cross-reactive fluorescence response patterns and broad emission coverage ranging from 573 to 734 nm, MR-SA generated multidimensional fluorescence fingerprints for different lung cancer subtypes while minimizing spectral crosstalk. The chemotherapy-induced mitochondrial alterations were monitored using MR-SA and combined with outlier analysis for evaluation of chemotherapeutic efficacy and drug resistance in nonsmall cell lung cancer cells. Furthermore, MR-SA fluorescence images were integrated with ResNet, a deep-learning framework, enabling rapid and accurate blind classification of lung cancer cells with a recognition accuracy of 99.71%. Thus, MR-SA successfully distinguished lung adenocarcinoma, lung squamous cell carcinoma, large cell carcinoma, and small cell lung cancer cells through differential mitochondrial microenvironment profiling. This work establishes a versatile fluorescence sensing strategy for multidimensional mitochondrial analysis and provides a promising analytical platform for intelligent cancer cell profiling and chemotherapeutic evaluation.

papers.abstract_en: In cancer diagnosis, liquid biopsy is a minimally invasive method, yet its diagnostic performance is constrained by insufficient sensitivity and restricted blood biomarkers. Therefore, the use of additional invasive methods is unavoidable to identify cancer-specific information, such as subtypes, stages, and mutation status. Here, we propose a deep-learning-based method for differential diagnosis, in which group-specific feature importance is assigned to Raman spectra of extracellular vesicles (EVs) and the spectra are decoded. The feature importance was extracted from the training dataset using explainable AI (XAI) to emphasize key spectral patterns. These features were then applied to the original spectra as weights to develop an AI-based diagnostic algorithm. As a result, the algorithm successfully identified the presence of lung cancer, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) value of 0.98. Moreover, it demonstrated the capability of precision cancer diagnosis with an average AUC of 0.96 across the detailed cancer information. These preliminary findings suggest the potential of liquid-biopsy-based differential diagnosis and its possible contribution to the establishment of rapid and tailored treatment strategies.

papers.abstract_en: Cigarette smoking is a primary etiological factor in lung cancer, and 4-(methylnitrosamino)-1-(3-pyridyl)-1-butanone (NNK) is a prototypical tobacco-specific nitrosamine carcinogen. Although FTO has been implicated in the progression of various cancers, its specific role in smoking-associated lung carcinogenesis remains incompletely understood. In this study, we built a model of NNK-induced malignant transformation of human bronchial epithelial Beas-2B cells (designated Beas-2B-NNK cells) to explore the function and regulatory mechanism of FTO during NNK-induced lung carcinogenesis. Through quantitative real-time PCR (RT-qPCR) assays, FTO levels were found to be notably higher in Beas-2B-NNK cells when compared with their parental Beas-2B cell line. Then, knocking down FTO expression using short hairpin RNA (shRNA) led to marked repression of proliferation, migration, and cell-cycle progression in Beas-2B-NNK cells. Bioinformatics analysis revealed a positive correlation between FTO and DIXDC1, and when FTO was knocked out, the sharpest drop in DIXDC1 expression was seen in Beas-2B-NNK cells. Combined bioinformatic and Western blot analysis observed that DIXDC1 regulates the malignant transformation of Beas-2B-NNK cells via the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. In summary, these findings suggest that FTO participates in NNK-induced malignant transformation of Beas-2B cells via the DIXDC1/PI3K/AKT signaling axis.

papers.abstract_en: Exhaled breath analysis offers a noninvasive route for disease screening, yet its practical implementation is constrained by ultratrace analyte levels, high humidity, and limited selectivity of existing enrichment materials. Herein, we report the rational design of a carboxyl-functionalized hyper-cross-linked polymer (HCPs-COOH) as a high-performance solid-phase microextraction (SPME) coating and its integration into a two-step preconcentration workflow for breath analysis. The HCPs-COOH exhibits an ultrahigh specific surface area (1916 m2 g-1) and hierarchical micromesoporosity, enabling high-capacity uptake and rapid mass transfer. Surface carboxyl (-COOH) groups introduce specific interactions (hydrogen bonding and dipole-dipole), while the hydrophobic framework mitigates water interference, collectively enhancing affinity and selectivity toward diverse volatile organic compounds (VOCs) classes. Coupling Tenax-TA adsorption tube sampling with solvent elution and headspace HCPs-COOH-SPME, followed by GC-MS detection, affords a sensitive and robust method for the simultaneous determination of five lung cancer-related biomarkers. The method achieved limits of quantification of 0.10-0.21 pg mL-1, excellent precision, and high enrichment factors up to 5304. Compared with commercial fibers and reported approaches, the HCPs-COOH coating provides faster equilibration, higher enrichment efficiency, and improved tolerance to humid matrices. Application to exhaled breath samples from lung cancer patients and healthy volunteers reveals consistently elevated levels of all five biomarkers in the patient group, demonstrating clear discriminative capability. This work establishes a versatile, cost-effective platform that integrates high-capacity adsorption with selective SPME enrichment, providing a powerful strategy for ultrasensitive breathomics and advancing the clinical translation of noninvasive cancer screening.

papers.abstract_en: Multiplexed protein profiling of tumor-derived small extracellular vesicles (TsEVs) requires signal-conversion strategies that are sensitive, low-background, and orthogonal. Collateral-cleavage CRISPR assays based on Cas12a or Cas13a provide efficient amplification but can compromise single-pot multitarget detection, whereas the sequence-specific cleavage of Cas9 remains underexplored for converting vesicle-surface protein recognition into orthogonal amplified outputs. Here, we report CHAI-sEV, a programmable Cas9-mediated trigger-release strategy based on PAM-bearing hairpin-locking probes (PHLPs) for dual-protein profiling of TsEVs. Each PHLP integrates Cas9 recognition and signal conversion into a single molecular substrate, in which sgRNA-guided Cas9 cleavage unlocks a sequestered CHA activator to initiate orthogonal signal amplification. After EGFR- or PD-L1-binding aptamers label TsEVs, engineered aptamer tails recruit specific Cas9-sgRNA complexes to the vesicle surface, enabling protein-specific PHLP activation and amplified fluorescence readout. This Cas9-programmed trigger-release mechanism enables dual-channel TsEV protein detection without relying on nonspecific collateral cleavage. Under optimized conditions, CHAI-sEV achieved detection limits of 162 and 328 particles/μL for EGFR and PD-L1. In plasma samples, CHAI-sEV differentiated lung cancer patients from benign-lung-disease patients and healthy controls and showed decreased EGFR and PD-L1 signals in post-treatment samples. As proof-of-concept extensions, the CHAI-sEV was further coupled to an IGZO-FET electrical readout and an exploratory machine-learning analysis combining dual-protein signals with clinical features. Overall, PHLPs provide a substrate-design principle that converts Cas9 cleavage into amplification-compatible and orthogonally multiplexable biosensing outputs, enabling sensitive and multiplexed protein profiling of TsEVs and offering potential for extension to diverse molecular targets.

papers.abstract_en: KRASG12C mutation occurs in approximately 14% of lung adenocarcinoma cases and has emerged as an important therapeutic target in precision oncology. In this study, a series of novel quinazoline-6-carbonitrile derivatives were developed as KRASG12C covalent inhibitors. Among them, the representative compound 8t displayed significant inhibitory activity against KRASG12C in biochemical assay and KRASG12C-mutant non-small cell lung cancer H358 cells with IC50 values of 3.13 and 1.8 nM, respectively. It also effectively blocked ERK and AKT phosphorylation with IC50 value of 4.67 and 23.74 nM, respectively. LCMS analysis confirmed that compound 8t binds to KRASG12C rapidly and covalently. In addition, 8t demonstrated moderate metabolic stability in human liver microsomes and moderate oral bioavailability in mice. Furthermore, compound 8t showed partial antitumor efficacy in H358 xenograft models following once-daily dosing at 30 mg/kg, without causing significant body weight loss. These findings indicated that 8t could serve as a promising lead compound for the treatment of KRASG12C-mutant NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: Intratumoral injection of cisplatin into lung cancer is feasible and can increase local drug exposure while reducing systemic toxicity. However, its success relies on achieving sufficient drug exposure to the tumor, which has not been quantitatively evaluated in a clinical setting. In the context of a Phase I clinical trial of intratumoral cisplatin injections into resectable lung tumors via robotic bronchoscopy (N = 6), we developed a quantitative framework to assess delivery effectiveness and long-term cisplatin exposure in tumors. Initial injectate retention was estimated using a novel image analytics pipeline based on intraoperative cone-beam computed tomography scans, by assuming that emerging high-attenuation regions are due to injectate deposition. Long-term drug exposure was estimated using a novel pharmacokinetic model tailored for intratumoral drug delivery and informed by sequential venous blood draws following the injections. The area under the platinum concentration curve in the tumor compartment at t = 3-21 h and platinum concentration in the tumor compartment (t = 3-6 h), estimated from the fitted pharmacokinetic model, showed a strong monotonic association with percentage pathological necrosis assessed post-resection by three independent, blinded pathologists (Spearman's ρ = 0.93, 95% bootstrap CI 0.67-1.00, unadjusted exact p = 0.033), which was not statistically significant when corrected for multiple comparisons (adjusted p = 0.17). No other pharmacokinetic variable correlated was significantly correlated with necrosis or other pathological response metrics prior to multiple comparison correction. This result aligns with the known time-concentration dependency of cisplatin action in tumor. Further studies will be needed to evaluate this observation for repeatability and clinical relevance. Our approach provides a framework for estimating intratumoral drug exposure in clinical settings, which may help with the interpretation of clinical trial outcomes and future evaluation of injection strategies.

papers.abstract_en: Histone post-translational modifications (PTMs) segregate genomes into heterochromatin and euchromatin by recruiting readers, such as Heterochromatin Protein 1, which binds methylation of histone H3 lysine 9 (H3K9me). Here, we report H3K9me-independent functions for the C. elegans HP1 orthologue HPL-2 and the H3K9 methyltransferase MET-2/SETDB1. The two colocalize in H3K9me-containing subnuclear foci independently of the PTM and each other. Their combined loss additively disrupts gene repression and organogenesis. A mutant HPL-2 deficient for H3K9me binding maintains localization to heterochromatin foci, restricts cell-fate decisions, and represses developmental genes, dependent on its multi-zinc-finger ligand, LIN-13. MET-2, catalytically active or not, requires its cofactor LIN-65 to form foci and silence genes in vivo. Molecular dynamics simulations and in vitro assays suggest that cofactor-driven condensate assemblies underlie H3K9me-independent focus formation in vivo, which correlates with gene silencing during organogenesis. This study defines two parallel, PTM-independent pathways through which a writer and reader can repress developmentally regulated genes.

papers.abstract_en: Cancer remains a formidable challenge in global oncology, with conventional treatments often failing to achieve durable responses in advanced stages. Adoptive cell therapy (ACT), despite its revolutionary success in hematological malignancies, faces critical bottlenecks in solid tumors, including a hostile immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), restricted cellular trafficking, and the rapid onset of T-cell exhaustion. This review systematically explores the evolution of ACT platforms, ranging from foundational tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) to precision-engineered chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T and T-cell receptor (TCR)-T therapies. We highlight how innovative engineering strategies such as the integration of "armored" CARs, synthetic gene circuits, and CRISPR/Cas9-mediated gene editing have been employed to enhance the persistence and polyfunctionality of effector cells. Beyond T-cell-centric approaches, we examine the emerging landscape of diverse immune effector cells, including CAR-natural killer (NK) cells, and CAR-macrophages (CAR-M), which offer unique advantages in antigen recognition and safety profiles. Furthermore, we detail the synergistic potential of multimodal combination regimens, where ACT is paired with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), localized radiotherapy, or nanotechnology-based delivery systems to dismantle TME barriers and achieve systemic anti-tumor immunity. By tracing the journey of therapeutic cells from ex vivo expansion to intratumoral infiltration and cytotoxicity, this review illuminates the molecular mechanisms governing therapeutic efficacy. Finally, we discuss the current clinical trial landscape, manufacturing hurdles, and the regulatory pathways essential for transitioning these sophisticated cellular products from bench to bedside.

papers.abstract_en: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by a dense desmoplastic stroma and early metastatic dissemination, both of which contribute to its poor prognosis. While forkhead box protein 3 (FOXP3) is best known as a lineage-defining transcription factor in regulatory T cells (Tregs), its aberrant expression in cancer cell-specific FOXP3 (c-FOXP3) may also support tumor-cell-intrinsic progression. Our findings suggest that high c-FOXP3 expression is closely linked to aggressive disease behavior and metastatic progression in PDAC. c-FOXP3 enhanced migration, invasion within three-dimensional collagen-rich matrices, and dissemination in orthotopic models. Integrated transcriptomic analysis, chromatin immunoprecipitation, and wild-type versus binding-site-mutant promoter assays identified matrix metalloproteinase 19 (MMP19) as a direct transcriptional target of c-FOXP3. MMP19 silencing significantly attenuated c-FOXP3-driven migration, matrix invasion, and metastasis. Single-cell sequencing further showed that MMP19 is abundant in cancer-associated fibroblasts but also defines a distinct epithelial pool that is reduced after epithelial Foxp3 deletion. Pharmacological profiling did not identify a validated MMP19-selective inhibitor, whereas the FOXP3-targeting antisense oligonucleotide AZD8701 reduced FOXP3 together with MMP19 mRNA and was accompanied by lower PDAC-cell migration and invasion in vitro. Together, these findings extend the known functions of FOXP3 beyond its classical role in immune tolerance and define a tumor-cell-intrinsic c-FOXP3-MMP19 program that supports matrix-invasive behavior in PDAC and provide preliminary evidence that c-FOXP3 is pharmacologically accessible.

papers.abstract_en: The development of isoform-selective HSP70 inhibitors remains challenging due to the high conservation of this chaperone family. Continuing our efforts to target the peptide-binding pocket within the substrate-binding domain (SBD) of GRP78 (BiP/HSPA5), we identified compound 12 using a Direct-to-Biology (D2B) strategy. Biochemical, biophysical, and cellular characterization showed that 12 directly engages the GRP78 peptide-binding pocket, selectively binds GRP78 over other tested HSP70 isoforms, and potently kills A549 lung cancer cells while showing minimal activity in other tested lung cancer cell lines. Cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) demonstrated GRP78 engagement in cells, and unfolded protein response (UPR) signaling analysis further showed that 12 modulates GRP78-related stress-response pathways, supporting its functional engagement of GRP78. Collectively, compound 12 represents a well-characterized, isoform-selective, cell active, and cell selective GRP78 inhibitor, providing a valuable chemical probe for dissecting GRP78 biology and a promising starting point for the development of GRP78-targeted therapeutics.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Thyroid cancer has a favourable prognosis, yet many survivors experience ongoing psychological and social challenges. Although support is available, it is often underused. This study explored barriers to support-seeking in the UK. METHODS: An inductive, qualitative approach was taken. Twenty-five adults with papillary or follicular thyroid cancer were recruited through an NHS Trust and a national charity. Semi-structured interviews were conducted and thematically analysed, with the findings compared to existing bodies of theory. RESULTS: Barriers clustered into two domains. Domain A focused on personal illness representations: (1) self-sufficiency and low perceived need ('I thought I could cope alone'), (2) altruistic reluctance ('others need it more than me'), and (3) limited sense of belonging due to age or cancer type ('not for people like me'). Domain B captured structural influences: (4) absence of proactive follow-up ('care ends at discharge') and (5) support options that did not meet individual preferences ('one-size doesn't fit all'). An approach that combined the Common-Sense Model of Illness Representations and Andersen's Behavioural Model of Health Services Use was most helpful in contextualising these findings. This approach showed how beliefs about coping, emotional regulation, and moral comparisons intersect with service design, information quality, and enabling resources to limit engagement with psychosocial support. CONCLUSION: Barriers arise through the interaction of belief-based and system-level factors. Clinically, routine assessment of illness perceptions, normalisation of help-seeking, proactive survivorship follow-up, and flexible, tailored support options may improve engagement. Embedding psychosocial care within standard follow-up could help position emotional well-being at the centre of thyroid cancer recovery.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Perioperative regurgitation of gastric or esophageal contents remains a severe complication during anesthesia. While standard fasting protocols and rapid sequence induction (RSI) are routinely employed, esophageal dilatation creates a hidden reservoir for retained food and secretions that conventional methods often fail to mitigate. Furthermore, standard gastric ultrasound lacks the field of view to detect mid-to-proximal esophageal pooling. CASE PRESENTATION: We present two parallel cases emphasizing this critical challenge. Case 1 involves a 68-year-old male with esophageal carcinoma who experienced massive regurgitation of white foam during RSI, despite five days of preoperative fasting. Airway security was ultimately achieved after intensified suctioning. Case 2 describes a 42-year-old female with achalasia and marked esophageal dilatation. Informed by preoperative computed tomography (CT) and barium swallow imaging, she was safely managed using targeted pre-anesthetic conscious endoscopic suctioning, leading to an uneventful induction and peroral endoscopic myotomy (POEM). CONCLUSION: These cases highlight the limitations of conventional fasting in managing proximal pooling. They underscore the diagnostic value of preoperative cross-sectional imaging, such as CT, when clinically indicated. Active pre-induction decompression, specifically through tailored endoscopic evacuation, is a valuable adjunctive strategy for preventing perioperative regurgitation in selected patients with megaesophagus.

papers.abstract_en: Biological systems exhibit complex hierarchical regulation, with interactions across multiple layers governing transitions between states. Identifying the causal architecture underlying these state transitions remains challenging because confounding can produce spurious associations in observational data. Here we present CauTrigger, a hierarchical deep latent variable model that integrates do-calculus to identify potential causal triggers and predict perturbation outcomes across multiple regulatory layers. By disentangling causal and spurious latent factors, CauTrigger recursively reconstructs the underlying regulatory hierarchy and enables interpretable reasoning from observational data. Across synthetic and real-world datasets with multilayer regulatory structures, CauTrigger outperforms existing methods in identifying causal triggers and forecasting system-level responses. Applied to single-cell multi-omics and gut microbiome datasets, CauTrigger prioritizes candidate causal triggers and uses in silico perturbations to generate testable hypotheses about biological state transitions and inform potential strategies for state navigation. Together, these results establish CauTrigger as a general-purpose framework for causal discovery in complex biological systems.

papers.abstract_en: Secretory clusterin (sCLU) has been implicated in inflammatory diseases, yet its role in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) remains poorly defined. Here, we showed that serum sCLU levels were significantly elevated in patients with RA compared with healthy controls (n = 192 RA; n = 139 HC) and were associated with disease activity. Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated moderate diagnostic performance for RA discrimination (AUC = 0.783, 95% CI 0.730-0.837). Mechanistically, M1-polarized macrophages exhibited enhanced sCLU secretion, whereas RA fibroblast-like synoviocytes (RA-FLS) produced minimal sCLU, identifying inflammatory macrophages as an important source of extracellular sCLU. Using a Transwell co-culture system and recombinant sCLU stimulation, we found that sCLU amplified inflammatory cytokine production and promoted the proliferative, migratory, invasive, and apoptosis-resistant phenotypes of RA-FLS under inflammatory conditions. These effects were accompanied with activation of the PI3K/AKT and NF-κB pathways and were significantly attenuated by pharmacological inhibition of either pathway. Proteomic screening, surface plasmon resonance, and co-immunoprecipitation analyses identified fibronectin 1 (FN1) as a direct binding partner of sCLU although its functional contribution requires further investigation. Importantly, genetic deletion of sCLU alleviated disease severity in collagen-induced arthritis mice. Collectively, our findings identify macrophage-derived sCLU as an inflammatory amplifier in RA and suggest that targeting sCLU may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for inflammatory arthritis.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Cervical adenocarcinoma (ADC) exhibits a poorer prognosis than cervical squamous cell carcinoma and lacks effective targeted therapies. Bombesin receptor- activated protein (BRAP, encoded by C6orf89) has been implicated in cell proliferation and stress responses in multiple biological contexts; however, its role in ADC progression and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) homeostasis remains unknown. METHODS: BRAP expression was evaluated in human cervical adenocarcinoma (ADC) tissues by immunohistochemistry and western blotting, and its clinicopathological significance was analyzed. BRAP function was investigated by siRNA-mediated knockdown in HeLa and SiHa cells using proliferation, apoptosis, migration, invasion, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) assays, and further validated in xenograft models. Ultrastructural alterations were examined by transmission electron microscopy. BRAP-interacting proteins were identified by yeast two-hybrid screening and validated by co-immunoprecipitation. ER stress, ER exit site (ERES) homeostasis, and autophagic flux were evaluated, and rescue experiments were performed by re-expression of BRAP or SEC24D. RESULTS: BRAP was markedly upregulated in cervical adenocarcinoma tissues and was associated with poor tumor differentiation. BRAP depletion selectively inhibited proliferation, migration, invasion, and EMT while promoting apoptosis in ADC-derived HeLa cells, but not in squamous cell carcinoma-derived SiHa cells. Mechanistically, BRAP deficiency disrupted ER homeostasis and selectively activated the PERK-ATF4-DDIT3/CHOP branch of the unfolded protein response (UPR), whereas pharmacological inhibition with GSK2606414 largely reversed these phenotypic alterations. We identified the COPII cargo adaptor SEC24D as a novel BRAP-interacting protein. BRAP maintained SEC24D protein stability by preventing excessive autophagy-lysosome-mediated degradation, thereby preserving ERES number and function, as reflected by SEC16A-positive ERES and peripheral LMAN1-positive structures, and maintaining ER-Golgi trafficking homeostasis. Restoration of SEC24D rescued ERES defects, attenuated PERK-dependent UPR activation, and reversed the impaired proliferation, migration, invasion, apoptosis, and EMT induced by BRAP depletion. CONCLUSION: BRAP promotes cervical adenocarcinoma progression by maintaining SEC24D stability and preserving ERES organization and function, thereby sustaining COPII-dependent ER export and ER homeostasis. Disruption of the BRAP-SEC24D axis impairs ERES integrity, activates PERK-dependent ER stress, and suppresses malignant phenotypes. These findings identify BRAP as a previously unrecognized regulator of ER homeostasis and establish the BRAP-SEC24D signaling axis as a potential therapeutic target for cervical adenocarcinoma.
