papers.abstract_en: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by severe immunosuppression and metabolic reprogramming, yet the spatial dynamics of lipid flux between malignant and stromal cells remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a profound, type-specific metabolic rewiring in HCC driven by the widespread downregulation of fatty acid transport protein 5 (FATP5). FATP5 deficiency in malignant cells selectively attenuates the uptake of long-chain fatty acids (LCFAs), creating an extracellular lipid surplus that is passively sequestered by neighboring FATP3-expressing tumor-associated endothelial cells (TECs). Within TECs, accumulated LCFAs function as endogenous ligands that activate the nuclear receptor PPARγ, culminating in the robust transcriptional upregulation and paracrine secretion of the chemokine CXCL12. Endothelial-derived CXCL12 subsequently engages CXCR4 on infiltrating CD8+ T cells, inducing PD-1 expression and driving terminal T-cell exhaustion, thereby establishing an immunosuppressive niche that accelerates tumor progression. Importantly, our data suggest that HCC subtypes marked by FATP5 depletion and CXCL12+ TEC enrichment may possess potential therapeutic susceptibility to PPARγ antagonism or anti-PD-1 immune checkpoint blockade. Besides affecting the secretory function of TECs, accumulated LCFAs can impair endothelial barrier function, thereby creating a microenvironment with hematogenous metastasis risk. Collectively, our findings delineate a novel tumor-promoting microenvironment cascade orchestrated by LCFA spatial redistribution, providing a promising mechanistic foundation to support the future development of targeted precision interventions for FATP5-low HCC.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Gastroparesis is a debilitating disease for which therapeutic strategies achieve variable success. This systematic review and consensus statements address the surgical management of medically refractory gastroparesis. METHODOLOGY: A systematic review was conducted, with a literature search through December 31, 2024, addressing the surgical treatment of gastroparesis, including gastric electrical stimulation (GES), gastric per-oral endoscopic myotomy (GPOEM), pyloroplasty and pyloromyotomy, and gastrectomy. Studies assessing symptom resolution and changes in gastric emptying were extracted. The findings were subsequently presented to a panel of surgeons and gastroenterologists, some of whom are members of the Society of American Gastrointestinal and Endoscopic Surgeons (SAGES), with the patient partner perspective considered. Consensus statements were generated from the presented data and subsequent discussion for each of the four treatment options. RESULTS: All consensus statements were based on expert opinion due to poor and heterogeneous datasets for each intervention. The panel judged GES, pyloroplasty, and pyloromyotomy, including gastric per-oral endoscopic myotomy, to be reasonable treatments for patients with medically refractory gastroparesis. The panel does not suggest surgical resection as a standard treatment option for medically refractory gastroparesis, but acknowledges that in specific patient cases, it may be reasonable. CONCLUSIONS: The consensus views achieved provide guidance for surgical approaches to medically refractory gastroparesis. The panel also highlighted evidence gaps that warrant research to strengthen the evidence base for surgical treatment strategies for gastroparesis.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Postoperative esophageal achalasia after lung surgery is extremely rare. Vagal nerve injury has been proposed as a possible mechanism of postsurgical esophageal dysmotility. We report a rare case of esophageal achalasia following robot-assisted lung cancer surgery. CASE PRESENTATION: A 63-year-old woman with lung adenocarcinoma (cT1cN0M0, stage IA3) underwent robot-assisted left lower lobectomy with systematic mediastinal lymph node dissection. On postoperative day 2, she developed vomiting and difficulty eating. Computed tomography revealed esophageal dilatation with retained food, and esophagography demonstrated absent esophageal peristalsis, narrowing at the esophagogastric junction, and contrast retention. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy revealed no mechanical obstruction. High-resolution manometry confirmed esophageal achalasia. Pneumatic dilation was performed on postoperative day 15, resulting in improvement of esophagogastric junction relaxation. She was discharged on postoperative day 24 and remained well without recurrence of achalasia 6 years after surgery. CONCLUSION: Postoperative achalasia is a rare complication of lung surgery. Although the causal mechanism in this case could not be established, perioperative vagal nerve or esophageal plexus injury was considered a possible mechanism. Careful handling of the vagus nerve and cautious use of energy devices near the esophagus may help prevent this complication, and achalasia should be considered in patients with persistent dysphagia after lung surgery.

papers.abstract_en: The application of clinical genomics in personalized medical practice increasingly reveals that variants from single loci can lead to phenotypic heterogeneity. This necessitates functional characterization and classification of serial variants to correlate their associated clinical features and molecular properties. Recently, a few putative pathogenic variants in YWHAZ, encoding the 14-3-3ζ protein, have been implicated in clinically variable isolated and syndromic neurodevelopmental phenotypes, based on a few reported affected individuals, but the molecular basis of this heterogeneity has remained unclear. Here, we assembled a large cohort of individuals harboring de novo YWHAZ variants and categorized their clinical stratification into distinct neurodevelopmental conditions, including a typical presentation of cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome and a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy with sleep disorders. By integrating structural analyses, molecular dynamics simulations, in vitro biochemical and cell-based signaling studies, unbiased proteomics analysis, and in vivo phenotypic assays, we define distinct functional classes of pathogenic YWHAZ variants and establish robust genotype-phenotype correlations. We show that disease-associated YWHAZ variants differentially perturb 14-3-3ζ function by variably affecting protein abundance and binding to interacting partners, including the BRAF and RAF1 kinases. Notably, the recurrent p.Ser230Trp (c.689C>G) variant uniquely underlying cardiofaciocutaneous syndrome specifically enhances MAPK signaling, whereas other variants do not significantly impact signal flow through the cascade under the used experimental conditions. Our data establish a mechanistic framework linking allelic variation in YWHAZ to phenotypic heterogeneity.

papers.abstract_en: DNA's anti-parallel structure presents a topological challenge to the replisome, as leading and lagging strands must be synthesized in opposite directions. How lagging-strand synthesis is coordinated with leading-strand synthesis remains unresolved in eukaryotes. To address this question, we directly visualized the dynamics of lagging-strand polymerases Pol α and Pol δ at active replication forks using single-molecule imaging in Xenopus nuclear extracts. Surprisingly, we find that neither Pol α nor Pol δ is stably tethered to the replisome. Instead, lagging-strand synthesis occurs distributively and entails the rapid recruitment of new molecules of Pol α and Pol δ for each Okazaki fragment. Consequently, leading- and lagging-strand synthesis are not intrinsically coupled. We propose that metazoans solve the problem of anti-parallel replication not by actively coordinating leading- and lagging-strand synthesis, but instead simply by recruiting new polymerases to synthesize each Okazaki fragment.

papers.abstract_en: The gut microbiota programs mammalian circadian metabolism, yet the mechanisms remain unclear. Because feeding behavior is inherently rhythmic and strongly influences microbial metabolism, we hypothesized that the microbiota translates feeding timing into host circadian programs. We show that gut commensal Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron (Bt), in concert with feeding schedules, promotes diurnal chromatin-binding activity of the histone deacetylase 3 (HDAC3) in intestinal epithelial cells. Bt produces inositol triphosphate (InsP3) in a feeding-entrained diurnal manner that enhances HDAC3 activity. Colonization with wild-type Bt, but not an inositol phosphatase mutant, enhanced genome-wide rhythms in epithelial histone acetylation and metabolic gene expression. InsP3-activated HDAC3 deacetylates the transcriptional coactivator PGC-1α, resulting in enhanced expression of nutrient transporter genes. This Bt-InsPs-HDAC3 axis worsens diet-induced obesity in overnourished mice while improving growth in undernourished juvenile mice. These findings reveal a co-evolved microbial-epigenetic-circadian axis that orchestrates nutrient absorption and impacts energy homeostasis across nutritional states.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Incisional hernias represent a significant source of morbidity for patients following liver transplantation, and repair of these defects remains challenging. Transversus abdominis release (TAR) is a posterior component separation technique enabling wide sublay prosthetic reinforcement which is suitable for the treatment of complex incisional hernias. TAR can be used with the enhanced view totally extraperitoneal (eTEP) approach, with favorable outcomes in non-transplant patients being reported. METHODS: This is a single center retrospective review of adult liver transplant recipients with incisional hernias who underwent robotic-assisted eTEP with bilateral TAR between December 2022 and July 2026. A comprehensive description of the surgical technique is included. Patient demographics, hernia characteristics, as well as clinical outcomes are also described. RESULTS: Twenty-six liver transplant patients who underwent incisional hernia repair with eTEP and bilateral TAR met the inclusion criteria. Median age was 60 (IQR 55-65) and patients were predominately male (81%, n = 21). Median BMI was 28.1 (IQR 24-32) and patients were predominately ASA 3 (81%, n = 21). Median hernia length was 12 cm (IQR 9-15) and width was 15 cm (IQR 10-22). Median mesh length was 30 cm (IQR 30-35) and width was 30 cm (IQR 27-37). Mesh was fixated in 65% of patients (n = 17), predominantly with sutures (88%, n = 15). Drains were used in 92% of patients (n = 24). Median operative time was 381 min (IQR 230-517). There were no conversions to open or intraoperative complications. One patient was readmitted for a mild drain site infection which was medically managed with no other complications. Median length of stay was 2 days (IQR 1-3). Over a median follow-up period of 11 months (IQR 7-18) no patients experienced recurrence. CONCLUSION: Patients with chevron incisional hernias following liver transplantation may be repaired with robotic-assisted eTEP with bilateral TAR. In a cohort of suitable candidates, we report favorable 30-day outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: Acute strokes encompass two main types: acute ischemic stroke (AIS) and intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). Each type involves specific imaging techniques and entails different clinical considerations. While deep learning has facilitated the analysis of stroke imaging autonomously, the technical differences between these two stroke types have not been examined within a shared analytical framework. This review addresses that gap through the examination of 84 peer-reviewed articles. A PRISMA-compliant search was conducted using multiple databases. Analysis of the ICH pipeline predominantly uses CT imaging and is primarily centered on a classification task. The main focus is on hemorrhage identification, subtype classification, hematoma expansion prediction, and forecasting associated clinical outcomes. The AIS pipeline is primarily based on quantification and therefore uses a variety of imaging techniques to optimize and automate the analysis of a specific set of clinical questions related to the stroke. Core tasks include segmentation of the infarct area, assessment scoring, large vessel occlusion, core-penumbra mismatch analysis, and prediction of outcomes. Convergence is also observed in outcome prediction approaches across both domains. Existing models demonstrate clinically acceptable performance across numerous tasks. Clinical deployment nonetheless remains limited by the lack of external validation, high costs of annotation, demands of real-time processing, and poor prospective evidence. This review offers practical guidance to develop fully operational AI systems that can be integrated into emergency stroke care.

papers.abstract_en: The construction of gene regulatory networks based on single-cell transcriptomics (scRNA-seq) data provides crucial technical support for decoding cell fate determination mechanisms at the single-cell level, elucidating molecular mechanisms underlying disease progression, and developing targeted therapeutics. Existing methods for constructing GRNs often rely excessively on gene expression features, struggling to achieve an effective balance between local direct regulatory signals and global multi-step regulatory pathways. This imbalance results in insufficient utilization of topological information within the network structure. Therefore, this study proposes a heuristic graph neural network-based GRN inference model (scHGNN). scHGNN integrates multi-order neighbor topological information into learnable weights through unified heuristic matrix and link prediction modules, thereby balancing local and global regulatory relationships. This approach effectively fuses gene expression features with network structural information to achieve precise inference of latent regulatory links within gene regulatory networks. Across GRN inference tasks using benchmark networks of varying gene scales and diverse origins, scHGNN consistently outperforms existing mainstream methods on key evaluation metrics. Furthermore, in target gene prediction cases for key transcription factors such as TP53, OTX2, and FOXP1, the model achieved validation rates as high as 76%-84% in the hTFtarget database. This not only supports its accuracy in identifying known regulatory relationships but also indicates its potential to identify high-confidence candidate regulatory interactions for further biological investigation. Collectively, these results demonstrate that scHGNN holds significant application value in elucidating gene regulatory mechanisms and exploring the molecular basis of related diseases.

papers.abstract_en: Non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a lethal malignant tumor worldwide. Although ferroptosis offers a promising route for curcumin-mediated non-small-cell lung cancer therapy, its efficacy is often constrained by the robust antioxidant defense maintained by the SLC7A11/GSH/GPX4 axis, which continuously sustains cystine uptake, glutathione biosynthesis, and GPX4-dependent lipid peroxide detoxification, thereby maintaining cellular homeostasis. Herein, we developed a glutathione-responsive metal-organic framework nanoplatform for the co-delivery of curcumin and a GPX4-targeting antisense oligonucleotide (ASO). After cellular internalization, the disulfide-bearing framework underwent GSH-triggered disassembly, enabling synchronized release of curcumin and ASO while depleting the intracellular GSH. Released curcumin increased ROS accumulation and disturbed redox homeostasis, whereas ASO silenced GPX4 expression to concurrently disable the antioxidant defense. Flow cytometry and Western blot assays confirmed significant ROS accumulation and SLC7A11 downregulation, which were detailed by molecular dynamics simulations with putative binding modes. Furthermore, the nanocomposite demonstrated robust anticancer effects in 3D multicellular tumor spheroids with a promoted oxidative imbalance. Taken together, this coordinated intervention disrupted the SLC7A11/GSH/GPX4 antioxidant axis, amplified lipid peroxidation, impaired mitochondrial function, and ultimately enhanced ferroptotic vulnerability.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Porcine Enteric Viruses (PEVs) pose a serious threat to the global pig industry, leading to substantial economic losses. However, traditional clinical diagnostic methods are limited by high costs, long turnaround times, and difficulties in rapidly addressing challenges such as co-infections with multiple viruses and the emergence of different viral species. To overcome the limitations of existing approaches in recognizing viruses under complex clinical conditions, poor adaptability to variant strains, and the insufficient extraction of key features, this study proposes a deep learning network integrating the ESM-2 protein language model and a multi-branch heterogeneous architecture, named DynML-Net. RESULTS: The model adaptively integrates decision outputs representing local architectural patterns, global dependencies, and long-sequence evolutionary features through a dynamic gating mechanism, and enhances classification performance via a deep mutual learning (DML) strategy. Experimental results demonstrate that DynML-Net achieves accuracies of 94.52% and 89.16% for binary and multiclass classification tasks, respectively, outperforming current mainstream models, while exhibiting robust performance under conditions of sample imbalance, data reduction, and heterologous viral datasets scenarios. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrated the efficacy of DynML-Net in PEVs identification and classification tasks, and based on DynML-Net, a Streamlit-based locally deployable system was developed to facilitate a closed-loop workflow from sequence upload to automated identification, providing an accurate and efficient computational solution for the rapid detection of PEVs.

papers.abstract_en: Nonhistone acetylation is a key epigenetic mechanism in osteoarthritis (OA), but its specific role in cartilage degeneration remains unclear. Here, we integrated transcriptomics, proteomics, and acetyl-proteomics to systematically analyze molecular changes in rat OA cartilage. Multiomics coenrichment identified the ECM-receptor interaction pathway as the core target, reprogrammed by increased acetylation of Fn1, Tnc, and Itgb1. Using 113 machine-learning strategies, we identified 11 core diagnostic genes, with Wisp3 showing the highest efficacy validated in independent data sets. In vitro experiments and single-cell RNA-seq confirmed that Wisp3 downregulation disrupts ECM homeostasis. This study reveals that nonhistone acetylation drives OA by reprogramming the ECM-receptor interaction pathway and provides novel early diagnostic biomarkers.

papers.abstract_en: Epidemiological and occupational studies increasingly link respirable particulate matter (PM), including mineral dust, exposure with elevated lung cancer risk, yet the immunological mechanisms underlying these associations remain poorly defined. In this study, we investigated how compositionally distinct respirable PMs affect natural killer (NK) cells, a key component of immune surveillance. Using in vitro exposure and K562 target-cell challenge models, we show that respirable mineral-containing PMs induce dose- and composition-dependent NK-cell injury, including increased apoptosis/necrosis, altered cytokine profiles, changes in perforin/granzyme B-associated functions, and impaired effector responses under tumor-cell challenge conditions. Silica- and silicate-rich particles caused the most pronounced dysfunction, whereas iron-bearing and carbonaceous dusts produced distinct patterns of oxidative injury and cell loss. Mechanistic analyses identified mitochondrial depolarization, reduced mitochondrial mass, and lysosomal deacidification as convergent organelle stress pathways associated with altered NK-cell function. Ascorbic acid-associated improvements in organelle function and IFN-γ production further support a contribution of ROS-associated organelle dysfunction to impaired NK-cell responses. Collectively, these findings provide the first integrated adverse outcome pathways linking respirable PM exposure to NK-cell dysfunction, highlighting oxidative stress-driven lysosomal and mitochondrial injury as central pathways that may compromise NK-cell-mediated immune surveillance under tumor-cell challenge conditions.

papers.abstract_en: Lorlatinib, a third-generation anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) tyrosine kinase inhibitor, is widely used to treat ALK-positive nonsmall cell lung cancer. However, lorlatinib has occasionally been associated with severe liver injury. Immune-mediated adverse events are frequently provoked by certain pharmacological agents or their reactive metabolites. However, the specific contribution of immune pathways to hepatotoxicity caused by lorlatinib is yet to be fully elucidated. In the present study, the potential for direct inflammasome stimulation by lorlatinib was examined in differentiated THP-1 cells. This was accompanied by an evaluation of inflammasome-activating factors present in the culture supernatants of FLC-4 cells treated with lorlatinib. Our results showed that lorlatinib did not directly activate inflammasomes in differentiated THP-1 cells; however, the supernatants from FLC-4 cells activated inflammasomes in differentiated THP-1 cells following treatment with lorlatinib. Detection of pyrido-pyrazole-containing metabolites in FLC-4 cells suggests that these reactive metabolites activate inflammasomes. Exposure of FLC-4 cells to lorlatinib resulted in elevated extracellular concentrations of heat shock protein 90 (HSP90), a damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP). These findings suggest that the reactive metabolites of lorlatinib promote hepatocellular release of damage-associated molecular patterns, which in turn activate inflammasomes. Thus, inflammasome activation may be an important step in the activation of the immune system by lorlatinib and may cause immune-related adverse events in some patients.

papers.authors: Zhang L, Wu Y, Su P, Wang M, Shi P
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Otolaryngology-Head and Neck Surgery, The Fourth Hospital of Hebei Medical University and Hebei Tumor Hosp…
papers.results: 两例估计出血量均<150 mL；最终病理均为结节性甲状腺肿。Case 1术中发生局灶性喉返神经离断并即时行端端吻合，术后3个月喉镜示右侧声带活动受限，但无明显声嘶、主观发声不满、呛咳或临床误吸。Case 2术后3个月喉镜无显著异常，无发声/吞咽不适。两例短期随访均无呼吸窘迫、临床显著钙/PTH异常、症状性低钙血症或临床复发。
papers.authors_conclusion: 两例提示隆突水平巨大胸骨后甲状腺肿需个体化选择手术入路；当病灶与颈段甲状腺及纵隔部分连续、且纵隔部分、下极血管、喉返神经与甲状旁腺可在直视下安全控制时，选择性病例采用颈前入路是合理的；当颈部暴露不足时，尤其对纵隔部分深在且颈段体积小的老年患者，T形延长颈前切口是有效辅助；重视喉返神经处理、甲状旁腺血供保护及术中灵活调整暴露，是实现完整切除与低并发症的关键。
papers.ai_note: 仅2例、无对照，属最低级别证据，无法支撑'低并发症'的量化结论；结论中'低并发症'与Case 1喉返神经离断的事实存在口径张力。'选择性T形延长'的指征系术后归纳，存在事后叙述与选择性报告偏倚；两例为非同质对照（颈段体积、隆突下延伸深度不同），术式差异与结局差异不能互为因果。随访仅3个月，'无临床复发'对良性结节性甲状腺肿意义有限且证据力弱；嗓音/吞咽结局仅用描述性喉镜与主观询问，无客观量表或声学检查；摘要未报告手术时间、住院日、引流与血肿等围术期指标，也缺乏失血量具体测定方式。

pico.p: 2例女性，年龄74岁与81岁，2025年因巨大胸骨后甲状腺肿（一例累及隆突，一例延伸至隆突下约1 cm）接受手术
pico.ic: 颈前入路手术切除：Case 1为单纯颈前切口；Case 2在颈前切口基础上加做T形延长切口以改善暴露；无对照组

papers.reason: 为累及隆突水平的巨大胸骨后甲状腺肿提供入路决策的病例层面参照：单纯颈前切口与T形延长切口的适用条件（是否与颈段腺体连续、颈段体积、纵隔延伸深度），可用于评估此类纵隔巨大甲状腺肿是否需胸外科支援或胸骨切开，并作为后续队列设计的对照基线；证据级别低，仅作假设生成。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Giant retrosternal goiter may extend to the carina or below while remaining biologically benign. The main operative challenge is not size alone but whether the mediastinal component can be safely mobilized under direct control of the airway, inferior vessels, recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN), and parathyroid blood supply. We report two elderly patients with carina-level giant retrosternal goiters to illustrate individualized surgical route selection between a cervical incision alone and a cervical incision with selective T-shaped extended. CASE PRESENTATION: Two women aged 74 and 81 years underwent surgery for giant retrosternal goiter in 2025. Both underwent contrast-enhanced CT of the neck and chest, thyroid function testing, anesthetic assessment, multidisciplinary operative planning with thoracic surgical support, and preoperative blood typing and cross-matching with blood products available according to institutional protocol. In Case 1, the goiter had a substantial cervical component and extended to the carina. Complete resection was achieved through a cervical incision, but focal RLN transection occurred during difficult inferior-pole/thoracic-inlet dissection and was repaired immediately by end-to-end anastomosis. In Case 2, most of the goiter was retrosternal with minimal cervical bulk and extended approximately 1 cm below the carina. T-shaped extended cervical incision was added to improve exposure, allowing controlled complete resection with RLN preservation. Estimated blood loss was less than 150 mL in both patients. Final pathology confirmed nodular goiter. At 3 months, Case 1 had impaired right vocal-fold movement on laryngoscopy but no obvious hoarseness, subjective voice dissatisfaction, choking, or clinical aspiration. Case 2 had no significant laryngoscopic abnormality or voice/swallowing complaint. Both patients had no respiratory compromise, clinically significant calcium/PTH abnormality, symptomatic hypocalcemia, or clinical recurrence during short-term follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: These two cases illustrate the need for individualized surgical route selection in carina-level giant retrosternal goiter. A cervical approach may be reasonable in selected patients when the lesion remains continuous with the cervical thyroid and the mediastinal component, inferior vessels, RLN, and parathyroid glands can be controlled safely under direct visualization. A T-shaped extended cervical incision is an effective adjunct when cervical exposure is inadequate, especially in elderly patients with a deep mediastinal component and minimal cervical bulk. Careful management of the recurrent laryngeal nerve, protection of the parathyroid blood supply, and intraoperative willingness to customize the exposure are essential for achieving complete resection with low morbidity.

papers.title_en: Cancer theranostics.

papers.affiliation_highlight: Institute for Experimental Molecular Imaging (ExMI), RWTH Aachen University Hospital, Aachen, Germany.
papers.authors_conclusion: Building on solid progress in target identification, probe design and hardware development, as well as on promising recent results achieved in clinical trials, we foresee a bright and broad future for multiscale theranostics, for the treatment of oncological pathologies and beyond.
papers.ai_note: 叙述性综述，无系统检索、纳入排除标准、偏倚评估或定量合并；结论为未来展望，未提供可验证的主要临床终点数据；将影像引导手术、纳米/微尺度诊疗纳入诊疗一体化属概念扩展，需警惕术语边界泛化。
papers.reason: 提供诊疗一体化从分子影像到放射性核素治疗及影像引导手术的概念框架，可作为胸部肿瘤放射性配体治疗与影像引导手术相关研究的背景参考，但不直接改变胸外科患者选择或随访决策。
papers.abstract_en: Theranostics refers to the inseparable combination of disease diagnosis and therapy, with the former critically guiding the selection, application and outcome of the latter. In oncology, theranostics traditionally encompass radiolabelled peptides for in vivo molecular imaging of receptor expression by cancer cells, followed by radionuclide treatment using the same peptides labelled with β-emitting radioisotopes. Here we provide an overview of the basic principles and current clinical practice of theranostic probes and protocols, and we expand the terminology to include locally and systemically applied nanotheranostics and microtheranostics, as well as imaging-guided surgical interventions. Building on solid progress in target identification, probe design and hardware development, as well as on promising recent results achieved in clinical trials, we foresee a bright and broad future for multiscale theranostics, for the treatment of oncological pathologies and beyond.

papers.authors: Hasegawa M, Koizumi Y, Das NK, Zhang L, Lyssiotis CA, Shah YM, Fukuda S, Núñez G et al.
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Pathology, University of Michigan Medical School, Ann Arbor, MI 48109, USA; Rogel Cancer Center, Universit…
papers.authors_conclusion: 结果揭示了 BSH 在 VRE 定植中此前未知的调控作用，并为 VRE 感染风险人群提示了治疗途径。
papers.ai_note: 该文属肠道微生物组/感染病学机制研究，与胸外科、胸部肿瘤学无实质交集，六类目为强制归类下的勉强匹配（非真实主题）；摘要未给出任何定量结果（抑菌幅度、定植减少量、样本量、统计值均缺），无法评估效应量与可重复性；作者结论由“机制发现”直接跃至“治疗途径提示”，属摘要层面的外推，尚无体内治疗或人体数据支持；机制链条（BSH 亚类—信号肽—DCA—定植置换）依赖多环节共培养体系，摘要未说明对照与混杂控制。信息不足，不能据此对该文的严谨性作进一步判断。

pico.p: 摘要未报告样本量与例数；研究对象为肠道内万古霉素耐药肠球菌（VRE）与拟杆菌目（Bacteroidales）菌种，属微生物学机制研究，非患者人群
pico.ic: 携带保留未切割 N 端信号肽 BSH 亚类的拟杆菌属（Bacteroides）菌种 vs 缺失该亚类者；DCA 生成依赖 Lachnospiraceae bai+ 菌的存在；并比较 N 端信号肽缺失对胞外酶释放与 VRE 抑制的影响

papers.reason: 该文回答的是 VRE 肠道定植抵抗的细菌学机制，不涉及胸部肿瘤患者选择、手术决策、结节风险判断或围术期管理，对胸科肿瘤临床判断与科研设计无直接参考价值；仅可作为“菌群—代谢物介导定植抵抗”这一通用方法学思路的选题外背景文献记录。
papers.abstract_en: Vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) residing in the gut are major causes of hospital-acquired infections worldwide. Bacteria belonging to the Bacteroidales order have been linked to protection against VRE, but the mechanism remains unclear. Here, we identify an important role for Bacteroidales species in mediating resistance to VRE through a distinct subtype of bile salt hydrolases (BSHs) that retain an uncleaved N-terminal signal peptide. This subclass of BSHs harbored by Bacteroides species promotes VRE inhibition through deoxycholic acid (DCA) production in the presence of Lachnospiraceae bai+ bacteria. Mechanistically, the N-terminal signal peptide is required for extracellular enzyme release, DCA production, and VRE growth inhibition. In the presence of VRE, Bacteroidales species producing this subclass of BSH eliminate and displace VRE from its ecological niche through DCA production. These results reveal a previously unknown regulatory role for BSHs in VRE colonization and suggest therapeutic approaches for individuals at risk of VRE infection.

papers.abstract_en: Postnatal immune maturation is commonly viewed as a developmental milestone associated with weaning. However, how postnatal microbiota exposure shapes immune cell heterogeneity across tissues, and whether this maturation is self-sustaining or requires continuous microbial input, remain unclear. Here, we conducted spatiotemporal single-cell transcriptomic profiling of 120,649 immune cells isolated from 10 tissues in both germ-free (GF) and specific pathogen-free (SPF) mice from weaning to adulthood. We demonstrate that microbial colonization drives the expansion and functional maturation of distinct monocyte, macrophage, and neutrophil populations, marked by enhanced antigen-processing capabilities across tissues. Simultaneously, commensal-derived signals reprogram lymphocyte metabolic and translational states, promoting oxidative phosphorylation and relieving PDCD4-mediated translational repression to sustain effector readiness. Notably, microbiota reconstitution through both co-housing and fecal microbiota transplantation demonstrated that immune competence is not a fixed developmental endpoint but instead requires continuous microbiota-derived input. Without sustained microbial signals, immune cells adopted a persistent hyporesponsive state rather than remaining developmentally immature. Together, these findings redefine immune maturation as a microbiota-dependent maintenance process, revealing potential strategies to restore immune competence through microbiota-targeted interventions.

papers.authors: Nara A, Nebbia M, Navarrete Galvez KM, Rodriguez Franco S, Bilal M, Bhalla S, Mungo B, Del Chiaro M et al.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Main duct intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (MD-IPMN) carries a substantial risk of malignant transformation and often requires surgical resection.1,2 Preservation of the remnant pancreas remains an important goal, particularly in elderly patients.3,4 Therefore, determining the optimal extent of resection requires a careful balance between oncological safety and preservation of pancreatic function.5,6 The utility of intraoperative pancreatoscopy during robotic pancreatoduodenectomy (RPD) for this purpose has not been well established.7 METHODS: We present two elderly patients with MD-IPMN who underwent RPD combined with intraoperative pancreatoscopy. After pancreatic transection, a Spyglass was introduced through a robotic port #1 and advanced into the remnant pancreatic duct under robotic guidance. The main pancreatic duct and branch ducts were systematically inspected for findings suspicious for high-grade dysplasia or skip lesions.8 Frozen-section analysis of the pancreatic margin was performed in both cases. RESULTS: The patients were in their 70s with pancreatic head IPMN and pancreatic duct dilation. Intraoperative pancreatoscopy demonstrated no suspicious lesions within the remnant pancreas. Frozen-section analysis confirmed the absence of carcinoma or high-grade dysplasia at the pancreatic margin. Based on these findings, no additional pancreatic resection was required, and the remnant pancreas was preserved in both patients. Final pathology revealed mixed-type IPMN with high-grade dysplasia and no invasive carcinoma in both cases. CONCLUSIONS: Intraoperative pancreatoscopy can be safely integrated into RPD and serves as an adjunct to preoperative imaging, potentially facilitating targeted biopsy. This approach may support preservation of the remnant pancreas in elderly patients with MD-IPMN.

papers.abstract_en: Radon (222Rn) is a radioactive noble gas released from terrestrial materials via the alpha recoil of its parent radium-226 (226Ra), and is the second leading cause of lung cancer worldwide. The fraction of radon atoms that escape from the solid grain matrix into connected pore spaces - the emanation coefficient (η) - governs the radon source term and is essential for indoor radiological hazard assessment. This study estimates η for one coal fly ash and one agricultural soil using γ-spectrometry for 226Ra quantification and an expanded 16-can sealed-can method with LR-115 type II solid-state nuclear track detectors (SSNTDs). The approximately 2.3-fold difference in η (fly ash: 0.0056 ± 0.0015; soil: 0.0127 ± 0.0035, expanded uncertainty k = 2), despite the higher 226Ra activity of fly ash (102.4 vs. 77.6 Bq kg-1), is consistent with the hypothesis that radium is less accessible for recoil release in the glassy aluminosilicate matrix of fly ash; no microstructural measurements were made to test this. The emanation data are combined with the semi-empirical Sahoo et al. wall exhalation model, using estimated diffusion lengths and assumed block and wall geometries, to assess the 3-D to 1-D diffusion geometry transition from sample to constructed wall. The resulting model-derived wall-to-sample flux enhancement factors are 2.35 (fly ash) and 4.1 (soil). Under the assumptions of this first-order model, the estimated dose for the investigated fly ash sample remains below the EU reference level of 1 mSv y-1; this has not been validated by direct wall-flux measurements and should not be generalized to fly ash as a material class. The results indicate that geometry correction may be important when extrapolating laboratory-scale exhalation measurements to building-scale exposure.

papers.abstract_en: Pluripotent stem cell-derived multicellular systems provide a promising platform for studying development and disease. However, they do not faithfully mirror their in vivo counterparts due to the presence of aberrant cells. Similarly, aberrant cell types emerge during tissue development in multicellular organisms but are effectively removed via proofreading mechanisms that often exploit apoptosis. Yet, the design and engineering of such processes are notably absent from current approaches for building stem cell-derived multicellular systems. We address this gap by introducing a "subtractive multicellular engineering" approach, using genetic circuits that integrate logic-gated computing and synthetic apoptosis. Through this approach, we enhance tissue maturity in human pluripotent stem cell-derived liver organoids. Additionally, we demonstrate the versatility of this approach in a human post-implantation embryo model, where it improves pro-amniotic cavity development, a key morphogenetic feature. Our results establish a framework for building tissues in vitro via controlled elimination of aberrant cells during morphogenesis.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: SAGES' space surgery task force was created in 2023 in response to the potential increased need for surgical intervention in space as humanity seeks to establish larger and more permanent populations in space environments. This task force sought to assess the needs, limitations, and anticipated challenges of surgical care in space environments and to offer leadership opportunities by surveying the SAGES membership. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional survey of the SAGES membership soliciting respondent's experience in aerospace medicine and related fields, as well as members' interests within space surgery and their opinions about the future surgical needs of space explorers. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize demographics, interests, and preferences, and narrative review and thematic analysis were used to analyze open-ended responses. RESULTS: Survey response rate was 6.1%. Most respondents were attending minimally invasive or general surgeons. Experience was reported in telehealth, artificial intelligence, austere environment surgery, and military medicine. Greatest interest was expressed in the application of robotic technologies in space. Respondents wished to participate in technical skills workshops and to view presentations by astronauts on space medicine as part of the future activities of the task force at SAGES annual meetings. Themes identified as challenges to space surgery included microgravity, resource limitations, remote surgery, training, and specific medical concerns. Future areas of focus included technology and innovation, protocol/system design, adjustment to medical standards, and training programs. CONCLUSION: This survey identified a strong interest among the SAGES membership in leading the conversation surrounding space surgery as humanity expands beyond low earth orbit. Numerous opportunities, challenges, and new directions were identified by respondents that will guide the future activities of the task force.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Women diagnosed with gynecological cancer face significant psychosocial challenges that impact their self-efficacy, self-esteem, and coping abilities. Understanding these factors is essential for developing effective psychosocial interventions. OBJECTIVE: To examine the relationships between self-efficacy, self-esteem, cancer coping strategies, and psychosocial adjustment in women with gynecological cancer in Turkey. METHODS: This correlational cross-sectional study involved 105 women with gynecological cancer from 2 university hospitals in Turkey. Data were collected using the General Self-efficacy Scale, Rosenberg's Self-esteem Scale, Cancer Coping Questionnaire, and Psychosocial Adjustment to Illness Scale. Statistical analyses included independent t tests, 1-way analysis of variance, Pearson correlation, and hierarchical regression. RESULTS: The mean psychosocial adjustment score was 70.22 ± 4.60. Significant negative correlations were found between psychosocial adjustment and self-efficacy (r = -0.572, P = .001), self-esteem (r = -0.277, P = .004), and cancer coping (r = -0.581, P = .001). Hierarchical regression revealed that self-efficacy (β = -0.462, P = .001), cancer coping (β = -0.280, P = .001), and treatment type (β = -0.332, P = .001) collectively explained 55% of the variance in psychosocial adjustment. CONCLUSIONS: Self-efficacy and coping strategies significantly influence psychosocial adjustment in women with gynecological cancer, whereas self-esteem showed no significant effect. These findings highlight the need for targeted interventions to strengthen self-efficacy and coping mechanisms in women with gynecological cancer. IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Healthcare professionals should implement structured interventions to enhance self-efficacy and coping strategies, as these factors are key to improving psychosocial adjustment and overall well-being in women undergoing gynecological cancer treatment.

papers.abstract_en: Late-onset depression (LOD) is a common subtype of depression in the elderly, characterized by high disability and recurrence rates, along with poorly understood biological correlates, posing a serious threat to the health of the aging population; moreover, the molecular correlates and diagnostic targets for LOD remain largely unknown. Aging and stress are recognized as two core risk factors for LOD; however, whether they interact and how such interaction is associated with the depressive phenotype remain unclear, so we established a rat model of LOD to analyze the interactive effects of aging and stress on depressive-like behaviors, and combined this with cerebrospinal fluid proteomics to explore potential protein correlates and provide experimental evidence for identifying candidate therapeutic targets. In terms of results, aging and stress exhibited a synergistic association with depressive-like behaviors in LOD rats, and enrichment was observed in extracellular matrix and sphingolipid metabolic pathways; furthermore, several proteins─including ceramide, MMP2, TIMP2, SPARC, FBN1, and collagen─were identified as candidate correlates worthy of further investigation. In conclusion, stress and aging exert interactive effects on behavioral phenotypes in LOD rats, with associated alterations in extracellular matrix and sphingolipid pathways, and key molecules including Cer, MMP2, Timp2, and Sparc warrant further investigation.

papers.abstract_en: The coral microbiome is believed to play a crucial role in sustaining corals and enabling adaptation to perturbations. A ubiquitous group of coral-associated bacteria, known as Endozoicomonas, are hypothesized to provide essential metabolites to corals, although detailed dynamics of the interactions between host and microbe are poorly understood. Here multi-omics and laboratory validation experiments reveal that Endozoicomonas encodes genes for the metabolism of coral-derived testosterone and converts ubiquitous cholesterol into testosterone and progesterone, both important steroids that accumulate within the coral holobiont during thermal stress. Field sampling along a natural temperature gradient showed general suppression of coral steroid hormones under thermal stress and during white syndrome manifestation. Provision of testosterone or progesterone to corals during laboratory thermal stress induced transcriptional reprogramming of the coral innate immune response, suggesting microbial involvement in host immune modulation. These findings highlight a previously unrecognized potential mechanism of microbial contribution to coral resilience.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Hospital at Home (HaH) models aim to deliver hospital-level care to patients in a home setting. In the context of allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), HaH is intended to improve patients' quality of life and reduce symptom burden. However, limited research exists on patients' perceptions of this innovative care model. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore how patients experienced HaH following HSCT. METHODS: A qualitative exploratory research design was employed, utilizing semistructured individual interviews. Sixteen patients who received HaH care following HSCT were interviewed. Reflexive thematic analysis was used to identify themes representing patterns of meaning across the dataset. RESULTS: The following 3 themes were identified: (1) actively working through the illness experience: participants needed to engage in active coping mechanisms, emphasizing the crucial role of their informal caregivers, (2) recognition of normality in the illness situation: experiencing autonomy and living in a homelike environment enhanced their sense of normality, and (3) fundamental aspects of daily life that promote recovery: psychological and emotional benefits of the private setting, including improved rest, calmness, relaxation, increased physical activity, and the opportunities to engage in familiar daily activities, facilitated recovery in ways that differed from the traditional hospital setting. CONCLUSION: This study suggests that HaH positively influences recovery and well-being among HSCT patients and has the potential to improve patient outcomes. IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: HaH offers a viable alternative to traditional hospitalization, promoting a more personalized approach to care.

papers.abstract_en: We report a 19-month-old girl with molecularly confirmed Perrault syndrome type 4 (PRLTS4), due to a homozygous LARS2 variant (c.457A>C, p.Asn153His), who developed dilated cardiomyopathy (ejection fraction 21%) at 2 months of age despite a normal neonatal echocardiogram, alongside bilateral profound sensorineural hearing loss and global developmental delay. No second causative cardiac variant was identified. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of dilated cardiomyopathy in molecularly confirmed LARS2-related PRLTS4, expanding the recognised phenotypic spectrum of this disorder and supporting cardiac surveillance in affected infants.

papers.abstract_en: Next-generation sequencing has radically transformed the diagnostic capability of rare neurodevelopmental disorders (RNDDs), yet translating these molecular insights into viable therapeutics remains a hurdle. While gene-directed modalities, specifically viral-mediated supplementation, antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), and CRISPR-based activation or precision editing, offer a means to rescue loss-of-function phenotypes, successful clinical implementation requires moving past the reductive framework of merely increasing the expression of the target gene towards approaches that account for spatial, developmental, and therapeutic windows. This review uses HNRNPU-related rare neurodevelopmental disorder (HNRNPU-RNDD), a condition marked with global developmental delay and refractory epilepsy, as an exemplar to discuss these translational hurdles. We discuss the homeostatic boundaries of this scaffold attachment factor, where unregulated overexpression risks localised cytotoxicity, and altered chromatin dynamics compromise editing safety. Furthermore, we assess how cell-type sensitivity and narrow developmental windows may dictate clinical efficacy. By using HNRNPU-RNDD to critically analyse the challenges of using each therapeutic platform, we hope to inform the creation of gene-directed therapies that aim to treat disorders resulting from structural pleiotropic dosage-sensitive proteins.
